   - **Top-level keys, exactly:** `population_rail`, `legacy_rule`, and the agreement counts — NULL on four of those five days and populated only on 09-02. **THE AGREEMENT COUNTS ARE A NESTED OBJECT, NOT THREE FLAT KEYS — corrected 2026-09-07 by D1, measured against the live parser and the live rows, because the sentence that stood here named the VIEW COLUMNS and a session following it literally would re-open the exact defect this bullet exists to close.** The operative view is `state.research_screen_calls` as redefined by `bigquery/122_decision_correction_append_only.sql` (which supersedes `bigquery/96_research_screener.sql`'s copy), and it reads `SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(fields,'$.agreement.both') AS INT64) AS agreement_both` — and likewise `$.agreement.ai_only`, `$.agreement.rule_only`. So the columns are named `agreement_*` and the KEYS are not: **write `"agreement": {"both": n, "ai_only": n, "rule_only": n}`**, exactly as `bigquery/96`'s own header schema block has specified since it was authored. A flat top-level `agreement_both` is read by nothing and lands the column NULL. **Measured 2026-09-07 across every D1 screen row since 2026-08-30:** the two rows whose agreement columns are POPULATED — 09-02 (`both` 8 / `ai_only` 3 / `rule_only` 1 on single-name) and 09-06 (`both` 6 / `ai_only` 4 / `rule_only` 6 on single-name; `0`/`5`/`0` on sector) — both carry the nested object and **neither carries a flat `agreement_both` key at all** (`JSON_VALUE(fields,'$.agreement_both')` is NULL on both), which is what establishes the nested form is the one that works rather than merely the one that was used. The 2026-09-06 run wrote it correctly *despite* this bullet, so the trap has not yet cost a row; it is closed here before it does. **Everything else in this bullet is unchanged and still binding** — in particular the per-item key list below, whose keys ARE flat and ARE named exactly as the parser reads them.
   - **Why it is not cosmetic:** W5's screens-rejecting-winners check is **name-keyed and cannot key on NULL**, and W5 recorded that check as VACUOUS on 2026-08-30. W2 did not test the causal link and neither does this note — what would confirm it is re-running that check against a screen whose `name` column is populated — but a check that cannot see its own input is not a check.

   **`surfaced_count` IS `ARRAY_LENGTH(passed)`, NOT THE LAYER-1 RAIL TALLY — pinned 2026-08-30 by D1, closing W2's `screen_surfaced_count_array_mismatch` finding (`ops.alerts` `da469b47`).** That finding measured D1's 2026-08-24 row `4d30f5d9` carrying `surfaced_count = 25` against a `passed[]` of 17, and correctly could not tell from the row alone whether 8 names had been LOST during the write or the scalar had been taken from a pre-filter tally. **It was the tally, and nothing was lost** — the 2026-08-24 `Daily.md` states it in its own words ("Of the 79, 29 moved ≥2%; **25 of those cleared the $2B cap rail**") and enumerates the 17 Layer-2 passes plus 5 `rejected_notable`. So this is a CONTRACT ambiguity, not data loss, and the ambiguity is the defect: `bigquery/96_research_screener.sql` parses the scalar and the per-item arrays into the SAME view, and W5's RESEARCH-SCREEN SCORECARD reads the scalar as D1's surfacing rate — so a rail tally there overstates surfacing by exactly the names Layer-2 declined, and `analytics.research_screen_disagreements` joins per-item and finds no rows for them. **Therefore: `surfaced_count` counts what this screen SURFACED — the Layer-2 passes written up, i.e. the length of `passed[]` — and the two must agree in every row.** Put the Layer-1 population arithmetic in `fields.rail_tally` (names clearing the mechanical ≥2% + ≥$2B + identified-event rail) and `fields.universe_measured` (how many distinct names this run actually measured), where it is a separate, honestly-named number rather than a second meaning for the same key. **ALSO WRITE `fields.selection_rule` — one line stating HOW the measured names were chosen out of the eligible universe (added 2026-09-20 by D1, adopting W2's `b_intake_population_coverage_unquantified` proposal, `ops.alerts` `08582955`; purely additive, changes no rail and no gate).** `universe_measured` on its own is a numerator with no stated denominator, and because W2's Strategy-B intake is exclusively this durable screen record, D1's bounded scan **IS** the definition of the B candidate population. W2 measured the consequence inside a 21-name sample it already held for other reasons: **24 close-to-close moves ≥5% across the five sessions D1 screened that week appear in NEITHER `passed` NOR `rejected_notable`** — more absent than present (21). A scan bounded by metered-call cost is legitimate and is not being widened here; an UNDESCRIBED one cannot be reported as a coverage ratio by any downstream scorecard, which is the actual defect. The REPORTING RULE above is unchanged and still governs the degraded case: on a degraded run `surfaced_count` is what you actually confirmed via IBKR, which is the same rule read through this definition, not a competing one.

   **CROSS-ROW CLOSE-CHAIN CHECK — RUN IT BEFORE THE INITIAL APPEND; FREE, NO PRICE PULL (added 2026-09-27, closing `d1_below_spec_floor_contradicts_own_anchor_prose`, `ops.alerts` warning `62775339-002b-4e12-8119-45409a6c4f01`).** Full contract in Operating_Protocols.md §19 CROSS-ROW CLOSE CHAIN TEST; the write-time obligation is this. For every item with a real `qualifying_event_date`, read the durable record for any OTHER item carrying the SAME name (`COALESCE($.name, $.ticker)` — both spellings exist historically) and the SAME `qualifying_event_date`, and compare closes numerically: your `prior_close` equal to that item's `event_close` — or your `event_close` equal to its `prior_close` — is a **CHAIN HIT**, and it proves your pair measures the session immediately after the one that item measured. One query covers the whole screen, so this costs one read per run. Resolve every hit against the release's own timing, never against the other item: an after-close anchor legitimately chains forward and is simply recorded in `reason`; a hit on an **intraday or pre-open** anchor means the pair was taken a session late, and the item may not be written until the pair is re-taken on the session the anchor implies and `metric_pct` / `below_spec_floor` are recomputed from it. A hit never aborts the screen. **This is also the mechanism by which one anchor gets screened twice, and nothing in this screen prevents it:** IONQ was recorded for anchor 2026-09-23 on BOTH 09-23 (`91b1a00c`, 40.74 → 42.54, `below_spec_floor=true`) and 09-24 (`6e179f3c`, 42.54 → 44.98, `false`), with the verdict flipped between them and the second item's own `reason` agreeing with the first. If a chain hit lands on an item for a name already dispositioned on this anchor, carry the earlier disposition forward or supersede it explicitly — never write a second, silently disagreeing one. **Coverage is 32% (17 of 53 pair-carrying items have any counterpart, measured 2026-09-27), so a clean pass is not a clearance**, and this check does NOT decide which session `below_spec_floor` is computed on — that is the separate, already-open notice `06c3b0db` against the ANCHOR CONVENTION limb above, adjudication W5.

   **Late-data discipline:** immediately before this initial append, re-read the relevant final state (including any D2a reconciliation that overlapped this D1) and compose the record from that read. If a fact changes after append, `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` for a complete replacement that preserves `entry_type='research-screen'`, carries tag `correction`, and passes `in_superseded_by=<old entry_id>`; never UPDATE, DELETE, or MERGE `events.decision_log`.

   **Strategy-B handoff identity.** For every D1-originated Strategy-B candidate or `research-screen` item, persist the qualifying public-event date as `qualifying_event_date` (not merely a ticker or the D1 run date).

   **ANCHOR CONVENTION — `qualifying_event_date` IS THE DATE THE EVENT BECAME PUBLIC, NEVER THE SESSION THE MOVE WAS MEASURED IN (added 2026-09-21 by D1, closing its own `d1_qualifying_event_date_anchor_unspecified`, `ops.alerts` info `03b8f773`, 2026-09-16).** The rule already existed — `Watchlist.md`'s **ANCHOR PIN** (D2 2026-08-19) states "the event date governs; the flag-date wording above is legacy" — but it was written **only inside D2's section and that file**, and **D1, which is the routine that actually SETS the field, carried no equivalent limb.** The consequence is measured, not hypothetical: on **four consecutive cycles** D1's anchor had to be corrected downstream at D2 — HPE/DELL right on 2026-09-13, JBHT wrong on 2026-09-16, SMR wrong on 2026-09-17, and **all five of the 2026-09-20 cohort wrong** (XENE, NUE, MSTR, COIN re-anchored 09-18 → 09-17; BE re-anchored 09-18 → 09-04, on which its entry window had **already closed**).
   - **The rule, stated operationally.** The anchor is the date the qualifying information CROSSED THE WIRE. A release that lands **after the close** of session S anchors on **S**, and the reaction you measure on S+1 is the *reaction session*, not the anchor — that is the single case D1 has gotten wrong every time, because the reaction session is the one the screen's own close-to-close arithmetic lives in. A release public **intraday** on session S anchors on S, and the ≥5% test is then measured on S itself. A release **pre-open** on session S anchors on S. Record BOTH dates in the item — `qualifying_event_date` (the anchor) and the reaction session the `prior_close`/`event_close` pair was taken from — so a later reader can see the two are deliberately different rather than suspecting a typo.
   - **WHY THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: THE ANCHOR CAN DECIDE ELIGIBILITY, AND IT ALREADY DID.** Strategy B Entry criterion 1 measures the ≥5% move **on event day**. Move the anchor and you move which session is tested. Measured 2026-09-20 on **MSTR**: on D1's 09-18 anchor it clears the frozen ≥5% floor by 3.3× (**+16.3856%**); on the convention-correct 09-17 anchor — the session the governing SEC release was actually public — it moved **+4.8106% and FAILS the floor by 19bp**. Same name, same tape, opposite verdict, decided entirely by a convention D1's own prompt did not carry. **COIN is the control that makes this a rule rather than an anecdote:** under the identical correction it moved **+5.7504%** on 09-17 and clears in its own right, so the correction is not uniformly disqualifying — it is simply load-bearing.
   - **It also silently shortens windows.** The 10-trading-day entry window runs from the anchor, so anchoring on the reaction session grants a candidate a day it does not have. **BE is the worked case:** anchored on 09-18 it looked like a live candidate with a window to ~10-02; anchored correctly on its 2026-09-04 S&P-500-addition announcement, its window had **already closed before D1 ever surfaced it**. No capital was at risk — B has been `DO-NOT-ACTIVATE` and capital-disabled throughout — which is exactly why this is the right time to fix it rather than after a router flip.
   - **Do not resolve the anchor from the price series.** The bar that moved tells you the reaction session and nothing about when the information became public; the anchor comes from the release's own timestamp on the issuer/authority source, which the EVENT-IDENTITY GATE above already requires you to record. If the release timestamp genuinely cannot be established, say so and record the anchor as UNRESOLVED rather than defaulting to the reaction session — a defaulted anchor is the failure mode this limb exists to close.

   A B thesis candidate's deterministic identity is `analysis_type='thesis-construction'` + `strategy='B'` + `ticker` + `qualifying_event_date`, with queue `item_key = thesis-<TICKER>-B-<YYYYMMDD>` (**KEY-FORMAT PIN, corrected 2026-08-23 by W4 — see §C of W4 for the full record; the previously-documented `thesis-B-<ticker>-<qualifying_event_date>` shape has NEVER been written by any routine and matching on it as a literal string returns a false-negative dedupe every time**). Before D1/D2 creates that handoff, check both open and terminal `events.queue_events` history and relevant `events.decision_log` decisions for that exact four-part identity — **match on the FIELDS `(item_type, strategy, ticker, due_date/qualifying_event_date)`, never on the key string**; do not duplicate it, but do not suppress a later distinct event in the same ticker. Carry `qualifying_event_date` and the originating `research-screen` decision id in `d1_actions` and every downstream queue payload. Ticker-only deduplication is prohibited.

4. Sector-level moves — **AI-SIGNIFICANCE SCREEN (Operating_Protocols.md §19, same call).** Layer-1 rail: any GICS sector ≥1% at sector-ETF level, or notable intraday dispersion. Layer-2: judge which sector moves are significant in regime context per §19 (a 1.3% defensives bid on a flat tape can outrank a 2.5% beta-day sweep). Per sector written up: magnitude, apparent driver, source, significance conviction + reason, `legacy_rule_pass` (sector ≥2%, the old bar — record-only; `metric_pct` = the raw sector-ETF close-to-close move — **measured from regular-session daily bars (`get_price_history`, `outside_rth=false`), never a snapshot; Operating_Protocols.md §19 PRICE BASIS** — **and read from the `close` array at both ends, logging `prior_close`/`event_close` with it (§19 FIELD / RECORD THE TWO PRICES, added 2026-09-20)** — and a dispersion-only surfacing logs `legacy_rule_pass=false` by convention, never NULL — §19). Log ONE `entry_type='research-screen'` row for this screen (screen='sector-move') per §19 — including quiet days. **`surfaced_count` here means the same thing it means in the single-name screen above — `ARRAY_LENGTH(passed)`, never the Layer-1 rail tally** (see that screen's 2026-08-30 pin; the sector rows drifted the same way, e.g. the 2026-08-24 `eac69f4a` row carries `surfaced_count = 11` against a `passed[]` of 4, 11 being the count of sector ETFs MEASURED rather than the count written up). Use `fields.rail_tally` / `fields.universe_measured` for the population arithmetic. Apply the same late-data discipline as the single-name screen: re-read final state before its initial append; after an append, emit an append-only complete replacement that preserves `entry_type='research-screen'`, carries tag `correction`, and passes `in_superseded_by=<old entry_id>`, never an events.decision_log UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE.

5. Notable commentary. Major sell-side reports issued, regulator or central-bank speeches with market-moving content, senior corporate commentary worth noting.

ANALYSIS — RISK TO EXISTING POSITIONS

MECHANICAL EXIT-TRIGGER SWEEP (run for EVERY open position regardless of whether any Development fired). Read the open book + its two MECHANICAL exit triggers (`convergence_target`, `time_exit_date`, with `contract_id`) from **`state.current_positions`** (BigQuery — authoritative per Operating_Protocols.md §15, D2-maintained), and pull live prices from the IBKR connector (`get_price_snapshot` per name). **Sweep the UNION of `state.current_positions` and live `get_account_positions` (self-improvement audit ITEM 14, 2026-07-11 — closes the exact gap that left the BURL convergence exit unactioned for days: a position real in IBKR but not yet reconciled into BigQuery was previously EXEMPT from this sweep entirely, since it enumerated from `state.current_positions` alone and used the connector only for a "flag divergence" side-note).** For a position present in the connector but NOT yet in `state.current_positions`: run its convergence-target / time-exit checks anyway using connector-supplied fields (ticker, average cost, live mark) — its entry record's `convergence_target`/`time_exit_date` are unavailable pre-reconciliation, so treat it as a **RECONCILIATION-LAG POSITION** requiring a same-day D2a Step-0 catch-up rather than skipping its exit check silently. Write a durable `ops.alerts` row — not prose — for every such position: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D1','position_reconciliation_lag', <ticker + strategy-if-known + first-seen-in-connector date>, <JSON: including ticker, strategy>)` (switched from `sp_raise_alert` to the `_once` variant, root-cause fix 2026-07-20 — the message is pinned to the first-seen date so it stays stable for a persisting occurrence, and `_once` dedups on (category, message) against unresolved rows; without it, a position that fails its same-day D2a catch-up — e.g. IBKR down, guard-blocked — would accumulate one duplicate alert row per subsequent D1 run instead of the one open alert every other persisting-condition category in this file gets). This is a genuine gap distinct from the existing `state.position_reconciliation` (B4) drift check, which compares two BigQuery views populated by the SAME write step and is structurally blind to a not-yet-reconciled connector position. For each position in the union, check the two MECHANICAL exit triggers:
- **Convergence target hit** (Strategy B / E price targets): live price at or through the convergence target → flag EXIT TRIGGERED (mechanical — the target IS the exit rule per Strategy.md; no judgment needed).
- **Time-based exit due**: today (America/Denver) ≥ the position's time-based-exit date → flag EXIT TRIGGERED.
This catches a target-hit the next morning without waiting for a per-position scheduled review — the lag that left the BURL convergence exit owed for days under the screenshot workflow. It retires the per-position pulse-check / time-exit / convergence-check calendar events entirely (this daily sweep replaces them). D2 converts every EXIT TRIGGERED flag into a crafted exit order.

PER-STRATEGY KILL-TRIGGER SWEEP (connector-driven; run for EVERY active strategy, alongside the per-position sweep above). Read each strategy's kill/gate state from **`perf.kill_flags`** (BigQuery engine — `drawdown_kill`, `runaway_review`, `m2m_underperf_review`, `gate_reached`, computed from the latest `perf.strategy_daily`). D1 runs before D2, so the engine row is yesterday's close — **UNCONDITIONALLY refresh `current_drawdown` against today's live marks (`get_price_snapshot`) for every open position, every run** (self-improvement audit ITEM 16, 2026-07-11 — removed the "if a position moved sharply intraday" judgment predicate: AI_Trading_Foundation.md 3b.3 reserves the drawdown-kill decision from AI discretion specifically because judgment under loss pressure is unreliable, so the ONE thing that decides whether this refresh even runs must not itself be a judgment call), then evaluate the flags below against the thresholds in Experiment_Parameters.md "Kill criteria (per-strategy)":
- **Drawdown kill (#1, mechanical / immediate):** if peak-to-trough deployed TWR has dropped ≥50% from the strategy's highest historical value since first trade → flag **STRATEGY TERMINATION — DRAWDOWN**. Rigid and context-independent — no judgment, no review.
- **Runaway-success (#3, pre-gate only):** if deployed TWR has **doubled** AND the strategy has not yet cleared its 30-trade gate → flag **RUNAWAY-SUCCESS REVIEW** (does NOT terminate directly — routes to an m2m-termination review to rule out reward-function exploitation / hidden tail risk).
- **Interim underperformance warning (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP interim-underperf-warning-no-consumer).** `perf.kill_flags.interim_underperf_warning` (`deployed_days >= 90 AND excess_vs_sgov <= -15%`, beta-adjusted; `bigquery/03_twr_engine.sql`) was built specifically because a long-horizon strategy (D's archetype) has no operative kill before the 756-day/36-month mark-to-market trigger and could otherwise silently underperform for ~3 years unguarded — but nothing ever read this column outside `state.daily_briefing`'s generic detail string. For each active strategy whose latest `perf.kill_flags.interim_underperf_warning = TRUE`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D1','interim_underperf_warning', '<strategy> — deployed >=90 days, beta-adjusted excess vs SGOV <= -15%, no mechanical kill triggers before the 756-day mark-to-market review', '<JSON: strategy, deployed_days, excess_vs_sgov>')` — a WARNING, not a termination trigger (this signal is explicitly early/advisory, not one of the rigid mechanical kill criteria); it does NOT enqueue a review or route to D2 like the two flags above — it exists to feed SL4's monthly QUALITATIVE-EVIDENCE INTAKE (its automated consumer, consumption-closure 2026-07-16) and any session second look, well before the 756-day trigger. `sp_raise_alert_once` naturally dedupes a persisting condition to one open alert, so this does not spam daily. HEAL-RESOLUTION: when the latest `perf.kill_flags.interim_underperf_warning` reads FALSE for a strategy that has an OPEN alert of this category, run `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='condition healed — beta-adjusted excess recovered' WHERE category='interim_underperf_warning' AND NOT resolved AND JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.strategy') = <strategy>` — the same sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve as D2 Step 0's `termination_close_staged` (ITEM 17 precedent). This category stays ABSENT from `ops.alert_policy` (it is not resolved by the generic `sp_auto_resolve_alerts`; D1 owns it with strategy-level evidence).
- **B open-book pairwise-correlation warning (finding M1, 2026-07-17 — the KL #12 metric-(d) control, `bigquery/83_correlation_controls.sql`).** `SELECT n_positions, avg_offdiagonal_corr, min_overlap_days FROM analytics.b_pairwise_correlation` (a single self-bootstrapping row — trailing ~63-trading-day daily-return CORR across every pair of open Strategy-B positions). If `avg_offdiagonal_corr > 0.5 AND n_positions >= 2 AND min_overlap_days >= 40` (a genuine, non-noise concentration — thin-history pairs are excluded from the average inside the view itself, and `min_overlap_days` is computed over the SAME >=40-day qualifying pairs (2026-07-18 audit fix: a global MIN let one fresh position suppress the whole-book alert), so the `>= 40` term is simply the "mature evidence exists" guard — NULL/no-qualifying-pairs safely fails it), `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D1','b_pairwise_corr_high', 'Strategy-B open book pairwise avg correlation exceeds 0.50 — KL #12 concentration control; see payload for the correlation, position count and minimum overlap', '<JSON: n_positions, avg_offdiagonal_corr, min_overlap_days>')`. A WARNING only — it does NOT terminate or block staging (correlation-bucket is informational per Rev 35, Watchlist.md), it surfaces the KL #12 diversification concern for the next B-entry sizing/eligibility decision. **THE MESSAGE IS A FIXED STRING, AND MUST STAY ONE — corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep); the sentence that stood here, "`sp_raise_alert_once` dedups the persisting condition", was FALSE as the call was written.** `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on `WHERE NOT resolved AND category = in_category AND message = in_message` (`bigquery/10_observability.sql`) — exact string equality on the message and nothing else — while the old template interpolated all three of `avg_offdiagonal_corr` (a rolling ~63-trading-day correlation, continuous, essentially certain to differ every session), `n_positions` and `min_overlap_days` (which increments by construction). So `_once` degenerated to a plain `sp_raise_alert` and a genuinely persisting B-concentration would have emailed a fresh warning EVERY DAY it held — the precise alarm fatigue `_once` was chosen to prevent, on a condition that by its nature persists for weeks. It has never manifested only because the check is inert (today B holds a single position (MDT), so `n_positions = 1 < 2`); this is a latent defect closed before first firing, not an observed one. Same defect class, same fix, as `probe_funding_stalled` (SL3 STEP 5, 2026-08-26), `queue_item_stale` (D3 QUEUE HYGIENE, 2026-08-31) and the three W5 sites. Inert unless B holds >=2 correlated positions with sufficient overlap (today B holds a single position (MDT), so `n_positions = 1 < 2` and the check is a no-op).
D2 converts a DRAWDOWN flag into an immediate strategy termination (close all positions + deterministic redistribution) and a RUNAWAY-SUCCESS flag into an enqueued review. (The mark-to-market #4 and foundation-change #2 triggers are detected on slower cadences — M4 monthly and Q3/A1 respectively — not here.)

For each open position, does any Development above ALSO trigger a (judgment-laden) thesis-invalidation exit criterion in the position's entry record (per Strategy.md exit rules for the relevant strategy)? For each position affected: position (ticker + strategy), triggering development, whether the invalidation criterion is met (YES with specific criterion / NO with reasoning).

**DIVIDEND NETTING ON A PRICE-LEVEL CRITERION — MANDATORY before you report a price test as met (added 2026-08-23; `ops.alerts` `070cc2f0`, B:MSCI:2026-07-27).** If the criterion names a PRICE LEVEL rather than a fundamental metric, you may not compare it to a raw close. Read `SELECT * FROM state.price_level_criterion_drift WHERE position_key = '<key>'` (`bigquery/197_price_level_criterion_dividend_drift.sql`) and test against `dividend_adjusted_level`, not `price_level`. The level was fixed at entry; the price series drops by every subsequent ex-dividend, so an unadjusted comparison drifts **always in the fire-earlier direction**. Report BOTH numbers and the dividend you netted out. **Two flags on that row are not optional reading:** `marks_cover_reference = FALSE` means `events.daily_marks` does not reach back to the reference date and the dividend total is an INCOMPLETE lower bound — reconcile the uncovered head of the window against FMP `calendar` / `dividends-calendar` (the date-range form works on this plan tier; the per-symbol `dividends-company` form does not) before concluding; `reference_date_declared = FALSE` means the criterion never recorded WHICH date its level was observed on, so the view fell back to the entry date, which is a lower bound rather than the truth. **The worked instance:** B:MSCI's criterion named the 550.79 post-event trough — the 2026-07-24 CUM-DIVIDEND closing low. MSCI went ex-dividend 2.05 on 2026-08-14. The 2026-08-17 close of 550.68 read as a breach by 0.11 (0.020%) against a line 2.05 (0.372%) too high — the distortion was **18.6x the breach margin**. The like-for-like line is 548.74, and 550.68 sits 1.94 ABOVE it: on a total-return basis the criterion was NOT breached. The position was exited anyway.

For each watchlist candidate: does any Development materially change candidacy status (closer to entry / invalidated / unchanged)?

ANALYSIS — ADD-CANDIDATE CHECK (Strategies A, B, D only — Rev 40, owner directive 2026-07-21; each strategy's "Adding to an existing position" section, `strategy/03_strategy_a.md` / `04_strategy_b.md` / `06_strategy_d.md`). This is a DIFFERENT strategy set than the reactive-cadence set the OPPORTUNITY CHECK above is scoped to (currently A, B, C, E) — **C (options) and E (pair) NEVER get an add flag here, and D IS in scope here despite carrying `review_cadence: long_horizon` and sitting outside OPPORTUNITY CHECK's reactive set**, because an add rides on the position-level read this routine already performs daily for every open A-E position (`state.current_positions`, read above with each position's entry-record thesis-invalidation criteria — ANALYSIS — RISK TO EXISTING POSITIONS), not on D's slower M4/Q4 NEW-entry generation cadence. Adds are AI judgment, case by case, exactly like a first entry's thesis call — there is no mechanical trigger.

For every currently-open position in Strategy A, B, or D (from `state.current_positions`): does any Development above, or the AI's own case-by-case read of the existing book, create an ADD opportunity — a second (or subsequent) independently sized tranche onto an already-held name? Every proposed add uses a fresh no-ceiling per-thesis risk budget, justified against the seven factors and adversarially attacked on size; it is never a fixed 2% tranche. Per each strategy's "Adding to an existing position" section, the trigger is either (a) **a dip against an intact thesis** (adverse price action with no invalidation news — the position's own "Not exit-triggering" list) or (b) **strengthened conviction** (new information reinforcing, not replacing, the original thesis) — either is AI judgment, not a formula.

**HARD GATE, checked first, per candidate — the ONLY gate:** does the add coincide with the position's ORIGINAL at-entry invalidation criteria (the same criteria already read for the RISK sweep above)? If those criteria are breached, or the add would itself sit in invalidation territory, this is **NOT an add — it is an exit**: route it through ANALYSIS — RISK TO EXISTING POSITIONS above instead, and do not flag it here. Only a position whose invalidation criteria remain UNBREACHED may be flagged as an ADD candidate. (No cumulative-tranche cap applies once this gate clears — Strategy.md "Adding to an existing position," each strategy's section.)

**REMEDY IS M3'S ASSESSMENT, NOT GATE RELAXATION (added 2026-09-27, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D1's `add_gate_uncovered_breach_status`, alert `3daf511e-3dcb-4d35-a385-d1e3a9b60336`).** A position whose `invalidation_status` cannot affirmatively confirm unbreached — including the `$.breach_status = 'NOT_ASSESSED_BY_THIS_BACKFILL'` case below — is CORRECTLY ineligible under this gate; the gate stays fail-closed. M3 owns backfilling a fresh breach assessment for such a legacy position each monthly cycle (see M3's BREACH-STATUS BACKFILL OWNERSHIP bullet) — a future session must not "fix" a structurally ineligible name by loosening this gate.

Per add opportunity flagged: ticker, strategy (A/B/D only), the existing position's entry date and original thesis ref (`events.decision_log` entry_id / `events.position_events` position_key), trigger type (dip-with-intact-thesis / strengthened-conviction) with the one-sentence reason, explicit confirmation the invalidation criteria are unbreached, next step ("full thesis construction required in a separate session, same rigor as a first entry, per Strategy.md 'Adding to an existing position'"). Adds are additionally subject to the SAME cross-strategy same-name exclusions as any first entry (no concurrent A-and-B, or A-and-C, position in the same name) — an add does not get a pass on those exclusions just because a position already exists.

**DURABLE LOG OF THIS SWEEP — including every DECLINE (added 2026-07-30, decision-record audit).** This section performs a real, substantive judgment on every open A/B/D position each day, and until now that reasoning existed ONLY in `Daily.md` — which is wholesale-OVERWRITTEN by the next session, not appended. So a decline was unqueryable within 24 hours and recoverable only by `git show` archaeology on a Daily.md commit. That is strictly worse than a prose log: it is a prose log that deletes itself. The declines are also where a systemic finding hides — on 2026-07-28 D1 evaluated all 11 open A/B/D positions and declined TWO (D:DIS, D:TSM) at the HARD GATE purely because their `invalidation_status` was NULL, so "unbreached" could not be affirmatively confirmed. That session's own process note escalated it ("legacy position rows without a populated `invalidation_status` are structurally ineligible for adds regardless of how good the case is"), but no routine could see or COUNT it, because the note lived only in a file that is overwritten the next day.

At the end of this section, write **ONE** `events.decision_log` row for the whole sweep (not one per position — this is a daily cadence over ~10-14 positions, and one row per position would bury the corpus at ~4,000 rows/year against a table currently holding under 500):

`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(<date>, 'add-candidate-review', NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, '<title>', '<body_md>', '<fields JSON>', <refs>, <tags>, NULL, 'D1 <date>')`

`fields` JSON contract (the established write-time-contract pattern — `bigquery/96_research_screener.sql` for `research-screen` is the model; parsed by `state.add_candidate_reviews`, `bigquery/116`):
- `positions`: array of one object per open A/B/D position evaluated, each with `ticker`, `strategy`, `mark_vs_cost_pct`, `trigger_type` (`dip-with-intact-thesis` / `strengthened-conviction` / `none`), `disposition` (`flagged` / `declined` / `declined_hard_gate`), `reason` (the one-sentence judgment, verbatim), and `invalidation_criteria_evaluable` (boolean — see below)

  **`mark_vs_cost_pct` PRICE BASIS — THE IBKR REGULAR-SESSION DAILY BAR, AND THE PER-TRANCHE COST, NOT THE CONNECTOR'S POSITION MARK (pinned 2026-09-07 by D1, measured, not inferred).** The numerator is the last completed session's close from `get_price_history` (`step='ONE_DAY'`, `outside_rth=false`) — the same basis §19 PRICE BASIS already imposes on both move screens — and the denominator is **that tranche's own** `cost_basis / shares` from `state.current_positions`, never the account-level blended `avg_price` from `get_account_positions`. **Neither half was stated before, and both go wrong quietly.** Measured 2026-09-07, a Labor Day run whose figures MUST equal the previous run's because no session intervened: four of twelve did not. `get_account_positions.market_price` served **GOOGL at 335.00 — the 2026-09-01 close, three sessions stale** — against a true 2026-09-04 close of 338.46, and `get_price_snapshot` returned AMZN at 258.30 carrying `is_close:false` (a live-looking tick on a closed market) against a true close of 258.51. Taken through the tranche arithmetic those two stale marks moved D:TSM:2026-07-29 by 0.24pp (+8.9334 → +9.1699), D:GOOGL:2026-07-09 by 0.07pp, D:GOOGL:2026-07-26 by 0.08pp and D:UBER:2026-07-09 by 0.08pp between two runs that saw the identical session. **The magnitudes are trivial and the failure mode is not:** this field is the only durable per-tranche price record the add sweep leaves, W5 reads the series for calibration, and a number that moves when nothing moved is unreadable as a series whatever its size. **The tell to check before trusting any holiday or after-hours mark: `is_close` must be TRUE, and a position-endpoint mark is not evidence of a close at all.**
- `invalidation_criteria_evaluable` is **FALSE when the HARD GATE cannot affirmatively confirm "unbreached" from the mirror field**. That means ALL THREE of these disjuncts, ORed together: `state.current_positions.invalidation_status IS NULL`; the case a plain IS-NULL test would miss — `JSON_VALUE(invalidation_status,'$.status') = 'NOT_DISCRETELY_RECORDED_AT_ENTRY'`, the honest marker `bigquery/117` wrote for the two Strategy B positions that genuinely recorded no discrete criteria at entry; **and `JSON_VALUE(invalidation_status,'$.breach_status') = 'NOT_ASSESSED_BY_THIS_BACKFILL'` (third disjunct added 2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D1's `add_review_evaluable_misses_breach_status`).** Do NOT implement this as `invalidation_status IS NULL`: since the 2026-07-30 backfill that is FALSE for all 14 open positions, so an IS-NULL test would report every position as evaluable and silently re-hide exactly the ambiguity this field exists to make legible.

  **WHY THE THIRD DISJUNCT EXISTS — the two-key test was measured to re-hide the ambiguity through a key it did not test (D1 2026-09-06, by writing the field, not by inference).** Applied literally to all 12 open A/B/D tranches the two-disjunct rule returned TRUE for **every one** — including the 3 that same sweep declined at the HARD GATE — because NOT ONE of the 12 carries a `$.status` key at all, while **SEVEN record the gap under a different key and value**, `$.breach_status = 'NOT_ASSESSED_BY_THIS_BACKFILL'`, written by the same `bigquery/117` mirror that transcribed criteria verbatim and explicitly did not assess them: `D:AMZN:2026-07-09`, `D:DIS:2026-05-07`, `D:GOOGL:2026-07-09`, `D:ISRG:2026-07-20`, `D:RTX:2026-04-27`, `D:TSM:2026-07-21`, `D:UBER:2026-07-09`. Four of those seven are covered at NAME level by a later tranche carrying a fresh assessment (AMZN, DIS, GOOGL, TSM); **three are covered nowhere in the record — ISRG, RTX, UBER — and are structurally ineligible for an add.** So the field reported `evaluable = TRUE` for exactly the positions whose breach status was never assessed, in the same direction as the IS-NULL mistake this bullet's own paragraph already warns against. **The gate verdict was never wrong** — D1 declined those three on the HARD GATE regardless and carried the gap in `disposition='declined_hard_gate'` plus `fields.breach_status_unassessed` / `fields.breach_status_uncovered_names` — but the FIELD said the opposite of what the gate did, and this field exists to be read by later sessions that will not re-derive the gate.

  **NULL-SAFETY — the literal transcription of the rule above returns NULL, not TRUE, for the healthy case (found and fixed 2026-08-17, D1).** Written as `NOT (invalidation_status IS NULL OR JSON_VALUE(invalidation_status,'$.status') = 'NOT_DISCRETELY_RECORDED_AT_ENTRY')`, a position with a populated `invalidation_status` that carries **no `$.status` key at all** makes the equality comparison NULL, so the expression evaluates `NOT(FALSE OR NULL)` = **NULL**. Measured 2026-08-17: that is the state of ALL 14 open positions — every one has a populated `invalidation_status` and not one carries a `$.status` key — so a session transcribing the rule literally emits 14 NULLs into `fields` instead of 14 TRUEs, silently degrading the exact field this bullet exists to keep legible, and in the same direction as the IS-NULL mistake the paragraph above already warns against. **Wrap it: `COALESCE(JSON_VALUE(invalidation_status,'$.status'), '') = 'NOT_DISCRETELY_RECORDED_AT_ENTRY'`** (or equivalently `NOT COALESCE(<the OR-expression>, FALSE)`), so an absent key reads as "not the honest marker" rather than as unknown. The two disqualifying conditions are a logical OR, not an AND — the prose "BOTH of" above enumerates the two cases the field must catch, and either one alone makes it FALSE.
- `n_evaluated`, `n_flagged`, `n_declined_hard_gate`

Use `trigger_type` values EXACTLY as spelled above — this is a controlled vocabulary for the same reason `entry_type` is (see "Decision-log lifecycle" → CURRENT ERA discipline 1); the two existing add rows already drifted (`fields.trigger='dip-against-intact-thesis'` singular vs `fields.triggers=['dip-with-intact-thesis',...]` plural, different key AND different spelling), which is precisely why it is pinned here. `body_md` carries the narrative process note as usual. This log is RECORD-ONLY: it changes no gate and blocks nothing. A day with zero open A/B/D positions writes no row.

**Late-data discipline for this durable add-candidate record:** immediately before the initial `sp_log_decision` call, re-read `state.current_positions` and any overlapping D2a reconciliation output, then write the final observed facts. If a fill/reconciliation or any other fact changes after the append, leave the original untouched and append one complete replacement through `sp_log_decision` that preserves `entry_type='add-candidate-review'`, carries tag `correction`, passes `in_superseded_by=<original entry_id>`, and supplies the full corrected `fields`/`body_md`. **Never UPDATE, DELETE, or MERGE `events.decision_log`.**

ANALYSIS — REGIME CHECK

Does any Development plausibly shift any strategy's router activation state enough to warrant an inter-monthly router review, given the shared regime vocabulary and per-strategy activation rules in Strategy.md? High bar; default NO on ambiguity.

EQUITY-BREADTH OBSERVATION (added 2026-08-05 — D1 OBSERVES, D2a CLASSIFIES; feeds D2a STEP 1e's `EQUITY_BREADTH` router key)

**Why this sits in D1 and not in D2a.** `strategy/01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md` defines Equity Breadth State as *"the percentage of S&P 500 constituents closing above their own 200-day SMA,"* computed **daily**. D2a owns the router's technical half but is a mechanical broker-reconcile routine with only IBKR / FMP / BigQuery — it has no research tooling, and neither connector can enumerate the ~500 constituents (see D2a STEP 1e for that measured, still-accurate finding). D1 is a **daily deep-research** routine that already holds Tavily / `web_search` / `web_fetch`, and Q1 already sourced this exact metric this way on 2026-07-01 (`Quarterly_Regime.md` — StreetStats and Barchart `$S5TH`, ~62–63% at quarter-end). **Fetching a published, pre-aggregated number is data acquisition, not AI classification** — the vocabulary's "no AI classification" rule binds the *threshold decision*, which stays mechanical in D2a. Do not move this step into D2a, and do not let D2a fetch it.

1. **Obtain the published % of S&P 500 constituents closing above their own 200-day SMA, for the LAST COMPLETED TRADING SESSION.** Candidate sources (a floor, not a ceiling — §"Evidence lists are floors, not ceilings"): **MacroMicro `US - S&P 500 Stocks above 200-Day Average` (https://en.macromicro.me/series/22718/sp-500-200ma-breadth) is the PREFERRED PRIMARY** — reachable only via Tavily extract (direct `web_fetch` returns HTTP 403), and its `Latest Stats` block states its own as-of date plus the prior reading. Then EODData `$S5TH` (https://www.eoddata.com/stockquote/INDEX/S5TH.htm — note the path omits the `$`), Barchart `$S5TH`, StreetStats, Investing.com, or any equivalent published tracker. Prefer a source that states the metric's **as-of session date** explicitly.

   **SETTLEMENT LAG — why MacroMicro is primary and EODData is not (measured 2026-08-18, D1).** EODData serves a NEAR-CLOSE, UNSETTLED value in the D1 evening slot and revises it upward afterwards; MacroMicro already carries the settled figure the same evening. Measured on the one occasion it could be checked: D1 2026-08-17 recorded **68.38** for 2026-08-17 off EODData at ~18:20 ET and treated it as settled, explicitly noting MacroMicro read 68.58 the same evening and dismissing the 0.20pp gap as inside tolerance. Re-fetched the next day, **EODData itself showed 68.58** for that session, and Investing.com independently carried 68.58 — three-source agreement that MacroMicro had been right and the recorded value was wrong. **Detection tell for an unsettled EODData bar: `Low == Close` on the current day's row** (the running low equals the last print), together with an on-page timestamp BEFORE 16:00 ET. If you see it, you are not holding a settled close. Investing.com typically has no row for the current session at all at D1 time, so it is a same-evening cross-check only for the PRIOR session.

   **MACROMICRO HAS BEEN UNREACHABLE ON EVERY RUN SINCE 2026-08-19 — SIX CONSECUTIVE FAILURES, so "PREFERRED PRIMARY" above currently names a source this routine cannot actually fetch (recorded 2026-08-25, D1).** Every attempt since 2026-08-20 has returned `Failed to fetch url` from `tavily_extract` (advanced depth, cache-busted) and HTTP 403 on a direct `web_fetch`; only the stale search-index snippet is retrievable, and it lags by a session. The 2026-08-20 run flagged this forward ("if MacroMicro stays unreachable across several runs that is a source-availability regression to act on, not absorb") and it has stayed unreachable for four runs since. **Keep trying it first — the designation is NOT withdrawn**, because the 2026-08-17 settlement-lag finding that earned it is unrefuted and a recovered MacroMicro is still the best source. But **treat Barchart `$S5TH` as the OPERATIVE primary while MacroMicro is down** (post-close timestamped, states its own session date, carries a Previous Close field), and do not record a run as having "cross-checked against the primary" when the primary never answered. A run that reaches a value through Barchart alone has a SINGLE usable source and must say so.

   **DESIGNATION RESTRUCTURED — BARCHART IS THE DECLARED PRIMARY; MACROMICRO IS A WEEKLY RE-PROBE, NOT A PER-RUN FIRST ATTEMPT (2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, adjudicating D1's `breadth_primary_source_persistently_unreachable`).** The paragraph above was written at SIX consecutive failures and answered the question by deferring it. D1 re-raised on 2026-09-02 with the streak more than doubled — **not one successful MacroMicro fetch on any run since 2026-08-19**, on both paths (HTTP 403 to a rendering `web_fetch`, `Failed to fetch url` to `tavily_extract` at advanced depth, with a cache-buster). W5 adjudicates it as follows, and the ruling is narrow: **this is a question about how long an unreachable-but-superior source stays NOMINAL, not an argument that Barchart is better.** The 2026-08-17 settlement-lag finding stands unrefuted and MacroMicro resumes the designation the moment it answers again.
   - **What changes.** Barchart `$S5TH` is the **PRIMARY** for this step. MacroMicro is a **re-probe candidate**: attempt it on the FIRST D1 run of each calendar week only (not every run), and on a success immediately restore it to primary for that run and every run after, recording the restoration in the `rationale`. **"CALENDAR WEEK" HERE MEANS THE SUNDAY-ANCHORED WEEK — i.e. the probe rides on the SUNDAY D1 run (disambiguated 2026-09-07 by D1, one line, before it could cost a probe).** D1's cadence is Sun–Thu, so a Sunday anchor puts the probe on the week's FIRST D1 fire and gives exactly one probe per week. Under the other natural reading — the ISO Mon–Sun week — Sunday falls at the END of its ISO week, so a week would probe on Monday AND again on the following Sunday (two probes, double the spend this ruling exists to cut) or, if a Sunday run were counted against the ISO week just ending, none at all in a week whose Monday run was skipped. Both failure modes are silent. **This changed nothing on the day it was written** and is recorded rather than merely acted on: 2026-09-07 was a Monday, but it was also a US market holiday with no completed session inside the scan window, so no breadth figure was owed from any source and no probe was due under EITHER reading — which is precisely why it was the right day to settle it rather than a day when the answer decided a metered call. Everything else about the step — the settlement-lag tells, the cross-check discipline, the single-usable-source disclosure, the idempotency rule — is unchanged and still binding.
   - **Why per-run probing is the wrong shape once the failure is persistent.** A per-run probe of a source that has failed 13+ consecutive times is a metered call that buys nothing, which is exactly what the shared "Metered external calls" rule names as *the one thing that IS waste*. This is measured, not asserted: W5's own 2026-09-06 EXTERNAL-SPEND DIGEST found `en.macromicro.me/series/22718/sp-500-200ma-breadth` is the **#2 repeat-fetched target in the entire fleet** at 4.46 credits on repeats (behind only `barchart.com/stocks/quotes/$s5th` at 7.09) — the fleet is paying, weekly, to re-confirm a 403. A weekly probe preserves the recovery path at ~1/5th the spend.
   - **What is NOT changed, deliberately.** No fallback is removed and no new source is added — the candidate list stays a floor, not a ceiling. The single-source disclosure obligation is **strengthened, not relieved**: a run reaching its figure through Barchart alone still has one usable source and must say so in `rationale`, and the fact that Barchart is now the declared primary does not make that disclosure optional.
   **AND BARCHART IS NOT IMMUNE TO THE SAME SETTLEMENT REVISION — measured 2026-08-25, D1.** The paragraph above frames the revise-upward-after-the-close behaviour as an EODData property that MacroMicro does not share. It is not exclusively an EODData property. On 2026-08-25 Barchart's own Previous Close field read **72.16** for the 2026-08-24 session against the **72.11** D1 had written the previous evening off that same Barchart page at 18:01 ET — i.e. Barchart revised its own settled figure by +0.05pp overnight. EODData's live quote-box PREV agreed at 72.16 while EODData's *settled historical table* still read 72.11, so the two vendors' live widgets agreed with each other and disagreed with the archived history. Internal consistency settles which is Barchart's own truth: its stated change of −1.59 reconciles as 70.57 − 72.16, not as 70.57 − 72.11. **Consequence for a session: a failed Previous-Close self-check of ~0.05pp against the stored prior value is EXPECTED NOISE, not evidence of a stale page** — the stale-page tell remains the on-page as-of date, never a small Previous-Close mismatch. Do not withhold a row over it, and **do not retroactively correct the prior session's row** (the idempotency rule below is unchanged and binding); record the revised prior value in the CURRENT day's `rationale` so the true day-over-day change is reconstructable. A LARGE Previous-Close mismatch is a different animal and still means the page is wrong — Investing.com was rejected on 2026-08-24 for a Prev. Close of 56.46 that matched no anchor at all.

   **DO NOT retroactively correct a prior session's row to fix this.** The key is idempotent on `(as_of_date, scope, key)` and D2a STEP 1e reads it `ORDER BY as_of_date DESC LIMIT 1` with **no `event_ts` tiebreak**, so a second row on the same `as_of_date` makes a live consumer read nondeterministically. Record the correction in the CURRENT day's `rationale` instead, stating the prior session's settled value so a reader can reconstruct the true day-over-day change.
2. **PIN THE MEASUREMENT DATE — do not accept "latest" blindly.** Record the value against the session it actually measures, never against today's fetch date. *This is the exact failure that produced the 2026-07-31 VIX / treasury defects* (an unpinned quote has no date argument, so "latest" silently meant the prior session). Prefer a source that states its own as-of session, and set `as_of_date` from that. **A Tavily/extract fetch can serve a STALE CACHE, and this has already happened here — pass a cache-busting query param (e.g. `?cb=<today>`), the same guard M1a's `hy_oas` step carries for `fred.stlouisfed.org`.** On the 2026-08-16 run a Tavily-extracted Barchart copy came back explicitly headed *"Quote Overview for Fri, Aug 7th, 2026"* — nine days stale — and **coincidentally also read 72.76**, the dangerous shape where a stale page looks confirmatory rather than obviously wrong (`Daily.md`, Sources-tried-and-REJECTED). The on-page date is what catches this, so a source that does not state one cannot satisfy step 2 at all: read the date off the page you actually received, never off the request you intended to make. **THE FETCH METHOD IS PART OF THE PROVENANCE — the SAME URL can serve different vintages to a rendering fetch and to a static extractor (measured 2026-08-26).** `stockanalysis.com/stocks/ANF/` returned to `WebFetch` the correct current quote correctly labelled *“At close: Aug 26, 2026, 4:00 PM EDT”*, while `tavily_extract` on that IDENTICAL URL returned a pre-rally cache (`Previous Close 109.01`, `Day's Range 109.83–113.42`, against a true close of 147.75) carrying no price header and **no as-of date at all**, and Tavily's search index held a third copy at an Aug 19–20 vintage. **Consequence for the rule above: an undated payload condemns THAT FETCH, not the SOURCE.** Before recording a site under Sources-tried-and-REJECTED, re-try it on the OTHER path — rendering `WebFetch` with a cache-busting param when an extract came back undated — because rejecting a site that a different path reads correctly is its own evidence loss. Record which path produced the figure you kept. Google Finance was correctly dated on BOTH paths the same session, so this is a per-site cache-tier defect, not a general property of third-party pages.
   **FALLBACK — post-close inference, explicitly labelled.** Measured 2026-08-05: the published trackers render their values client-side, so a fetch reliably returns the NUMBER but not an as-of date (Barchart `$S5TH` served a value with its date field unfilled; StreetStats and indexindicators returned no parseable values at all; Barchart's daily price-history URL 404s; FMP `chart` is plan-gated for index symbols). So a strict dated-source-only rule would write nothing, every day. Therefore: when only an undated live value is obtainable, you MAY attribute it to the last completed session — **but ONLY if all three hold**: (a) D1 is running in its normal post-close slot and the US session for that date has actually closed (check, do not assume — an intraday value is not a close); (b) you record the literal token `date_attribution=inferred_post_close` in `rationale`; and (c) you record the fetch timestamp alongside the value. **Never** apply this fallback to a pre-close or weekend/holiday fetch, and never let an inferred-date row silently look like a source-dated one — a downstream reader must be able to tell the two apart mechanically.

   **THE ON-PAGE TIME IS PART OF THE CHECK, NOT ONLY THE ON-PAGE DATE — added 2026-09-20 by D1, measured on its own prior row.** A correct as-of DATE does not establish a SETTLED close, and the settlement-lag paragraphs above only ever pinned the date. D1's 2026-09-17 run wrote **51.09** for session 2026-09-17, correctly source-dated ("Quote Overview for Thu, Sep 17th, 2026"), cross-checked against EODData at the identical value, and recorded in the same `rationale` that **both** sources carried an on-page timestamp of **14:58 ET — roughly an hour BEFORE the 16:00 ET close — despite being fetched at ~18:10 ET**. Re-fetched 2026-09-20, Barchart and EODData both carry **50.29** for that session: the figure settled **0.80pp LOWER**, which is **16x** the ~0.05pp overnight-revision band the Barchart paragraph above blesses as expected noise. The documented compound EODData tell (`Low == Close`) did NOT fire, and two independent sources agreeing did NOT help — they agreed on the same unsettled snapshot. **So: require the page's own timestamp to be at or after 16:00 ET for the session it claims. When it is not, re-fetch before recording; if the value is recorded anyway, carry the literal token `unsettled_at_fetch=<hh:mm ET>` in `rationale` so a later reader can tell.** The idempotency rule below is unchanged and binding — do NOT go back and correct the prior session's row; state the settled prior value in the CURRENT day's `rationale` instead.
3. **Cross-check when a second source is obtainable.** If two independent sources disagree by more than 5 percentage points, write NO row and say so in `Daily.md` — D2a's carry-forward-with-staleness-alarm handles the gap correctly, and a wrong number is far worse than a stale one.
4. **Write it:** `INSERT INTO events.regime_events (as_of_date, scope, key, value, numeric_value, rationale, source_review_ref)` with `scope='TECHNICAL_INPUT'`, `key='EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT'`, `as_of_date` = the measured session's date (step 2), `numeric_value` = the percentage as a 0–100 number, `value` = the source name, `rationale` = the source URL + the figure as published + the as-of wording the source itself used, `source_review_ref = 'D1 <run date> EQUITY-BREADTH OBSERVATION'`. Idempotent on `(as_of_date, scope, key)`. **Do NOT write to `scope='TECHNICAL_SIGNAL'`** — that scope is D2a's, and the HEALTHY/WEAK threshold is D2a's to apply.
5. **Best-effort, and fail SILENT-BUT-VISIBLE.** A fetch failure must never abort D1. On failure write **no row at all** — never a guessed, recalled, sampled, or model-produced figure, and never a number carried over from a monthly prose paragraph. Note the miss in `Daily.md`. **Reason this is stated so bluntly:** the value this key carried until 2026-08-05 (67) was exactly that — an unsourced figure that appeared unprompted in an M1a rationale, whose reported window even changed between runs (May: "~54% above 50-day"; June: absent; July: "~67% above 200-day"), and it fed two strategies' activation gates for days. An absent row is honest; an invented one is not.

PARK ALLOCATION CALL (owner-review design `PARK_ROUTER_DESIGN.md` v2, 2026-07-18 — the AI Park Allocator; loop `park_allocator` in `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`, Operating_Protocols.md §13.F). The natural last analytical output of this scan — D1 already reads the whole tape every trading day, and the park call should see the day's developments.

Evidence gathering, fresh each session (house "no memory recall" discipline) — a floor, not a ceiling, the session is free to weigh, discount, or seek evidence beyond it:
- Live `^VIX` — **PRIMARY: IBKR `get_price_history` (`contract_id=13455763`, `security_type='IND'`, `exchange='CBOE'`, `step='ONE_DAY'`)**, which returns a clean daily OHLC series; FMP `mcp__FMP__quote`/`mcp__FMP__chart` is the FALLBACK and may be unavailable — `quote` returns ACCESS DENIED (plan-gated) as measured by D1 on 2026-08-23 and again 2026-08-24, `ops.alerts` category `fmp_quote_plan_gated`. **DO NOT RAISE A FRESH `fmp_quote_plan_gated` ROW FOR THE STANDING CONSTRAINT (added 2026-08-26 — the third re-raise in four days).** FMP's tier surface is a STANDING vendor limit, fully recorded in the shared FMP TIER MATRIX rule and in `ops/connector_tools.yaml`; re-alerting it each cycle is the alarm fatigue this fleet's alert discipline exists to prevent, and it has already cost three operator notifications (2026-08-23, 08-24, 08-26) for an unchanging fact. **Only a MOVE in the surface is new information** — an endpoint the matrix records as WORKING now denying, or a denied one now returning. Before raising, (i) re-read the TIER MATRIX, and (ii) re-test the single-symbol canary (`quote` on AAPL) so the row states a MEASURED tool-wide outage rather than a batch-endpoint denial generalised to the tool. **And never state a tier claim the same run has already contradicted:** the 2026-08-26 row asserted “FMP quote (all endpoints) … plan-gated” in a run whose own `ops.run_log` note records a successful FMP `aftermarket-quote` read for NVDA. A degraded SCREEN is reported in `Daily.md` and in the `research-screen` decision_log record per that screen's REPORTING RULE — that is the channel for it, not a repeat vendor-tier alert. **CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (D3):** this line previously asserted that "no daily VIX series exists anywhere else in this stack" and named FMP as the only source; that assertion is false in both halves and was verified false in-session by pulling the IBKR series above (2026-08-19 close 14.89 → 08-20 16.01 → 08-21 15.13 → 08-24 15.85, matching the reading D1's 2026-08-23 run already took from this same path). `events.signal_marks` (D2a STEP 1d) remains a deliberately isolated evidence layer on its own merits — that design does NOT rest on VIX being otherwise unobtainable.
- Index level and general character of today's tape — IBKR `get_price_snapshot`/`get_price_history`, FMP fallback.
- `state.park_signal_daily` — trend/drawdown/vol context for the menu tickers (briefing input the AI may weigh or override, never a mechanical input).
- The latest `hy_oas` (`state.macro_fred_latest WHERE metric='hy_oas'`) and `state.current_regime`'s `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` scores (incl. `shock_overlay`, `inflation_trend`).
- Today's own DEVELOPMENTS section above.
- Anything else this session judges relevant.

THE CALL (structured, auditable — no threshold, no lookup table, no formula anywhere in this decision):
- `vehicle` — any menu instrument from `state.park_menu` (KEEP = today's `state.park_policy_current.vehicle`)
- `conviction` — HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW + a numeric `conviction_pct`
- `rationale` — one paragraph explicitly addressing why this instrument beats the runner-up
- `invalidation` — the observable development that would flip this call. **SYMMETRIC EVIDENTIARY STANDARD (2026-08-18).** State it at the same bar as the evidence that justified the CURRENT position, in both directions. Concretely: if a de-risk out of the default vehicle was made on a narrative/judgment case, the conditions for returning must not be a conjunctive numeric checklist — and vice versa. This is a discipline about how the criteria are WRITTEN, not a threshold or a rule table; the call itself remains AI judgment end to end (`PARK_ROUTER_DESIGN.md` §1), and naming criteria never binds a later session against its own judgment. **Why it matters structurally, not for performance:** the 2026-07-26 directive retired every anti-churn rail and named *next-session reversibility* as the compensating control for having none. A re-entry bar materially harder to clear than the exit bar makes the defensive position sticky and quietly removes that control. Worked precedent: the 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-02 KEEP-SGOV calls named a conjunctive re-entry bar ("30Y sustained below ~5.10% AND September hike odds under ~50% AND a confirmed Hormuz reopening — any one alone is not enough") after an exit justified narratively; the 30Y was still 5.31% on 2026-08-17, so honoring that bar literally would have held the park in SGOV through VOO 684.56 → 706.23 (~$265 of foregone return on the park as then sized). The 2026-08-03 SWITCH correctly overrode it — the self-correction worked, and this note exists so the next session does not have to rely on catching it.
- `theater_check` — a one-line self-audit that the rationale isn't narrating a foregone conclusion

Default-KEEP on ambiguity — the same high-bar, default-NO posture as the ANALYSIS — REGIME CHECK flag above. `Daily.md` gets a mandatory `## PARK ALLOCATION CALL` section carrying the five fields above, every trading day, including a KEEP day.

**GRADED ALLOCATION — THE CALL NOW CARRIES A TARGET FRACTION (activated on live capital 2026-09-04,
owner directive; `PARK_ALLOCATOR_V4_DESIGN.md` §2.3, `bigquery/216`/`218`/`220`/`221`).** The park is a
TWO-SLEEVE book: a risk sleeve (default VOO) and a defensive sleeve (default SGOV), with a defensive
fraction **f in {0, 25, 50, 75, 100}**. The call emits `target_f_pct` alongside the sleeves; a "switch"
is a WEIGHT DELTA, not a vehicle swap, and f=0 / f=100 remain legal and mean exactly what VOO-only and
SGOV-only always meant.

  - **Read `state.park_axis_daily` for today.** It publishes, mechanically, each axis's LEVEL
    (defensive or not, from its last MEASURED reading) and EVENT (`is_firing` = ENTERED defensive
    within 2 sessions), plus `standing_defensive_count`, `firing_count`, `cap_pct`,
    `increase_gate_open` and `testable_axes`. **A standing state is never news** — that distinction is
    the whole point, and is the defect behind the 2026-09-01 record counting a three-week-old
    `shock_overlay='acute'` as same-session deterioration.
  - **MIXED VINTAGE — CHECK `measured_on` PER AXIS.** On a live D1 run the four price-derived axes
    (volatility, credit, index, shock) are **ALWAYS one session behind**: D1 runs 16:12-16:36 MT and
    D2a, whose STEP 1d writes `events.signal_marks`, does not start until 16:41 MT. Only `breadth` is
    same-session, and only because D1 wrote `EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT` itself minutes earlier. This is
    structural, not an outage — `axes_measured_today` on the same view counts the fresh ones. Where
    your own live readings contradict a carried axis, record it in `fields.axis_overrides` with the
    reading and its as-of date. **The mechanical count may NOT BLOCK or DEMOTE a de-risk on an axis
    whose `measured_on` is not today** — that would let yesterday's stale quiet veto today's observed
    deterioration. The ratchet still holds the other way: a carried axis may never be counted as
    FIRING, because an event is by definition a change and a carried reading is not evidence of one.
  - **CAP — `park_axis_daily.cap_pct` IS THE RAW CAP, NOT THE ONE YOU CLAMP TO.** It is
    `LEAST(100, 25 x standing_defensive_count)` off TODAY's standing count alone. The cap f is actually
    clamped to is the DECAY-CONFIRMED cap of the next bullet, which is STICKY — it holds high while a
    lower standing count is still being confirmed. These are different numbers: measured 2026-09-04
    they disagree on **8 of 68** live sessions, maximum gap **75pp** (2026-06-05: raw 25, confirmed
    100). The confirmed cap is PATH-DEPENDENT and is **not** recoverable from any fixed-width window
    over `cap_pct` — a 3-session `MAX`, the obvious approximation, misses all eight. Compute the clamp
    in-session per the DECAY bullet; `analytics.park_ladder_shadow.confirmed_cap_pct` is the same
    quantity computed retrospectively, for reconciliation only. Note the confirmed cap is >= the raw
    cap on every session measured, so it is a CEILING that the one-way ratchet below forbids you from
    using to license a larger de-risk than your own hand-scoring supports.
  - **INCREASING f (de-risking) requires the gate:** at least one axis ENTERED defensive within 2
    sessions AND `standing_defensive_count >= 2`. A single standing axis never engages an increase —
    that is the landed cardinality floor, preserved, and all 15 measured one-day single-axis episodes
    in history cost $0.
  - **CONVICTION SIZES IT.** Suggested target = the step NEAREST to `conviction_pct x cap_pct`, ties
    round DOWN, never above cap. You may deviate by ±1 step with a NAMED reason. Worked: MEDIUM-60 at
    cap 50 -> 30 -> **25**. HIGH-95 at cap 100 -> 95 -> **100**. Conviction-85 at cap 100 -> **75**.
    This is the owner's specific ask made mechanical: a MEDIUM-60 two-axis de-risk no longer moves the
    same capital as a HIGH-95 four-axis one.
  - **DECAY IS AUTOMATIC AND YOU MUST STATE IT.** Each session f is clamped to the confirmed cap. The
    cap steps DOWN only on the first session at which the lower standing count has ALREADY held on the
    two preceding measured sessions (three consecutive readings, step on the third); a clamp from
    f >= 50 unwinds at most ONE step per session; a clamp crossing only 25->0 executes immediately; and
    a crisis-entered increase is exempt from the clamp for 2 sessions. **Compute the clamped f, state
    the arithmetic in the rationale, and emit the clamped value** — decay never happens outside a
    session, which is precisely what keeps this AI judgment inside rails rather than a rule table
    running the book (`PARK_ROUTER_DESIGN.md` §1's rejection of v1 turns on exactly that distinction).
  - **DECREASING f is always allowed and never delayed** — re-risks have measured RIGHT (both the
    2026-08-03 and 2026-09-03 re-entries were correct).
  - **CRISIS OVERRIDE:** a single-session index move <= -2.5% or VIX >= 28 lifts the cap to 100 that
    session.
  - **Log `target_f_pct`, `risk_sleeve`, `defensive_sleeve` in `fields`** alongside the existing keys.
    `vehicle` stays populated as the MAJORITY sleeve (tie at f=50 -> the risk sleeve), because
    `dbt/models/sources.yml` carries a live `not_null` test on it.

**FORWARD TEST IS RUNNING — this is not a settled system.** Activated 2026-09-04 against a measured
record that does NOT flatter it: over 15 historical episodes the defensive signal had mean forward edge
−0.638pp (SD 1.308) and won only 4 of 15, and across the three shadow episodes the ladder beat the
binary path every time (**+2.30 / +2.72 / +0.84pp** against the explicit binary counterfactual arm; CORRECTED 2026-09-04 from +1.62 / +1.56 / +0.84, which was measured before two defects were fixed — the STRICT decay was implemented as a trailing MAX rather than three-consecutive-readings, and the binary comparison was inferred from the policy vehicle STRING instead of scored as its own arm) while trailing never-switching every time (−1.09 /
−0.91 / −0.63pp). Read that as: GRADING beats the all-or-nothing switch, and de-risking at all still
costs against simply holding VOO. W5's PARK FORWARD-TEST COUNTDOWN forces the re-evaluation after
three post-activation episodes.

**DE-RISK EVIDENCE CARDINALITY (added 2026-09-03; SUPERSEDED as the SIZING rule by the graded ladder
above, RETAINED as its floor — a single standing axis still licenses no increase).** A **de-risk** — a SWITCH to a LOWER `state.park_menu.risk_tier` than today's opening `state.park_policy_current.vehicle` — converts the park only when **at least two INDEPENDENT evidence axes fire in the same session**. The axes are: **volatility** (VIX in any form), **breadth**, **index level/trend** (the index against its moving averages or its trailing closing high), **rates** (the 10Y, policy-path odds, the curve), **credit** (`hy_oas`, HY/IG spreads), and **shock/commodity** (`shock_overlay`, Brent, a named geopolitical channel). **Two readings on the SAME axis are ONE axis** — VIX below 15 outright and VIX below its own 20d is one axis, not two; that is the whole point of the rule. If exactly one axis fires, D1 calls **KEEP** and records `fields.park_watch = true` plus `fields.watch_axis` naming the axis that fired and what a second, independent axis would have to do to carry a de-risk; the call is then re-decided **fresh next session on next session's evidence**, exactly like any other KEEP. This is **not** a cooldown, a budget, a conviction gate, or an approval step — nothing is deferred to another party, no later session is bound by it, and a two-axis de-risk still binds and converts the SAME DAY at ANY conviction, precisely as before. **Re-risks and laterals are NOT subject to this rule** and are unchanged in every respect. D2 needs no change: a WATCH is an ordinary bound KEEP, and D2 already no-ops when the called vehicle equals the current policy vehicle.

**Why — measured 2026-09-03 (interactive-session probe), not inferred.** The 2026-09-01 de-risk fired on **ONE** axis (breadth); VIX's own clause explicitly did NOT fire, Brent missed by $0.35 and the VIX-50d leg by 0.11. The 2026-09-03 re-entry required **TWO** axes and got them on both limbs each. Exit on one, return on two — cheap to leave and dear to return, which is backwards for a park whose default vehicle is the risk asset. The 2026-08-18 SYMMETRIC EVIDENTIARY STANDARD above **cannot see this**: it compares clause KIND and HEIGHT, never clause **CARDINALITY**, so the two rules are complements and neither replaces the other. Measured cost of that one round trip: **$214.32** to the 2026-09-03 close (foregone VOO appreciation $215.61 against $3.03 SGOV carry and $1.75 commissions; execution was clean, slippage was $12.88 FAVORABLE), plus a wash-sale disallowance originally recorded as **$107.73 of the $149.18 realized loss** and twice corrected since. **(i)** SUPERSEDED 2026-09-04 by `bigquery/219`: the pre-rebuy figure is **$0.00**, because 13 of its 14 "replacements" were the sale's own basis seen through sibling legs of the same exchange-split order — a full liquidation was being washed by itself. **(ii)** The "of the $149.18" framing MIXES TWO BASES and they must never be netted: IBKR reports **−$149.18** account-level on AVERAGE-COST basis, while the repo's FIFO lot ledger (`analytics.park_tax_lots`, 20 fragments, 21.888 sh) reports **−$100.06** for the same liquidation — of which the losing legs are −$107.73 and the winning legs +$7.67. The **$49.12** gap is a BASIS-METHOD SEAM, not an un-disallowed remainder, and an earlier version of this sentence read it as one. The realized loss itself is broker-tied and unaffected throughout, and the 09-04 rebuy — FILLED at the broker 2026-09-04 13:30 UTC (VOO 21 @ 709.89 ARCA + 0.4714 @ 709.83 IBKR = the staged 21.4714), with the repo figure flipping when that session's D2a records it into events.parking_events — IS a genuine replacement and disallows essentially the whole $107.73 (`state.wash_sale_exposure`). Segment-scored on `analytics.park_counterfactuals` (AI era, anchor 2026-07-24), **both defensive excursions this allocator has taken have lost ground** (0-for-2): −2.841pp (SGOV 07-27..08-04) and −1.019pp (SGOV 09-02..09-03) — the two CLOSED defensive excursions of the AI era; the intervening −0.352pp (VOO 08-04..09-02) is the RISK-ON segment between them and is NOT a defensive excursion; AI +1.073% against never-switching VOO +4.650%. Note the reversal itself was NOT a freak: conditional on that exit state the re-entry set cleared within two sessions in 33.3% of 42 historical analogues, so the timing was genuinely unlucky — what was not luck is that a single-axis MEDIUM-60 de-risk was permitted to move ~97% of NAV at all.

**Counterfactual check — the test any rail here must pass, and DO NOT re-propose the alternatives.** This rule sends 2026-09-01 to WATCH, and leaves BOTH re-risks untouched: 2026-08-03 (a re-risk) and 2026-09-03 (a re-risk, and two axes regardless). It also leaves PA-01's three-axis crisis de-risk binding same-day. The **retired** rails do the opposite and were re-measured this session: a **5-day cooldown** blocks only the RE-ENTRY, holding the park in SGOV through ~09-08 while VOO rallied — a DEEPER loss, not a shorter one — and a **HIGH-conviction re-risk gate** blocks BOTH re-risks the allocator has ever made (08-03 and 09-03 were each MEDIUM 60), which would have stranded the park in SGOV from 07-26 through VOO ~690 → ~710. Both are strictly worse than doing nothing; do not re-propose either. The allocator already applied this discipline informally — clauses fired on 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-31 and it declined to flip both times.

**IMMEDIATE BINDING (owner directive 2026-07-26 — loop `park_allocator` is `active_auto` in `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`; Operating_Protocols.md §13.F; qualified for de-risks ONLY by the DE-RISK EVIDENCE CARDINALITY rule directly above, 2026-09-03).** Every well-formed call logs `status='BOUND'` the same day — a SWITCH (de-risk, lateral, or re-risk) at ANY conviction, or a KEEP (trivially BOUND, since D2's PARK ALLOCATION CONVERSION step already no-ops when the called vehicle equals the current policy vehicle — the "bound KEEP" case below). No conviction gate, no budget/cooldown check, and no next-session concurrence check gates whether `'BOUND'` is assigned. The only other status is `'HOLD'`, reserved for the connectors-down / evidence-ungatherable case below — D2 acts on any `status='BOUND'` call.

**LOGGED EVERY DAY, INCLUDING KEEP DAYS** (the daily no-change record is what makes calibration and the Q1 retrospective possible): `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(..., entry_type='park-allocation', ...)` with `fields` JSON carrying `{vehicle, conviction, conviction_pct, direction, status, readings}` (`status` is `'BOUND'` or `'HOLD'` only, per IMMEDIATE BINDING above) — `direction` = de-risk / lateral / re-risk / keep relative to today's opening `state.park_policy_current.vehicle`; `readings` = the evidence snapshot gathered above (VIX, hy_oas, the FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS values, `park_signal_daily` context). This is what `state.park_allocation_latest` surfaces to D2.

**READINGS PROVENANCE — EVERY CITED NUMBER MUST BE IN `fields.readings` (added 2026-09-04, park v4 Phase 1 evidence integrity; `PARK_ALLOCATOR_V4_DESIGN.md` §2.5).** Any numeric claim the rationale makes — an index level, a VIX print, a breadth reading, a sector count, a consecutive-session count — must appear in `fields.readings` as a key carrying the VALUE, its SOURCE, and its AS-OF date. A number that appears only in prose is not evidence; it is an assertion, and this system has now measured that assertion class failing twice in two consecutive sessions: `bigquery/213` corrected the 2026-09-01 record's "eight of eleven GICS sectors lower" (measured seven, and the four that rose were the three defensives plus energy, making the corrected pattern defensive rotation rather than the indiscriminate repricing the figure was recruited to prove — LOAD-BEARING, it was the stated ground for expiring the prior session's override), and `bigquery/214` corrected the 2026-09-03 record's "third consecutive improving session" (measured the second; harmless, because the clause it cleared asked for two). **COUNTS ARE COMPUTED, NEVER ASSERTED:** a consecutive-session count, a how-many-of-N count, or a threshold-crossing count must be derived from a series the readings name — `state.park_axis_daily` computes the axis-level and event-level counts mechanically and is the reference for anything it covers. **AND SO ARE SUPERLATIVES AND RECORD-CLAIMS — "largest ever", "first since", "widest on record" (added 2026-09-21, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D2's `park_rationale_unsupported_superlative`, alert `c9a8c721-8ffd-48e9-af88-ec4991cd6019`).** A superlative is a claim over an ENTIRE SERIES, so it is the least checkable sentence a rationale can contain and the one a reader is least likely to challenge. MEASURED: the 2026-09-08 park call (`events.decision_log` `c915970c-388e-4cb2-82cb-b1e222f0dfed`) asserted that a −3.38pp breadth move "is the largest single-session decline this key has recorded"; recomputed over `events.regime_events` `TECHNICAL_INPUT` / `EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT` it was the **third** largest, behind −4.38pp (2026-08-17) and −3.58pp (2026-09-01). **The rule: a superlative or record-claim must either appear in `fields.readings` with a source and a stated comparison window, so D2's EVIDENCE RECOMPUTE can check it, or not appear in the rationale at all.** "Largest in the trailing 60 sessions, source `events.regime_events` `EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT`" is a reading; "largest ever" is not. **This is deliberately NOT a new refusal trigger for D2.** That 2026-09-08 call CONVERTED correctly and should have: the defensive verdict rested on `60.63 < 66`, which was supported and true, and striking the superlative left standing count 3, cap 75 and f=25 all unchanged — so the claim was not load-bearing, and D2's EVIDENCE RECOMPUTE refusal fires on arithmetic CONTRADICTING `fields.readings`, which an unsupported superlative does not do. The fix belongs at the writing site, here: do not compose the sentence unless the series is in hand.

**AXIS SCORING IS ADVISORY, AND THE RATCHET IS ONE-WAY.** `state.park_axis_daily` (`bigquery/216`) publishes a mechanical LEVEL and EVENT per axis. D1 may consult it and MUST record any disagreement in `fields.axis_overrides` with a named reason. The AI's own hand-scoring remains authoritative for ACTION — this **survived the 2026-09-04 Phase-3 activation and is not scoped to any phase**; activation made the ladder SIZE the call, it did not make the mechanical count authoritative over the session's own reading — and the mechanical count may only BLOCK or DEMOTE a conversion whose rationale overstates its evidence — it may NEVER upgrade a KEEP into a conversion, nor a one-axis call into a two-axis one. That direction is deliberate and measured: mechanical scoring finds MORE two-axis days than the AI hand-counted, and unratcheted it would have turned the landed cardinality rule's correct $0 KEEP on 2026-09-01 into a full conversion.

**HEARTBEAT (every D1 firing, regardless of outcome — the `meta_monitoring_heartbeat` dead-man's-switch marker, `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`):** `INSERT INTO ops.heartbeat (source, note) VALUES ('loop:park_allocator', '<vehicle> call, status=<status>')`.

**CONNECTORS-DOWN / EVIDENCE UNGATHERABLE:** no call binds — log `status='HOLD'` and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','D1','park_router', 'evidence ungatherable — park allocation HOLD', '<JSON>')` (`park_router` category, auto-resolvable next clean run).
