On ANY error — `git fetch` fails, `gh` absent or unauthenticated, a BigQuery read/UPDATE/INSERT in (c)/(e)/(f) errors — abort THIS step, note it in the run `<note>`, and continue. The non-gating rule covers this step's SQL calls exactly as it covers its git calls.**

(a) DETECT — pure git, no `gh` required. **HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK — run this FIRST, before any ancestry test in this step and before (f)'s history-window test (shallow-clone hardening 2026-08-04, closing `ops0_landing_sweep_defect`).** The routine container clones SHALLOW by default, and on a shallow clone the git checks below do not error — they return CONFIDENTLY WRONG answers that are indistinguishable from a real strand: MEASURED 2026-08-03, the clone was truncated at boundary `f5bbade` with 65 commits reachable from `origin/main` (972 after `--unshallow`), and in that state `git merge-base --is-ancestor` returned FALSE for `dcf92b5` / `9c52cfab` / `7beef36` — all three genuinely ON `main` — while `git log origin/main --since=...` returned nothing for windows that did contain commits. **RUN THE SHARED HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK — §Execution environment, "GIT HISTORY IS TRUNCATED IN THE ROUTINE CONTAINER".** The canonical three-step ASK / DEEPEN / RE-ASK procedure, the reason those three must not be collapsed into a single "try to deepen, bail on any error" test, and the reading of `fatal: --unshallow on a complete repository does not make sense` (proof the clone is COMPLETE, never evidence it is undeepenable) all live there and are deliberately NOT restated here — hoisted fleet-wide 2026-09-08 so the procedure has exactly one home and cannot drift between two copies. That hoist also put a best-effort `git fetch --unshallow` in the SessionStart hook, so on most fires this precheck's step 1 already prints `false` and STEP 4 proceeds with no fetch at all; it is a fast path, not a reason to skip the ask. This paragraph keeps only what is specific to STEP 4. Treat the clone as **UNDEEPENABLE** only when that precheck's step 3 still prints `true`, or when its step 2 failed for a reason that genuinely left the history truncated (network failure, GitHub rate-limiting the deepen). This distinction matters because the skip path below is deliberately SILENT — misclassifying a healthy full clone as undeepenable would disable the entire landing sweep indefinitely with nothing to alert on, which is a worse failure than the one this precheck fixes. **DEEPENED-OK** — the tests below carry evidentiary weight; proceed. **UNDEEPENABLE** — treat every non-ancestor verdict below and every "no commit found" in (f) as **INCONCLUSIVE, never as evidence of a strand**: this run's DETECT yields ZERO candidate stranded branches (so (c) and (d) have nothing to act on), (e)'s ancestry test is skipped so no `stranded_branch` alert is resolved or re-raised on truncated evidence, (f) is skipped outright, and the run `<note>` must say `git history could not be deepened this run — (c)/(d)/(e)/(f) skipped, no strand/unlanded conclusions drawn`. This precheck exists because (a)'s verdict is what makes a branch eligible for (d)'s AUTONOMOUS ADOPT path: on a shallow clone an ALREADY-MERGED (or deliberately reverted) `claude/*` branch reads as stranded, and (d) would merge it back onto OPS0's own branch with no human in the loop. It did not bite on 2026-08-03 only because `origin` happened to carry zero `claude/*` refs. Prior record: `events.decision_log` entry `0e9a757e` (OPS0 2026-07-29) recommended exactly this fix after two false positives (D1 2026-07-22, D1 2026-07-25); routing it to a self-improvement audit did not land it, and OPS0 cannot self-correct it because plan prose is outside OPS0's `writes:` list. THEN: `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' --prune`, then for every `refs/remotes/origin/claude/*` ref that is NOT an ancestor of `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <ref> origin/main`), take the tip committer age; a healthy branch drains within ~30s of green CI, so treat age > 6h as stranded (same threshold as the CI-side check). EXCLUDE this session's own branch. (Deliberately scoped to `claude/*`, the routine fleet's own branches — narrower than `stranded-branch-check.yml`, which sweeps every prefix; a stranded `jack/*` branch is the operator's own work and not this routine's business.) **Outside (d)'s tightly-gated ADOPT path and the HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK's `--unshallow` fetch above, this step performs NO other git operation: it never checks out, rebases, cherry-picks, or resets, and it must leave the worktree exactly as it found it.**

(b) DIAGNOSE — best-effort enrichment only. If the `gh` CLI is available and authenticated (**NOT confirmed present in the routine container** — every other `gh` use in this repo lives in `.github/workflows/*.yml`; test it once, and on any failure record cause `unknown` and continue to (c), never halt): CI conclusion for the exact tip SHA (`gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=<sha>&per_page=1" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].conclusion'`) and whether an open PR titled exactly `Auto-merge conflict: <branch>` exists whose head SHA equals that same tip SHA. A missing diagnosis degrades the alert's detail, never its delivery.

(c) ALERT — for every stranded branch: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','OPS0','stranded_branch','<branch> unmerged','<JSON: branch, tip_sha, age_h, cause, ci_conclusion, pr_url>')`. Use the `_once` dedup variant and keep BOTH the age AND the diagnosed cause OUT of the message — payload only. `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on the exact `(category, message)` text (`bigquery/10_observability.sql`), so ANY field that can vary between runs defeats the dedup and lets undeduped rows accumulate — the documented failure mode behind `bigquery/111`'s comments. `<cause>` is exactly such a field: it flips between `unknown` and a real diagnosis as `gh` availability varies run to run, so embedding it would produce a fresh alert on every flip. Keep the message a stable `<branch> unmerged` so a branch stranded for a week produces one alert, not seven — matching the `owner_confirmation_stale` / `book_drawdown_soft_breach` precedent. **Severity stays `warning` and NEVER escalates to `critical`, however old the branch gets.** `stranded_branch` is not in the blocking-criticals exclusion list of the live gate views (`bigquery/107_halt_echo_missed_run_gate.sql`, which excludes only `trading_halted` / `staleness` plus the halt-echo cases), so a `critical` here would flip `state.trading_enabled` FALSE and halt the whole book over a git-plumbing delay — a wildly disproportionate blast radius for unlanded prose. If a future revision wants the 24h escalation, it must FIRST add `stranded_branch` to that exclusion list. Skip the alert entirely when CI is green, no conflict PR exists, and age is under 12h — that is an ordinary drain window, not a strand; it re-evaluates tomorrow.

(d) ADOPT — rescue a stranded branch by merging it onto OPS0's OWN branch, so its work reaches `main` with no human. **Enabled 2026-07-29**, replacing this step's earlier detect-and-alert-only posture, once the preconditions it recorded were satisfied. The gate is NOT the remote CI verdict — that needs `gh` (unconfirmed in the routine container) and never tested the merged content anyway, since CI only ever saw each side pre-merge. The gate is: **the merged, resolved tree passes the project's own checks locally**, which is strictly more evidence than a green tick on the pre-merge branch. **ADOPT ONLY IF ALL SIX HOLD, checked in order; on ANY failure take the ABORT PATH and fall through to (c)'s alert.**

1. **CLEAN WORKTREE.** `git status --porcelain` must be empty before anything is touched, and record `START_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` for the abort path. STEP 2's self-registration and STEP 3's `cron_utc` bootstrap both commit inline so this normally holds; if it does not, do NOT merge — an entangled tree is how a rescue becomes a second incident.
2. **NO HARD-EXCLUDED PATH.** Compute `git diff --name-only origin/main...origin/<branch>` BEFORE merging; abort if ANY path matches ANY of: (i) `strategy/0N_strategy_*.md`, `strategy_math/**`, `c_options_math.py`, `strategy/roster.yaml` — resolving a spec-locked surface invalidates `spec_hash` and fails `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py`; (ii) **`bigquery/**`** (recursive — it MUST also cover `bigquery/scheduled_queries/*.sql`, which `ci.yml`'s own SQL dry-run step treats as a separate glob; apply-in-order + superseded-marker semantics, plus the five files carrying `scripts/gen_routine_lists.py`'s generated regions, make a hand-merged SQL file actively dangerous) and **`dbt/**`**; (iii) **`.github/**`** — a branch editing `auto-merge-claude.yml`'s inline drain/gate logic or `ci.yml`'s job definitions would pass precondition 5 completely, because that suite runs the underlying scripts DIRECTLY and never exercises the workflow YAML wrapping them, so a weakened merge gate would land unreviewed and degrade every FUTURE landing; (iv) **`.claude/**`** — `scripts/check_settings_toolcov.py` is by its own docstring a ONE-DIRECTION guard (it fails only on a *referenced-but-missing* tool, never on an *added* or widened permission), so a broadened `permissions.allow` would sail through and take effect for every later unattended session; (v) **`scripts/**` and `tests/**`** — these ARE precondition 5's verification machinery, and a branch that weakens a checker would then be validated by the very code it weakened. What remains adoptable is essentially the routine-output surface this step exists to rescue: cadence and research `.md` files and non-spec `ops/*.yaml`. Residual, accepted: `ops/cadence.yaml`'s `depends_on` is only typo-checked, not semantically validated, so a cadence-only edit could still remove a real dependency undetected. Those last two exclusions are what make this step sound, and the argument was verified against `ci.yml` on 2026-07-29 rather than assumed. Three blocking CHECKS cannot be reproduced in the routine container (no WIF identity, and `dbt` is not installed). Two of them are now STEPS inside the single `warehouse-validation` job rather than the separate `sql-validate` / `dbt-parity` jobs they used to be (consolidated 2026-07-30 — billing is per job, so merging them saved a job floor per run; the SQL dry-run steps stay unconditionally blocking and the dbt steps stay advisory-unless-`DBT_PARITY=block`, and each half runs on `always()` so neither can suppress the other): the SQL dry-run step runs only over CHANGED `bigquery/*.sql` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, "Dry-run changed bigquery/*.sql"); the dbt-parity steps are path-gated and emit `dbt parity skipped — no bigquery/** or dbt/** changes in this push`; and `dbt parse` always runs (in the `checks` job) but reads only `dbt/`. Excluding exactly `bigquery/*.sql` and `dbt/**` therefore makes an adoptable branch one that all three would pass trivially or skip — so the locally-runnable subset is the COMPLETE set of gates that would actually gate it, not a weaker proxy. **Never narrow these exclusions without redoing that argument against the current `ci.yml`.**
3. **THE MERGE RESOLVES UNAMBIGUOUSLY.** `git merge --no-ff origin/<branch> -m "OPS0: adopt stranded branch <branch>"`. For a conflict in a GENERATED file — `task_plan/*.md` (from `Claude_Task_Plan.md`) or `strategy/*.md` (from `Strategy.md`) — never hand-merge the generated file: resolve the MASTER, re-run `scripts/split_task_plan.py` / `scripts/split_strategy.py`, and take the regenerated output. Resolve a non-generated conflict only where both sides' intent is unambiguous from the diff; if it is not, abort.
   **REGENERATE ON A CLEAN MERGE TOO, NOT ONLY ON A CONFLICT (corrected 2026-08-19, OPS2 — this omission made ADOPT unable to rescue the single most likely strand class).** The paragraph above fires only when git reports a CONFLICT, but the commonest reason a branch is stranded in the first place is that its author edited a MASTER file and never regenerated its slices — in which case the merge is perfectly CLEAN (the stale slices are simply unchanged on both sides, so there is nothing to conflict), no regeneration is triggered, and precondition 5's `split_task_plan.py --check` / `split_strategy.py --check` then FAILS on inherited staleness that the adopting session did not cause and, under the letter of this step, must abort over. ADOPT would therefore refuse precisely the branches it exists to rescue, and would do so silently — falling through to (c)'s alert as though the content were unsafe, when it is sound and one mechanical command from green. **So: after ANY successful merge here — conflicted or not — if `git diff --name-only "$START_SHA" HEAD` touched `Claude_Task_Plan.md` or `Strategy.md`, run the corresponding `split_*.py` and stage its output BEFORE evaluating precondition 5.** A `--check` failure that SURVIVES that regeneration is a real abort; one that the regeneration clears was never a defect in the merged content at all. This is a strict widening of an existing sanctioned repair (the same command, on the same generated files, for the same reason) — it grants ADOPT no new authority over any hand-edited file. **Worked precedent: `claude/d1-2026-08-19` (tip `d619877`), stranded ~5h45m on all-33-slices-stale, merged clean, adopted by OPS2 on exactly this path once the regeneration was run.**
4. **NO CONFLICT RESIDUE.** `git diff --check` must be clean, AND a conflict-marker scan must come back empty. **Scope that scan to the files this merge actually touched and anchor it to line-start** — `git diff --name-only "$START_SHA" HEAD | xargs -r grep -l -E '^(<{7}|={7}|>{7})'` — never a repo-wide grep for the bare marker strings: THIS PARAGRAPH contains those strings, as does its generated mirror in `task_plan/OPS0.md`, so an unscoped repo-wide grep matches the plan's own text on every run, can never pass, and would silently disable ADOPT entirely. Any hit aborts.
5. **THE LOCAL CHECK SUITE PASSES ON THE RESOLUTION.** Run `ci.yml`'s `checks`-job steps (the four jobs `test`/`lint`/`shell-lint`/`dbt` were CONSOLIDATED into one `checks` job on 2026-07-30 to stop paying four rounded-up billable minutes for 136s of work — the step list below is unchanged by that, only its job label) (`python c_options_math.py`; `python -m pytest`; `split_strategy.py --check`; `split_task_plan.py --check`; `check_cadence_consistency.py`; `check_prose_invariants.py`; `python3 scripts/check_routine_scope.py`; `check_cadence_marker.py`; `gen_routine_lists.py --check`; `routine_backup.py check`; `check_cron_dst_safety.py`; `check_roster_consistency.py`; `check_autonomy_consistency.py`; `check_handoff_contracts.py`; `check_script_version_consistency.py`; `check_sq_version_registry.py`; `check_superseded_markers.py`; `check_superseded_by_discipline.py`; `check_alert_message_stability.py`; `check_roster_notice_lockstep.py`; `check_settings_toolcov.py`; `check_connector_tools.py`; `check_dbt_view_coverage.py`; `tests/test_auto_merge_logic.sh`; `tests/test_resolve_diff_base.sh`; `tests/test_notify_webhook.sh`; `tests/test_ci_finding.sh`; `tests/test_bq_csv.sh`; `tests/test_restore_drill.sh`; `tests/test_session_start_hook.sh`; `node ops/weekly_report/test_pure_helpers.js`) plus all three former-`shell-lint` steps (now inside `checks`) when their binaries exist: `actionlint`, `shellcheck -S warning`, and the pure grep/sed check that `ci.yml`'s and `golden-scenarios.yml`'s `name:` fields still match `auto-merge-claude.yml`'s `workflow_run` trigger list (that third one needs no binary at all and guards a rename that would silently stop auto-merge re-triggering). A missing linter binary is NOT a pass — note it in the payload and continue; a FAILING check is an abort. **This step list is hand-kept against `ci.yml`; `scripts/check_adopt_gate_coverage.py` (added 2026-08-20, `ci.yml`'s own `checks` job) is a BLOCKING CI step that parses `ci.yml`'s `checks`-job steps and fails the build if any blocking step's script/test target is missing from this paragraph — the drift class that let this list fall seven scripts behind (`ops0_adopt_gate_drift`, verified 2026-08-20: `check_cadence_marker.py`, `routine_backup.py`, `check_cron_dst_safety.py`, `check_sq_version_registry.py`, `check_superseded_by_discipline.py`, `check_connector_tools.py`, `check_handoff_contracts.py` — the last of those seven landed via an unrelated OPS0 commit mid-fix, and the checker below caught it on the very next run, before this fix even shipped) can no longer land silently. Still re-read `ci.yml`'s blocking jobs when running this by hand — the checker guards the list from staying stale, not from a single run misreading it — and treat any step you find there but not here as also required.** This is the step that catches the real stranding class on record: the 2026-07-27 `claude/runbook-47-gaps` branch was red on `check_superseded_markers.py`, a zero-credential check.
6. **PUSH IMMEDIATELY once 1–5 pass** — do not hold the adoption to session end. A container death between a passing suite and the push discards the whole rescue on the next SessionStart hard-reset (the stranded branch is left untouched, so no harm — but the work is wasted). This is the checkpoint-push rule at its highest-value case.

**ONE ADOPTION PER RUN.** If (a) found several stranded branches, attempt ADOPT on exactly ONE — the OLDEST by tip-committer date — and leave the rest to (c)'s alert; they become eligible on the next daily sweep. Do NOT loop: `START_SHA` is captured once, so a second attempt's abort would `reset --hard` the branch back PAST the first adoption's already-pushed merge commit, leaving the local branch behind its own remote and turning every later push in the session into a rejected non-fast-forward.

**ABORT PATH (any failure above):** `git merge --abort || true`, then `git reset --hard $START_SHA`, then `git clean -fd` (NOT `-x` — do not destroy legitimate ignored artifacts) to remove any untracked file the mid-merge regeneration in precondition 3 may have created, then confirm `git status --porcelain` is empty. **That confirmation is load-bearing, not decorative: if it is NOT empty, make NO further commit or push this session and raise `ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','OPS0','stranded_branch','adoption abort left a dirty worktree — OPS0 made no commit this session', ...)`** — OPS0's session-end "commit all changes" would otherwise sweep the residue of a supposedly-reverted adoption into a real commit that lands on `main`. The no-commit rule is the actual protection here; the alert only reports it. Keep the severity at `warning` even though this is serious — per (c), `stranded_branch` is not in `bigquery/107`'s blocking-criticals exclusion list, and halting the entire book over OPS0's dirty worktree would be wildly disproportionate. Leave the stranded branch and its conflict PR untouched for the human path, and put the abort reason in (c)'s alert payload. A session killed mid-merge needs no cleanup: `.claude/session-start.sh`'s `git reset --hard origin/main` clears `MERGE_HEAD` and all residue on the next run.

**AFTER A SUCCESSFUL ADOPTION:** `INSERT INTO ops.routine_commit_markers (routine, run_date, git_commit, commit_subject, source)` a row for the ORIGINAL routine and run_date the adopted branch carried, `source='OPS0-adoption'` — `auto-merge-claude.yml` writes a marker only for a branch it merges DIRECTLY, so an adopted branch would otherwise land with no marker and re-trip (f) forever. Then one `events.decision_log` entry (`entry_type='stranded-branch-adoption'`, source `OPS0`) naming the branch, the conflicted paths, the resolution taken and the checks run, plus `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','OPS0','stranded_branch_adopted','<branch> adopted onto OPS0 branch — no action needed','<JSON: branch, tip_sha, files, resolution, checks_run, checks_skipped>')`. Record `checks_skipped` honestly: `warehouse-validation`'s SQL dry-run and dbt-parity steps were not run, and omitting them is sound ONLY because precondition 2 excluded their trigger paths.

(e) SELF-RESOLVE — `stranded_branch` is absent from `ops.alert_policy` and therefore latching by construction, so OPS0 owns its clear, per the sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve (same pattern as D2a's `owner_confirmation_stale` / `book_drawdown_soft_breach`). **Distinguish the two exit paths — they are not the same event and must not share a note.** **Gated by (a)'s HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK: if the clone was shallow and could not be deepened this run, skip this sub-step entirely — leave any open `stranded_branch` alert exactly as it is and re-evaluate next sweep. A truncated history can make a branch that genuinely landed read as a non-ancestor, which here would mean declaring a landed branch `deleted_without_landing`.** If the branch is now an ancestor of `origin/main`, it genuinely landed: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='branch landed on main — verified ancestor by OPS0 git landing sweep' WHERE category='stranded_branch' AND NOT resolved AND JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.branch') = '<branch>'`. If instead the branch has VANISHED from `origin` without ever becoming an ancestor of `main`, that is a possible loss of routine output, not a success — do **NOT** auto-resolve it; leave the alert open and re-raise once at `'warning'` with cause `deleted_without_landing` so it stays visible until a human confirms nothing was lost.

(f) NEVER-PUSHED / UNLANDED COMPLETED RUNS — **SHADOW ONLY: write the finding, raise NO alert.** `ops.routine_commit_markers` (bigquery/38) detects one direction only — commit landed on `main`, `run_log` missing its `'completed'` row. The REVERSE — `run_log` says `'completed'` but nothing reached `main` — is the 2026-06-22/06-24 D1 stranding signature (RUNBOOK §20). A detector for it WAS specified — `Operating_Protocols.md` §17, "D2 Step-0 Stranded-Session Reconciliation (Never-Pushed-Branch Detector)", raising `never_pushed_branch` — but verification on 2026-07-29 found it **orphaned: it was never inlined into `Claude_Task_Plan.md` or any `task_plan/` slice** (its 2026-06-23 commit touched only `Operating_Protocols.md` + `ops/RUNBOOK.md`), no routine references §17, and RUNBOOK §20's claim that "the D2 Step-0 detector (§17) fired correctly" reflects a session self-executing freshly-written prose, not a wired step. Note also that W5 used to CONSUME an open `never_pushed_branch` alert (that consumer is now removed, per the 2026-07-29 resolution below) while nothing anywhere ever produced one, and that §17's literal test ("absent from `git ls-remote` ⇒ stranded") would false-positive on every normally-merged branch, since auto-merge deletes the branch after landing. **§17 is now retired** (bolded RETIRED tag in place, spec kept as history only) and W5's dead consumer removed. **Do NOT resurrect `never_pushed_branch`** — that name is retired with §17 and must not be produced by any routine again.

**DETECT ON GIT EVIDENCE, NOT ON MARKERS — live (no longer shadow) as of 2026-07-29.** `ops.routine_commit_markers` is NOT a usable universal signal and must not be the primary test: verification on 2026-07-29 found it has only EVER received rows for three routines (D1, D2, W5) out of the whole fleet. The cause is not WIF (the `GCP_WIF_PROVIDER` / `GCP_WIF_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` repo **variables** are set and the writer is working) — it is that `auto-merge-claude.yml`'s marker step parses the branch tip's commit SUBJECT and requires both a leading routine token AND a full `YYYY-MM-DD`. `D1 Market Development Scan 2026-07-28` matches; `A1 2026: annual foundation re-derivation` does not, so A1/A2/A3 land real commits and get no marker. (**That parser was FIXED on 2026-07-29**: the field extraction moved into `scripts/auto_merge_decision.sh` as `marker_routine_from_subject` / `marker_run_date_from_subject` — pure functions the workflow sources and `tests/test_auto_merge_logic.sh` covers directly — and `run_date` now falls back to the commit's author date rendered in the OPERATING timezone (`TZ=America/Denver git log -1 --date=short-local --format=%ad`) when the subject carries no full ISO date, so a year-only subject is marked correctly. A subject-embedded ISO date still wins, so D1/D2/W5 behaviour is unchanged. **That fallback originally used `--format=%as` and was corrected 2026-08-04:** `%as` renders the commit's OWN recorded offset, and routine containers commit in UTC, so any routine committing after ~18:00 MT was marked with TOMORROW's date — reintroducing exactly the midnight-UTC misattribution the fallback exists to prevent. It produced a phantom `SL2 / 2026-08-04 / completed` row in `ops.run_log` (via the §38 marker self-heal) for a run that never happened, which in turn made SL2 read `days_silent = 0` in `state.queue_driven_silence_watch` — blinding the detector added the day before to catch SL2 going quiet. Markers should therefore become fleet-wide from the next merges onward; until that is OBSERVED across a full cadence cycle, still treat a present marker as corroboration and an absent one as weak evidence — which is why the primary test below remains git evidence, not markers. **THAT OBSERVATION IS NOW IN (measured 2026-08-20, OPS2) — the "only D1/D2/W5" figure is STALE and must not be re-quoted:** `ops.routine_commit_markers` holds rows for **21 distinct routines** spanning every tier — daily (D1, D2, D2a, D3, OPS0, OPS1, OPS2, SL3), weekly (W1–W5), monthly (M1b, M2, M3, M4) and queue-driven (AR_att, AR_orc, SL2, SL5) — with the newest at `run_date = 2026-08-20`. The parser fix works. So the trailing claim this parenthetical used to carry — that `ops.sp_backfill_run_log_from_markers` (RUNBOOK §38 layer A) "has only ever been able to self-heal those same three routines" — is now FALSE, and demonstrably so: on 2026-08-20 it healed a landed-but-unlogged **SL3** row off its `auto-merge-claude.yml` marker (see OPS2 STEP 0). **What does NOT change is the posture of the test below.** Markers being fleet-wide makes an absent marker *less* likely to be a parser artifact, but a marker is still written only after CI's marker step runs, so a genuine landing can briefly precede its marker — absence stays weak evidence and git evidence stays the primary test here. Only the reach of the §38 self-heal was ever gated on this, and that gate is now open fleet-wide. The remaining tiers with no marker yet (A1/A2/A3, M1a, M5, Q1–Q4, SL1, SL4) are routines that simply have not merged a commit since the fix, not routines the parser still misses.)

So use the repo's existing git-evidence idiom instead (the same technique the dependency gate's fallback and D3's golden-scenario check already use). **This history-window read is gated by (a)'s HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK — if that precheck found the clone shallow and undeepenable this run, skip (f) entirely (already recorded in (a)'s `<note>`); do not run the check below and do not draw an unlanded conclusion from it. Both false `unlanded_completed_run` positives on record (D1 2026-07-22, D1 2026-07-25) and the 2026-08-03 recurrence came from exactly this test reading a truncated history.** For each `'completed'` `ops.run_log` row in the last 7 days:

**MARKER PRE-CHECK FIRST — a marker's PRESENCE is conclusive; its ABSENCE stays weak (added 2026-08-20, OPS0).** `SELECT git_commit, commit_subject FROM ops.routine_commit_markers WHERE routine = <routine> AND run_date = <run_date>`. If a row exists, the run's work LANDED: `auto-merge-claude.yml` writes a marker only for a branch it actually merged into `main`. Record `marker_present=TRUE`, EXCLUDE the run, and do NOT run the pathspec test on it at all. **This is not a reversal of the "markers are not the primary test" posture two paragraphs above** — that posture is about marker ABSENCE, which stays weak evidence (a genuine landing can briefly precede its marker) and still routes to the git test below exactly as before. Only the positive direction is used here, and only to SUPPRESS a false alarm, never to raise one. **It cannot mask a real strand, and the reason is structural: a genuinely stranded run is one auto-merge never merged, so it has no marker by construction** — the pathspec test still runs on precisely the population that matters. The residual case (a run that landed one branch, earning a marker, while a second branch of the same run stranded) is already covered by (a), which sees that unmerged `claude/*` ref directly. MEASURED 2026-08-20: this pre-check is what correctly suppresses all three false positives on record of the class below — D1/2026-08-17 (`2dd38be`), D2/2026-07-19 (`6eecc61`), OPS1/2026-08-20 (`7fa97fc`) — each of which carries an `auto-merge-claude.yml` marker row. **SUBJECT PRE-CHECK — the SAME asymmetry, for the routines whose declared paths cannot decide it (added 2026-08-31, closing OPS0's own `ops0_landing_sweep_defect` for SL5).** After the marker pre-check and before the pathspec test, also run `git log origin/main --format='%H %s'` over this run's window and look for a commit whose SUBJECT names BOTH the routine id and the `run_date` — the fleet's landing convention, `<ROUTINE> <YYYY-MM-DD>: <what changed>`. **A match is conclusive and EXCLUDES the run; a miss proves nothing and falls through to the pathspec test unchanged.** **WHY IT IS NEEDED — the pathspec test is not merely weak for SL5, it is unsound in BOTH readings, and OPS0 measured this on itself.** SL5's declared `writes:` are `strategy/roster.yaml`, `Strategy.md`, `strategy/*.md`, `Claude_Task_Plan.md` plus BigQuery objects, and only `strategy/roster.yaml` is routine-EXCLUSIVE — which a no-op roster cycle legitimately never touches. So the exclusive-path reading raises a FALSE `unlanded_completed_run`, while the full-declared-list reading passes only by matching FOREIGN commits on the shared globs (SL5/2026-08-30 would have been 'confirmed landed' by `a3489af` (SL2) and `5ccb32b` (W4) touching `strategy/*.md` and `Strategy.md`) — a vacuous pass that would equally have 'confirmed' a run that never landed at all. SL5/2026-08-30 carried no marker and no catch-up-replay subject, yet demonstrably landed as `1b7d6c5` — subject `SL5 2026-08-30: correct two measured SL5 claims that had drifted to false`, exactly the shape this check reads. **THIS IS NOT THE `title`-REGEX DEFECT AR_orc's STEP 4 PROVENANCE CONTRACT FORBIDS, and the difference is the direction of failure.** That contract bans matching free-text prose because there a failed match drives a fail-CLOSED branch — a `critical` `review_handoff_stuck` and `state.trading_enabled = FALSE` raised over a verdict that had in fact executed. Here a failed match only declines to suppress, leaving this step exactly as it behaves today, so the worst case of a wording drift is the status quo rather than a false halt. Positive evidence read positively is safe; the same string read as a REQUIREMENT is not. **DO NOT close this instead by adding a shared path to SL5's `writes:` list** — per this step's own measurement rule any added path must be routine-EXCLUSIVE and measured over fifteen 2-day windows first, and `Strategy.md` / `strategy/*.md` / `Claude_Task_Plan.md` are exactly the shared globs that produced the vacuous pass. The same unsoundness applies to any routine whose only exclusive path is conditionally written; SL5 is simply where it was measured first.

**CATCH-UP-REPLAY COMMIT-SUBJECT CHECK — SECOND POSITIVE-EVIDENCE PATH (added 2026-08-25, closes `ops0_landing_sweep_defect` alert `7d58e7ef`).** An INTERACTIVE catch-up-replay session commits under the OPERATOR's own git identity, not `noreply@anthropic.com`, so `auto_merge_decision.sh`'s `marker_author_is_routine` guard correctly WITHHOLDS a marker for it — the same guard that prevents a W5-class phantom completion. The MARKER PRE-CHECK above will therefore never find a row for these runs BY CONSTRUCTION, not by gap. And because a catch-up replay records its findings to whatever narrative file fits the work rather than to the replayed routine's own `writes:` paths, the pathspec test below ALSO returns nothing for a run that demonstrably landed: MEASURED 2026-08-24, OPS0's own `90b4921` and D3's own `7f3b1d1` each touch ONLY `Daily.md`, matching neither `ops/cadence.yaml`/`ops/trigger_ids.json` (OPS0) nor `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`/`bigquery/*.sql`/`tests/golden_scenarios/scenarios.yaml` (D3). D3/2026-08-23 nonetheless "passed" only by coincidence, matching an unrelated commit (`56989bf`) whose `bigquery/196`/`197` files happen to hit the `bigquery/*.sql` glob in the same window. **Do NOT close this by adding `Daily.md` to any routine's `writes:` list** — `Daily.md` is D1's own declared path and is legitimately touched by every routine's halt-record and catch-up-replay commits (33% of its last 45 days of commits are non-D1), so adding it elsewhere would make (f) exactly as vacuous for OPS0/D3 as `task_plan/SL2.md` was measured to be for SL2 on 2026-08-20. **Do NOT close it by having `auto-merge-claude.yml` write a marker for these commits either** (the remedy OPS0's own alert proposed): that requires weakening `marker_author_is_routine`'s `@anthropic.com` requirement, so ANY operator-authored commit whose subject merely resembled the convention would earn an unverified landing marker — editing the verifier's own input surface until it agrees. INSTEAD, before falling through to the pathspec test, run `git log origin/main --oneline -i --grep='^<routine> catch-up replay <run_date>:'`. A match is conclusive landing evidence for exactly that `(routine, run_date)` pair, on the same structural reasoning as the MARKER PRE-CHECK: a run that never replayed has no such commit, so this can only SUPPRESS a false alarm, never mask a real strand. MEASURED 2026-08-24, all eight catch-up-replay commits to date (AR_att, AR_orc, D2, D2a, D3, OPS0, OPS2, SL3) follow `<ROUTINE> catch-up replay <YYYY-MM-DD>: <summary>` with zero deviation, and any future interactive catch-up-replay commit MUST use that exact subject shape. On NO match, fall through unchanged — a future drift in the convention degrades silently back to today's safe-if-noisy behaviour, never to a new silent miss.

Only when NO marker exists: take that routine's repo-file outputs from its `writes:` list in `ops/cadence.yaml` (the entries that are file paths, not `dataset.table` names) and check `git log origin/main --oneline --since=<run_date 00:00 America/Denver> --until=<run_date + 2 days> -- <those paths>` (this window is already gated by (a)'s HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK — on an UNDEEPENABLE clone (f) is skipped outright and no unlanded conclusion is drawn). A commit is evidence the work landed; none is the stranding signature. **Use only the routine-EXCLUSIVE entries as evidence and ignore any fleet-shared path in the list** (`Claude_Task_Plan.md` is the live instance — SL5 declares it, and it is touched by 220 of the last 695 commits, ~31.6%, so treating it as evidence would make (f) a coin-flip for SL5). A shared path is still legitimately DESCRIBED in `writes:`; it is simply not evidence here. **EXCLUDE from the check** (absence of a commit is expected, not a strand): any run whose own `<note>` records that it made no repo changes, and every routine whose `writes:` list contains no repo-file path at all — today D2a, OPS2, AR_att, AR_orc, SL1, SL3, SL4, M1a, M1R and M5. (OPS1 was on this list until its 2026-08-12 AUTO-ADD capability gave it a conditional repo-file entry in `ops/cadence.yaml`'s `writes:` — it is now checked like OPS0's own conditional entries, i.e. covered by the note-based exclusion earlier in this sentence on an ordinary no-drift day, and actually checked for a landed commit on an `added`-drift day.) AR_att / AR_orc persist completed review transcripts in BigQuery only, so their completed run is never evidence of a stranded repository output. If a routine's `writes:` list and its actual behaviour disagree, fix `ops/cadence.yaml` rather than special-casing here — but **any path added for that purpose must be EXCLUSIVE to the routine, and its exclusivity must be MEASURED before it is added, never inferred from the filename (2026-08-20, OPS0).** These entries are consumed as git pathspecs matched against ANY commit in the window by ANY author, so a path other routines also touch does not merely dilute the signal: it makes (f) VACUOUS for that routine, trading a noisy false POSITIVE for silent blindness — strictly the worse failure, and the one with no alert to reveal it. The measurement to run is: over the last fifteen 2-day windows, count those in which the candidate path matches a commit that is NOT the routine's own. **A DECLARED EXCLUSIVE PATH CAN ALSO BE NEVER-CORROBORATING, WHICH IS A THIRD FAILURE THIS TEST HAD NO NAME FOR (recorded 2026-09-08 from OPS0's own 2026-09-01 measurement, closing `ops0_landing_sweep_defect` `809ad3c1`).** Exclusivity asks "do OTHER routines touch this path?"; it does not ask "does THIS routine ever touch it?", and a path that the owning routine never writes cannot produce positive evidence no matter how exclusive it is. Two live instances, both measured by OPS0 over the same fifteen 2-day windows (2026-08-02..2026-09-01, `America/Denver`, `origin/main`): **`ops/trigger_ids.json`** (declared by OPS0) took **ZERO commits by ANY author in the 90-day span**, so it can never corroborate OPS0 — OPS0's evidence rests entirely on `ops/cadence.yaml` (10/15 matched, 5/15 masking, 6 own of 25), which remains usable; and **`AI_Trading_Foundation.md`** (declared by D3) matched 2/15 windows with **0 D3 commits**, so all of its matches were foreign — the masking shape, not the corroborating one. With `bigquery/*.sql` (12/15 masking) and `tests/golden_scenarios/scenarios.yaml` (3/15 masking) also unusable, **D3 has no sound exclusive path at all and is the SL5 case exactly**: do NOT run the pathspec test on D3, and rely on the MARKER and SUBJECT pre-checks above, which already cover it (D3 lands under the fleet convention — `D3 2026-09-06: correct D3's stale golden-scenario SCALE counts`, `D3 2026-09-08: the unwired-monitor bridge must not fire on an apply-lag`). **Do NOT close this by adding a shared path to D3's `writes:` list** — that is the vacuous pass this step forbids, the same trap declined for SL5. **SL2 IS THE SAME CASE AND THIS PARAGRAPH OMITTED IT (added 2026-09-13, D3, closing `ops0_landing_sweep_defect` alert `691c65af`; OPS0 raised it on 2026-09-09 and could not self-correct, because `Claude_Task_Plan.md` is outside OPS0's own `writes:` list).** SL2 declares exactly two repo-file paths — `Strategy.md` and `strategy/*.md` — and this step already names BOTH as fleet-shared and non-exclusive in the SL5 passage above, so SL2 likewise has ZERO routine-exclusive repo path: **do NOT run the pathspec test on SL2 either.** Verified this run against `ops/cadence.yaml` directly (not from the alert prose, per the report-not-an-instruction rule), and both paths carry heavy foreign traffic on `origin/main` — W4's `5ccb32b`, the Rev 44 / 46+47 / 48 landings and the CaR-retirement commit `cae86cf` all touch them without being SL2. SL2 differs from D3 only in WHICH unsoundness applies — D3's declared paths are never-corroborating, SL2's are masking — and the remedy is identical, so the exclusive-path reading leaves SL2 an EMPTY pathspec that can only ever raise a FALSE `unlanded_completed_run`, while the full-list reading passes vacuously on foreign commits. **Do NOT close this by adding a path to SL2's `writes:` list**: `Strategy.md` and `strategy/*.md` are precisely the forbidden shared globs, and `task_plan/SL2.md` was measured 77% masking and REMOVED on 2026-08-20 for blinding SL2's own detector. The MARKER and SUBJECT pre-checks already cover SL2 — OPS0's own 2026-09-02..09-09 sweep measurement reports all six SL2 pairs reconciled, four by marker and two by an affirmative no-repo-change note. Like D3's, the exposure is LATENT rather than live: OPS0 recorded the pathspec rung as unreached on all three of 2026-09-07, 09-08 and 09-09, so no false verdict has been produced. The exposure was measured LATENT rather than live: in the 2026-08-25..08-31 sweep all 64 completed runs were reconciled by the marker / subject / no-repo-writes / note-affirmed rungs, so zero pairs ever reached the pathspec test and no false verdict was produced. **When adding or auditing a path here, measure BOTH directions — foreign commits (masking) and own commits (corroboration) — because a path with zero of the latter is silently inert.** **`task_plan/<ID>.md` is NOT exclusive and must never be added on the assumption that it is** — every slice regenerates whenever the ROUTINE INVENTORY table in `Claude_Task_Plan.md` changes, so all 35 move together on most routine commits. MEASURED 2026-08-20: `task_plan/SL2.md` matched 13 of 15 windows, **10 of them containing no SL2 commit at all** (77% masking; 79 commits touch it in 45 days, 3 are SL2's — 96.2% foreign), and `task_plan/OPS1.md` matched 13 with 9 foreign (69%); `task_plan/D1.md` is 98.7% foreign and `task_plan/D2.md` 98.8%. Contrast `Daily.md`, a genuinely exclusive path: 13 matched windows, **zero** masking. The `task_plan/SL2.md` entry added on 2026-08-19 to fix a real SL2 false positive was therefore REMOVED on 2026-08-20 — it had blinded SL2's detector rather than repaired it — and the same addition was considered and DECLINED for OPS1, D1 and D2. The MARKER PRE-CHECK above is what actually covers that whole class, and covers it without costing any detection power.

On a genuine hit: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','OPS0','unlanded_completed_run','<routine> logged completed for <run_date> but no output reached main','<JSON: routine, run_date, checked_paths, marker_present>')` — `warning`, never `critical`, for the same blocking-criticals reason given in (c). Also write ONE `events.decision_log` entry (`entry_type='unlanded-completed-run'`, source `OPS0`) with the full list each run, so the record survives even when nothing alerts. SELF-RESOLVE on the same evidence-based pattern as (e): when a later sweep finds the expected commit did land after all (a late push, or an adoption via (d)), resolve the row with `resolved_note='output later found on main — verified by OPS0 git landing sweep'`.

STEP 5 — EXTERNAL-CALL TELEMETRY SWEEP (added 2026-08-21, external-spend audit; daily, every run). Two read-only checks over the metered-call telemetry the shared "Metered external calls" rule's part (d) obliges every routine to write immediately before `sp_routine_end`. **NON-GATING and best-effort, exactly like STEP 3 and STEP 4 and the shared NON-GATING + FALLBACK rule: this step must NEVER halt OPS0 and never change STEP 1/2/3/4's outcomes. On ANY error — a view missing, a read or `UPDATE` failing — abort THIS step, note it in the run `<note>`, and continue.** Both alerts below are `warning` and NEVER escalate to `critical`, for the same reason (c) gives: neither category appears in `bigquery/107_halt_echo_missed_run_gate.sql`'s blocking-criticals exclusion list, so a `critical` here would flip `state.trading_enabled` FALSE and halt the whole book over telemetry. **Neither check throttles, caps, gates or re-fires anything** — no routine is stopped, no call is refused, and no per-routine credit cap follows from either (the shared rule's standing prohibition on a cap from spend alone is unchanged).

(a) **COVERAGE — a completed run of a metered routine that logged NOTHING.** `SELECT * FROM state.web_call_coverage w WHERE w.expected_metered AND w.missing_telemetry AND w.run_date = (SELECT MAX(run_date) FROM state.web_call_coverage w2 WHERE w2.routine = w.routine)` (the view LEFT JOINs completed `ops.run_log` runs against the distinct `(routine, run_date)` pairs present in `ops.web_calls`; `expected_metered` is TRUE for the routines whose own prose names a metered surface). **TWO CORRECTIONS, 2026-08-25 — closes `ops0_telemetry_sweep_defect` (alerts `d33a7a8b` + `2014bbad`).** (i) The column is `missing_telemetry`; this step previously named a column (`missing_token`) the view has never had. Run literally that is `Unrecognized name`, and because THIS STEP IS NON-GATING the error aborts the step silently into the run `<note>` — the whole coverage check goes dark with nothing to alert on. A stale identifier in a non-gating step is invisible by construction, which is why it is worth pinning rather than trusting the executing model to silently correct it. (ii) The predicate is now SCOPED TO EACH ROUTINE'S MOST RECENT COMPLETED RUN. The view retains a `(routine, run_date)` row for every historical day inside its trailing-45-day window, so an unscoped read re-matches a routine that has since become compliant on nothing but old history it already recovered from — `sp_raise_alert_once` re-raises it and the resolve clause below clears it again in the same sweep. MEASURED 2026-08-25: OPS1 (alert `4c34d633`) was raised 04:40:53Z and resolved 04:41:01Z by the same sweep, 7 seconds apart, and still generated an operator email. The earliest gap cohorts do not age out of the 45-day window until early October, so unscoped this recurs once per sweep until then. For each such `(routine, run_date)`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','OPS0','web_call_coverage_gap','<routine> completed a run and logged no ops.web_calls rows','<JSON: routine, run_date, expected_metered, session_id>')`. Keep `run_date` and every other field that varies between runs OUT of the message and in the payload, per (c)'s dedup rule — `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on the exact `(category, message)` text, so a per-ROUTINE message yields one open alert per non-compliant routine instead of one per missed day. That distinction is load-bearing here rather than theoretical: MEASURED 2026-08-21, 7 of 219 completed August runs carry any `ops.web_calls` row (3.2%) and 25 of the 30 routines that ran have logged nothing, ever, so the first sweeps will name most of the fleet and the dedup is what keeps that a standing list rather than a flood. SELF-RESOLVE on the same evidence-based, routine-owned pattern as (e) — this category is absent from `ops.alert_policy` and therefore latching by construction: when a later sweep finds that routine's MOST RECENT completed run (the same `MAX(run_date)`-per-routine scoping as the raise predicate above — NOT merely any historical compliant day) now logs at least one `ops.web_calls` row, `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='auto-resolved: routine now logging ops.web_calls on its most recent completed run — verified by OPS0 telemetry sweep' WHERE category='web_call_coverage_gap' AND NOT resolved AND JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.routine') = '<routine>' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM state.web_call_coverage w WHERE w.routine = JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.routine') AND NOT w.missing_telemetry AND w.run_date = (SELECT MAX(run_date) FROM state.web_call_coverage w2 WHERE w2.routine = w.routine))`. **Both halves must be scoped, not just the raise (2026-08-25).** An unscoped resolve clears the alert on a single old compliant day and MASKS a routine that has since regressed — D2a is the live shape of that risk: compliant 2026-08-20, zero rows on its latest completed run 2026-08-24. Not yet observed firing (D2a's and W3's alerts each survived the one intervening OPS0 sweep unresolved), so this closes a latent masking path rather than reversing an already-fired false resolve. **The `auto-resolved:` prefix is load-bearing, not decoration:** `ops/monitoring/alert_emailer.gs` (v7) prints `AUTO-RESOLVED` only when `resolved_note` starts with that exact prefix, and plain `RESOLVED` otherwise — which reads to the operator as *a human closed this*. Without the prefix an OPS0 self-heal is reported as human action, the same mislabel class v7 fixed on 2026-08-05 in the opposite direction. The note still names OPS0 so triage can tell which resolver ran. **CONDITIONAL-SURFACE CARVE-OUT (2026-08-25; WIDENED FROM A NAMED LIST TO AN EVIDENCE TEST 2026-08-26, OPS0).** `expected_metered` is a STATIC per-routine flag, but a routine's metered surface can be CONDITIONAL — W5's market-calendar auto-extend and NO-GO-shadow FMP fallback, and SL1's per-quarter research calls, are the cases whose own obligation paragraph says in terms that a quiet cycle legitimately owes ZERO rows. **The carve-out is keyed on the EVIDENCE IN THAT CYCLE'S OWN `ops.run_log` NOTE, not on that list of routine ids** — the list names the known instances and is never a closed set. When ANY `expected_metered` routine's latest completed run logged nothing AND its own `ops.run_log` note AFFIRMATIVELY records that no metered call was made, that is COMPLIANCE, not a gap: do not raise, and note the suppression. MEASURED 2026-08-26 (OPS0) — the third instance, and the one that forced this widening: **W3**/2026-08-23, a deep-research routine nobody had listed as conditional, logged zero rows on a cycle whose in-scope book was EMPTY (zero open A/B/C/E positions, a first in recorded history), so its research surface had nothing to research. Its note states `METERED SPEND: ZERO ... every fact came from BigQuery, the IBKR connector, or repo files, all free ... an honest zero, not an omission`, and separately reports its sub-agents' capped web budget as `0 of 3 used`. Under the old named-list reading OPS0 would have raised a known-false `warning` that — per the row-bearing-resolve limitation named just below — could never clear until W3 next happened to have a research-heavy cycle. Enumerating the exempt routines BY ID was itself the defect: conditionality is a property of a given CYCLE, and only that cycle's own note can report it. MEASURED 2026-08-24: W5's cycle stated "market-calendar auto-extend NOT triggered ... so no FMP call spent", yet it still carried an open `web_call_coverage_gap` warning it could never clear, because the evidence-based resolve rule can only fire on a row-BEARING run. If the note is absent or ambiguous, do NOT suppress: raise, or leave an existing alert open, rather than guessing. **DETECTION ONLY — do NOT re-fire the routine, do NOT write an `ops.web_calls` row on its behalf, and do NOT read the gap as evidence the run itself was defective:** a run that made no metered call correctly writes no row, which is precisely why `expected_metered` scopes this check to routines whose prose names a metered surface, and why a gap outside that set is not a finding.

(b) **FMP DAILY BUDGET — early warning on the one metered limit whose failure mode is silent evidence loss rather than a bill.** `SELECT * FROM state.fmp_daily_budget WHERE run_date = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')` (logged `ops.web_calls` rows with `provider='fmp'` for the day, against the free tier's **250 requests/day ACCOUNT-WIDE** ceiling, with the percent consumed and a `fan_out_day` flag for days on which more than one fan-out-authorized routine completed). At **`>= 60%` of the cap (150 requests)**: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','OPS0','fmp_budget_pressure','FMP logged requests reached 60% of the 250/day free-tier cap — a later routine should degrade deliberately and SAY it degraded','<JSON: run_date, n_requests, pct_of_cap, fan_out_day>')`, counts in the payload only, message stable, same dedup reasoning as (a). SELF-RESOLVE identically once a later run reads back under the threshold: `resolved_note='FMP daily consumption back below 60% — verified by OPS0 telemetry sweep'`. **STATE THE COUNTER'S HONEST LIMIT WHEREVER THIS NUMBER IS QUOTED, per the State-provenance rule: `state.fmp_daily_budget` counts only LOGGED calls, so it is a FLOOR, not a meter.** A routine that called FMP and skipped its `ops.web_calls` INSERT is invisible to it — the same gap (a) exists to close — so until coverage is broad this warning can stay silent on a day the real cap was genuinely under pressure, and its absence is never evidence the day was clear. The 60% threshold was a GUESS against a measured weekday baseline of 12 requests (4.8% of cap, 2026-08-20), pending a full Sunday — when W1-W5, the dailies and SL3 all complete — being actually logged. **THAT PRECONDITION IS NOW DISCHARGED and the caveat is retired (W5 2026-09-13, adjudicating OPS0's `fmp_budget_threshold_now_measured` notice).** Three full fan-out Sundays are logged since the `ops.web_calls` obligation floor: **51.2% (128 requests, 2026-08-23), 38.4% (96, 2026-09-06), 25.2% (63, 2026-09-13)**, against a weekday baseline of 8-16.8%. So 60% sits **8.8pp above the highest Sunday yet observed and roughly 3.6x the weekday baseline** — calibrated rather than obviously wrong in either direction — and it has never fired. **Keep 60% and stop calling it a guess; it is now a measured-and-retained threshold.** Two honesty limits stay binding and are the reason this is not stronger than "retained": `state.fmp_daily_budget` counts only LOGGED calls, so every percentage here is a **FLOOR, not a meter**, and the 2026-09-13 sweep that produced these figures itself suppressed 3 coverage gaps under the conditional-surface carve-out, so real consumption on any of these days may be higher than the number quoted. Revisit only on a Sunday that actually exceeds 60%, or on evidence that the logging floor has moved materially. It exists because this cap does not fail cleanly: `quote` returns `Limit Reach`, `company/batch-market-cap` drops denied symbols at HTTP 200, and `marketPerformance` filters are accepted and ignored (all measured, shared rule part (a)) — and because exhausting FMP early pushes every structured lookup for the rest of the day onto metered search, so it is itself a Tavily cost driver. The 2026-08-17 sweep that lost COHR is what this warning exists to give a routine time to avoid.

**SCOPE GUARDRAIL (restated — already enforced by the view, not re-checked here): NEVER re-fire D2, D2a, M4, Q4, A3, or SL4.** These carry live-order-crafting or capital-adjacent-proposal dependencies where a late catch-up run is harmless to execute but does not recover the value a same-day run would have had — they keep their existing human-visible `missed_run`/`period_missed` alert only, unchanged by this routine. W4 is deliberately absent: its idempotent queue-only research handoff is catchup-safe. `state.catchup_refire_readiness` is built to never emit a row for the excluded routines; if it ever does (a future edit to `bigquery/59` regressed the exclusion list), STOP and raise a critical alert rather than re-firing — do not treat an order-staging routine's absence from the exclusion list as license to auto-refire it.

**Shared refire log + in-progress exclusion (v2, 2026-07-18).** `ops.catchup_refire_log` rows may now also be written by a BLOCKED DOWNSTREAM routine's dependency-wait ACTIVE REPAIR (note prefix `refired by <ID> dependency-wait`, tier-aware miss_key identical to this routine's own format) — the log's semantics are unchanged (permanent idempotency; any row for a miss_key = attempted; skip it), so treat such rows as normal, not as an anomaly. Separately, `state.catchup_available` / `state.period_catchup_available` (bigquery/90) now EXCLUDE a routine with a `'started'` run_log row in the last 3h and no terminal row — a routine legitimately mid-DEPENDENCY-WAIT past the 21:00 deadline is in-flight, not missed; refiring it would double-run it (its own guard's in-progress variant is the session-level backstop for the same race). The `needs_attention` ALARM itself deliberately keeps NO such exclusion — the dead-man's switch stays maximally paranoid; a `missed_run` alert for a still-waiting routine is acceptable noise (non-latching, auto-resolves on completion).

CHAT OUTPUT: one-line summary (e.g., "OPS0: 2 misses auto-refired (D1/2026-07-13, W2/2026-W28); 0 no_trigger_id. Sunday trigger sweep: 29 checked, 1 corrected, 0 warned. Landing sweep: 1 stranded (1 adopted, 0 alerted); 0 unlanded completed runs. Telemetry sweep: 3 web_call coverage gaps, FMP at 5% of daily cap.").
```

## OPS1. Morning Connector Liveness Probe — regular routine

Runs pre-market (06:30 MT), ~9.5 hours ahead of the 16:10-17:15 MT Sun-Thu cadence (owner-approved
2026-07-19, after an IBKR OAuth expiry was discovered only at D2a's 16:20 MT pre-flight and cascaded
into a halted evening). Detection-only: probes the connectors this system depends on with one read-only
call each and surfaces a re-auth need in the morning alert email instead of mid-cascade. This routine
NEVER refires anything and stages nothing. It writes no repo files EXCEPT the one narrow AUTO-ADD case in
the TOOL-INVENTORY DRIFT CHECK below (a new-tool manifest row, `added` drift only) — see that section for
the full scope; every other day, and every other kind of drift, it is still writes-no-repo-files exactly
as before.

```
Read access scope: none beyond the standard connector pre-flight — no Strategy.md, no roster, no
order-staging surface, no state table reads beyond `state.trading_day_today`.

Observability preamble binds as normal: run logging (`sp_routine_start`/`sp_routine_end`), the standard
BigQuery-liveness pre-flight read, TRANSIENT-FAILURE WAIT-AND-RETRY, and INCIDENT INHERITANCE. If
BigQuery itself is down, the standard pre-flight halt path already covers it (RUNBOOK §26) — that outage
class is loud everywhere already, nothing extra needed here. `depends_on: []`, same rationale as OPS0: a
probe that exists to catch an auth failure early must never itself be blocked by one.

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD** (the generalized guard that binds every `catchup_safe: true` routine — added for OPS1 2026-07-27 now that OPS2's inline catch-up can re-invoke it): FIRST, before anything else, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='OPS1' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "OPS1 already completed today" and END IMMEDIATELY; likewise END if another session's `'started'` OPS1 row for today exists with `log_ts` within the last 3 hours and no terminal row (an in-flight original). OPS1's probes/self-heals are each individually idempotent, but this makes a redundant re-run (its own late trigger, or an OPS2 inline catch-up) a clean no-op instead of a duplicate.

PROBES (read-only, one call each; on a transient-looking failure, one ~60s-spaced retry per the shared
ladder, then classify what's left): IBKR `get_account_summary` **and** `get_price_snapshot` for SPY (a
structurally valid snapshot response is a pass; pre-market empty bid/ask is expected and is NOT a failure);
Google Calendar `list_calendars`; FMP
`chart` (historical-price-eod, light) for `^VIX`, last ~5 days — probe the FMP-PRIMARY `^VIX` path
specifically, do NOT probe a tier-gated endpoint (`quote`, ETF historical chart) — a plan-tier ACCESS
DENIED there is a known, accepted state (OWNER_ACTIONS.md item W) and must NOT raise anything; Gmail
`list_labels`.

CLASSIFICATION. An AUTH-class failure (401/403/token-expired/"requires re-authorization"/OAuth wording)
surviving the retry: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','OPS1','connector_reauth_needed',
'<Connector> requires re-authorization — re-auth in claude.ai connector settings before the 16:10
MT Sun-Thu cadence (D1/D2a/D2)', '<JSON: connector, error_verbatim, probed_at>')` — one alert per
connector; `sp_raise_alert_once` keeps it idempotent. A non-auth `get_price_snapshot` failure surviving
the retry is a distinct, action-relevant partial IBKR outage: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning',
'OPS1','connector', 'IBKR get_price_snapshot surface unavailable for SPY after retry; account-state and
history surfaces require independent checks — quote-dependent MARKET crafts will defer while this
persists', '<JSON: connector="IBKR", surface="get_price_snapshot", probe_symbol="SPY", error_verbatim,
probed_at>')`. A non-auth failure on every other probe (e.g. an FMP rate-limit on the `^VIX` probe —
fired live 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-17): record in the run_log note AND, wrapped best-effort (IN-RUN
ISSUE REPORTING bullet above, Observability § — a REFUSED here must never kill OPS1 mid-run):
```
BEGIN
  CALL ops.sp_report_run_issue('OPS1', <today>, 'connector_probe_degraded', '<one-line summary naming the probe and the failure>', '<JSON: connector, probe, error_verbatim, probed_at>');
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN SELECT @@error.message;  -- swallow: a REFUSED validation floor must never abort OPS1 mid-run
END;
```
— this is deliberately NOT an `sp_raise_alert[_once]` call and must not use the `connector_reauth_needed`
category above, which is reserved for AUTH failures; note-only used to reach nobody (chat is
unmonitored), and this makes the degradation a durable, emailed fact instead, while the trading
routines' own pre-flights keep hard-stop authority for these surfaces exactly as before (wrapped per
FIX 1, 2026-09-08).

SELF-HEAL. On a HEALTHY probe of connector X while an unresolved `connector_reauth_needed` alert for X
is open: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note =
'verified-clear: OPS1 healthy <tool> probe for <Connector> at <ts>' WHERE NOT resolved AND
category='connector_reauth_needed' AND <connector match>` — same bespoke in-routine clear pattern as
D2a's `owner_confirmation_stale`.

On a healthy SPY snapshot probe, also read only these unresolved `connector` alerts: (a) `source='OPS1'`
with payload `connector='IBKR'`, `surface='get_price_snapshot'`, and `probe_symbol='SPY'`; (b) `source='D2a'`
with that connector/surface and `scope='account-wide'`; or (c) the legacy account-wide incident shape
`source='D2a'` and `failing_method='get_price_snapshot'` (the 2026-08-12 alert predates the structured
connector/surface payload contract). **Never** select a D2a `scope='symbol-specific'` alert here: SPY's
success does not prove VOO or another target recovered; D2a clears that only after a fresh successful
target-symbol snapshot. For each returned **`alert_id`**, resolve only
that exact row: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(),
resolved_note='verified clear: OPS1 SPY get_price_snapshot probe succeeded at <ts>' WHERE
alert_id='<that id>' AND NOT resolved`. Do not clear a generic IBKR `connector` alert from an account,
order, or other market-data surface: the successful proof is narrow and must match the alert payload.

<!-- connector-tools-checker: ignore-start -->
TOOL-INVENTORY DRIFT CHECK (added 2026-08-08). The four PROBES above prove each connector is
authenticated; they say nothing about the other ~99 tools those connectors expose. When a connector
vendor ships a NEW tool it arrives as "ask" / "needs approval" in the claude.ai connectors UI, and an
unattended routine that later calls it gets a permission prompt nobody can answer — the step stalls
with no error message and no dedicated alert class. This step exists to catch that drift the morning it
appears instead of the evening a trading routine happens to hit it.

Read the repo manifest `ops/connector_tools.yaml` (the expected inventory: 7 connectors, each with
`name`, `settings_prefix`, `tools[].name`, `tools[].use` ∈ required/optional/unused, and an `absent`
list) and enumerate the tools ACTUALLY available in this session, per connector, from the session's own
tool inventory (the deferred-tool listing the harness provides, and/or targeted `ToolSearch` probes
scoped per connector). **FAIL CLOSED — THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING RULE OF THIS STEP.** If the session
cannot enumerate a connector's tools completely and reliably, it must NOT report that connector clean:
record `enumeration_ok = FALSE` for that connector and let the alert fire. An enumeration this step
could not perform is an unknown, never a pass.

Write the observation with `CALL ops.sp_record_connector_tools('OPS1', <today America/Denver>,
<rows_json>)`, where `rows_json` is a JSON array over the UNION of observed tools and manifest tools —
one element per (connector, tool) with keys `connector`, `tool_name`, `present`, `in_manifest`,
`manifest_use`, `enumeration_ok`, `note`. Recording the union (not just the diff) is what makes an
absence a row rather than an inference.

**THE UNION INCLUDES EACH CONNECTOR'S `absent:` ENTRIES — pinned 2026-08-27, OPS1.** "The UNION of
observed tools and manifest tools" reads two ways, and the fleet took both: OPS1 wrote 120 / 120 / 115 /
121 / 116 rows on 2026-08-23 / 24 / 25 / 26 / 27, where the ±5 is entirely Hugging-Face's five-entry
`absent:` block being included on three of those runs and dropped on two — a write surface whose record
shape changed day to day with no rule to appeal to. **Include it.** An `absent:` entry names a tool the
manifest has already CONCLUDED is gone, so dropping it is precisely the "inference from a missing row"
that `bigquery/151_connector_tool_inventory.sql`'s STATEMENT 1 comment forbids, and it silently retires
the only per-run evidence that a DATED retirement (e.g. `paper_search`, `verified: 2026-07-28`) has not
quietly reappeared. Encode each such entry `present` = whatever was actually observed (normally FALSE),
`in_manifest = FALSE`, `manifest_use = NULL`. That pair is drift-NEUTRAL under `state.connector_tool_drift`
— its `added` arm needs `present AND NOT in_manifest` and its `removed` arm needs `in_manifest AND NOT
present`, so an absent-and-still-absent tool matches neither and raises nothing — while a REAPPEARANCE
flips `present` to TRUE and correctly surfaces as `added` drift, which is exactly the branch the AUTO-ADD
rule below already anticipates. Do **not** set `in_manifest = TRUE` for an `absent:` entry: it is not in
that connector's `tools:` list, and that encoding would leave the absence of a false `removed` alert
resting on `manifest_use` happening to stay NULL. Then `CALL ops.sp_raise_connector_tool_drift('OPS1')`, which
raises one `connector_tool_added` warning per newly-appeared tool, one `connector_tool_removed` alert per
vanished manifest tool (critical when its `use` is `required`), `connector_tool_enumeration_failed` on
an incomplete sweep, and mechanically self-heals any of these once the drift clears.

OPS1 does NOT change any connector permission — it cannot; the claude.ai connectors UI is owner-only,
and this step never touches it.

AUTO-ADD, `added` drift only (owner directive 2026-08-12 — the operator grants every new tool
"Always allow" regardless of relevance and will not manually edit this manifest, so a routine must, or
the alert nags forever). Scope: **only** the `added` case below. `removed` stays fully manual — a
vanished tool can break routine text calling it, which is a human judgment call, not a rubber stamp; do
NOT extend this auto-add to `removed` or to `connector_tool_enumeration_failed`.

First, for every `added` drift tool, check that connector's `absent:` block for a same-named entry — a
tool that was previously recorded absent (e.g. Hugging-Face's
`hf_doc_search`/`hf_doc_fetch`/`hf_hub_query`/`space_search`) can reappear and re-observe as `added`
drift exactly like a genuinely new tool, and CHECK1 in `scripts/check_connector_tools.py` hard-fails the
instant a name appears in both a connector's `tools:` and `absent:` lists. **Branch on that entry's
`verified` field:**
- **`verified: unconfirmed`** (not yet proven gone, reappearing is the expected resolution the manifest
  itself anticipated) — DELETE that `absent:` entry as part of the same edit, then proceed with the
  append below as normal.
- **`verified: "<a date>"`** (a dated, confirmed retirement, e.g. Hugging-Face's `paper_search`) — do
  **NOT** auto-delete it and do **NOT** append a `tools:` row for this one tool. A confirmed-dead tool
  reappearing is a surprising, higher-stakes event (deleting that record permanently disables CHECK4's
  ability to block a future accidental call to it, and nothing ever re-creates an `absent:` row since
  `removed` drift is never auto-reconciled) — leave the `connector_tool_added` alert OPEN for this one
  tool and add a note to the run_log flagging it by name for a human glance, same as any other
  OBSERVED-NOT-ACTIONED item. Continue auto-adding every OTHER `added` tool from this run normally; one
  flagged tool never blocks the rest.

For every tool cleared by the branch above, append one entry to that connector's `tools:` list in
`ops/connector_tools.yaml` — alphabetically among its existing siblings, matching the file's existing
convention — with `use: unused` and a note. **The note MUST be written as a YAML block scalar (`note: >`
or `note: |`, matching this file's own existing multi-line notes, e.g. `list_labels`'s), never a bare
single-line scalar** — the note text itself contains `` `use: unused` `` (a literal colon+space), and a
plain unquoted scalar containing `: ` is invalid YAML that `yaml.safe_load()` (what
`scripts/check_connector_tools.py` and OPS1's own next-run manifest read both use) throws a
`ScannerError` on — silently wrecking both the CI gate and the very self-heal this step depends on. Note
text: "Auto-added by OPS1 <today, America/Denver>. Vendor-added tool, first observed in the live
connector's tool inventory. `use: unused` is the conservative default — nothing in this fleet calls it
(mirrors the IBKR `whats_new` precedent, July 2026). Promoting it to required/optional and adding routine
prose that calls it is a separate, deliberate feature-adoption decision this step never makes on its
own." `use: unused` grants no routine any new capability — `scripts/check_connector_tools.py` CHECK 3/4
still block any routine text from calling a tool that isn't `required` — so this is safe to do
unconditionally, regardless of whether the operator has actually flipped the tool to "Always allow" in
the connectors UI: that flip is unobservable from this side (RUNBOOK §15a NAMESPACE NOTE) and is no
longer a precondition for silencing the alert.

Before committing, run `python scripts/check_connector_tools.py` and confirm the edit introduced no new
CHECK1 (manifest internal validity) finding. **If a new CHECK1 finding appears anyway** (e.g. a stale
unmerged auto-add branch from an earlier run already added the same row) — do NOT commit a manifest that
fails CI: revert this run's edit to `ops/connector_tools.yaml`, leave the `connector_tool_added` alert(s)
open, and add a run_log note naming the CHECK1 finding verbatim for a human to resolve; every OTHER
successfully-added tool this run still commits normally. Otherwise, commit and push per the standard
session-end procedure (OPERATING MODEL § Branch and state propagation) — this is the one case where OPS1
has repo output. The alert(s) raised THIS run are not resolved THIS run (the observation rows already
written this run still carry `in_manifest=false` from before the edit); each self-heals mechanically on
OPS1's next run once the merged manifest makes that day's fresh observation read `in_manifest=true` — the
existing self-heal arm in `sp_raise_connector_tool_drift` is unchanged and already keys on exactly this.
<!-- connector-tools-checker: ignore-end -->

RECURRENCE. If the same connector has alerted on OPS1's last 3+ CONSECUTIVE COMPLETED RUNS — count run-over-run
(e.g. consecutive `ops.run_log` OPS1 completions each carrying a `connector_reauth_needed` alert for that
connector), not calendar mornings; a gap where OPS1 itself did not run neither breaks nor pads the streak
(owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW naming convention — no evidence-window widening applies
to OPS1 itself, see Observability § above) — say so in that day's alert
message and note that the expiry interval should be recorded per RUNBOOK §15 and a provider-side fix
considered (e.g., an IBKR support ticket on OAuth session lifetime).

Log `'completed'` with a one-line per-connector status summary plus the TOOL-INVENTORY DRIFT CHECK result
(e.g., "IBKR OK, Calendar OK, FMP OK, Gmail OK. Tool inventory: no drift." or "IBKR requires re-auth
(alert raised); Calendar/FMP/Gmail OK. Tool inventory: 1 added (warning raised, auto-added to
ops/connector_tools.yaml as use: unused, self-heals next run), Tavily enumeration_ok=FALSE (alert
raised)."); no repo changes, no git output UNLESS this run auto-added a manifest row for an `added`
drift tool, in which case commit + push per the standard session-end procedure and say so in the note.

**THE FMP `^VIX` PROBE IS A METERED CALL — OPS1 ALWAYS OWES EXACTLY ONE `ops.web_calls` ROW PER RUN
(added 2026-08-20, OPS1).** The shared run-logging template's `ops.web_calls` sub-paragraph binds every
routine that touches FMP, and this routine touches it every single morning: the PROBES step's `^VIX`
EOD-chart call spends one of FMP's **250 free requests per day, account-wide** — the same cap whose
exhaustion cost the 2026-08-17 sweep its COHR detection. So write one row immediately before the
terminal `sp_routine_end` call, inside the same best-effort wrapper: `provider='fmp'`, `tool='chart'`,
`target=` the `^VIX` EOD-chart request (endpoint + symbol + date range), `depth=NULL`, `credits=1`,
`credits_reported=FALSE` (FMP reports no usage figure, so this is a rate-card ESTIMATE by construction
— per the State-provenance rule, say so when quoting it). **Log the row even when the probe FAILED** —
a rejected or errored request still consumed the day's allowance; only a call that never issued at all
is omitted, and then say so in the `<note>`. Count a retry as its own row (a second attempt is a second
request). **Why this is restated here rather than left to the shared template:** OPS1 is the one routine
whose metered-call count is a fixed, known CONSTANT, which makes it the fleet's cleanest control on the
telemetry itself — an OPS1 `run_date` missing from `ops.web_calls` is unambiguous evidence the row was
SKIPPED, never evidence of a quiet day, so it is the one routine where the "made no metered call" and
"made calls and forgot" ambiguity that `state.web_spend_month.has_unreported_runs` exists to flag can be
resolved outright. Measured 2026-08-20: `ops.web_calls` held zero OPS1 rows for any date, while every
OPS1 run since the table was created had made this probe.
