## W4. Weekly Research Handoff — regular routine

Runs after W1, W2, W3 are all saved. Converts distinct weekly research into idempotent queue work; D2 remains the sole daily revalidation and order-conversion owner.

```
Read access scope: Weekly cadence. Query `events.decision_log` (+ `analytics.find_precedents()`) bounded to the recent operationally-relevant window — all history, queryable, no live/archive split (§15). Read `Strategy.md`, `Experiment_Parameters.md`, `Operating_Protocols.md`, `Watchlist.md`, `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md` as relevant (positions from `state.current_positions`, regime from `state.current_regime`, decisions from `events.decision_log`).

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (generalized guard; W4 is catchup-safe).** FIRST, before the dependency gate or any read/write: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='W4' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "W4 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or W4's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY. Also END if another session's `'started'` W4 row for today exists with `log_ts` within the last 3 hours and no terminal row. W4's idempotent queue-only handoff is safe to catch up, but never to duplicate.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('W4', ['W1', 'W2', 'W3'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if W1, W2, or W3 have no `completed` run anywhere in the current weekly period — W1/W2/W3/W4 are `weekly_sun`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any W1/W2/W3 completion with `run_date BETWEEN` that week's Sunday `AND` today, not only a completion on this exact calendar day (this is also what fixed the pre-existing false-positive on a W4 running Monday afternoon against a Sunday-completed W1/W2/W3); self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

**NO W4 STAGING GATE EXISTS.** W4 no longer detects mechanical exits or crafts any order, so it must not read/raise the trading-enable gate, invoke broker tools, call an order guard, write staged-order or position-lifecycle records, or create a calendar confirmation. It may always write idempotent `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entries and Watchlist changes. D2 performs the only revalidation and capital-movement decision under its own daily gates.

Read the just-saved weekly research files:
- `Weekly_Catalyst_Calendar.md` (W1 — Strategy A and C shortlists)
- `Weekly_Post_Event_Screen.md` (W2 — Strategy B shortlist)
- `Weekly_Position_Deep_Dive.md` (W3 — per-position hold/weekly-thesis-action/research recommendations + weekly-only action flag)

**BOUNDARY: no direct exit or order staging.** Do not repeat D1's mechanical detection (convergence, time exit, option-expiry mechanics, or daily development-triggered invalidation); do not call broker order tools, order guards, `state.open_orders`, `events.position_events`, or Calendar MCP. D2 is the only routine that revalidates and converts either daily or weekly action findings. W4's only conversion is an idempotent `PENDING_ANALYSIS` handoff plus its distinct W1/W2 research queues and Watchlist work.

A. WEEKLY-ONLY THESIS ACTIONS FROM W3 — for each `weekly-thesis-action` recommendation or `WEEKLY-THESIS-ACTION` flag, insert one due-today `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry for D2 with the exact cumulative criterion, W3 evidence span, D1 windows already reviewed, and conservative default. Idempotently check open and terminal queue history plus relevant `events.decision_log` first; use a stable item key `weekly-thesis-<strategy>-<ticker>-<W3 ISO week>-<criterion-key>`. This handoff asks D2 to independently revalidate and, only if still confirmed, perform the sole order conversion. It is never an exit instruction and carries no staged-order write.

(Thesis construction and research deferrals are no longer scheduled as human-pasted calendar events. W4 enqueues them to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`); the daily D2 routine drains and runs them in-session, each as an isolated sub-task for fresh context. This keeps W4 light at high fan-out and incurs at most ~1 day latency — negligible against B's 10-day window.)

B. RESEARCH DEFERRALS FROM W3 — for each position with recommendation "further research":
   - Enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`): analysis_type research-deferral-checkpoint; the position's ticker/strategy; due_date = the date the resolving information becomes available (next trading day if already available); context = the specific information gap from W3 + reference to Strategy.md exit rules + "D2 must resolve the gap under its daily conversion rules"; conservative_default = exit the position if unresolved on due_date.

C. THESIS CONSTRUCTION FROM W2 (Strategy B) — for the W2 top-tier shortlist:
   - **ROUTER GATE FIRST — check `state.current_regime` (scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, key `B`) before enqueuing anything (limb added 2026-08-23 by W4; this codifies three consecutive cycles of actual behaviour and closes a spec gap referred to W5 on 2026-08-09 and again on 2026-08-17 that was never actioned).** If B is **DO-NOT-ACTIVATE**, the router bars every NEW B entry (`Strategy.md`'s Regime router section — the DO-NOT-ACTIVATE definition: no new entries, existing positions run to normal exits), so a thesis-construction row could only ever resolve to a foregone decline: enqueue **no** B thesis, route the top-tier candidates to the `Watchlist.md` "Strategy B watch overflow" section instead, marked **router-gated, not rank-gated**, and record the disposition. If B is **ACTIVATE**, proceed with the bullets below unchanged. This is the exact structure §D already carries for Strategy A ("If DO-NOT-ACTIVATE → route to Watchlist.md A-queue … no thesis"), and it is a **strategy gate, not a load cap** — the "no per-week cap, no overflow to Watchlist.md" wording below governs CAPACITY only and never licenses enqueuing into a closed router. Cycles 2026-W32, 2026-W34 (Mon) and 2026-W34 (Sun) each reached this outcome by inference, and W2's own file directs it in advance ("W4 must not enqueue these as staged entries while the DNA stands"). **Known and accepted cost, do not re-litigate it here:** a B window is only 10 trading days, so a router-gated candidate expires ungraded rather than waiting for a flip. That is the router doing its job; the calibration question about the router/window interaction belongs to W5 and M1a, not to W4.
   - Enqueue one `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) per top-tier candidate (no per-week cap, no overflow to Watchlist.md): analysis_type thesis-construction; strategy B; due_date per the **HARD CHECK** below; context = B-specific enrichment from W2 + the originating D1 research-screen decision id + Strategy.md B criteria + B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md + Operating_Protocols.md; conservative_default = decline (no entry) if the entry window closes unresolved. **Deterministic event-identity dedupe is mandatory:** before INSERT, inspect both open and terminal queue history plus relevant `events.decision_log` for `analysis_type='thesis-construction'`, strategy B, ticker, and `qualifying_event_date`. **KEY-FORMAT PIN (corrected 2026-08-23 by W4, on a defect W2 2026-W34 found and assigned to W4 as the owner of the enqueue-key format; W4 independently confirmed it against the table the same day).** Use exactly `item_key = thesis-<TICKER>-B-<YYYYMMDD>` — e.g. `thesis-MSCI-B-20260726`. **This is a correction of the specification to match production, not a change to production.** Every one of the ~40 B thesis rows ever written to `events.queue_events` uses this shape (`thesis-CARR-B-20260803`, `thesis-ISRG-B-20260719`, …); the shape this document previously mandated — `thesis-B-<ticker>-<qualifying_event_date>` — has **never been written by any routine**, and `SELECT … WHERE item_key LIKE 'thesis-B-%'` returns **zero rows** against the whole table. A session performing the documented dedupe as a literal string match would therefore have found "no prior identity" *always*, including for an event already enqueued — a false-negative that duplicates a thesis and, downstream, a position. Writing the old shape now would have been worse than the status quo: it would have split the identity space into two incompatible key families and orphaned all existing history from any key-based check. **So: match on the FIELDS `(item_type='thesis-construction', strategy='B', ticker, due_date)`, never on the key string** — that field-based match is what makes the dedupe correct regardless of key shape, and it is what the 2026-08-23 W2 and W4 runs both actually used. Skip only that already represented event, never every event for a ticker; a later distinct event remains eligible. Carry `qualifying_event_date` and all originating D1/W2 decision ids in the payload. Order by days-remaining-in-window (fewer first) so D2 prioritizes.
   - **HARD CHECK — due_date MUST be the earliest-doable date, NEVER a next-trading-day default (earliest-wins; §"In-session analysis and the Pending_Analysis.md queue").** W2 only shortlists names whose qualifying move has ALREADY REALIZED (the Operating_Protocols.md §19 significance judgment operates on realized closes, and PART 2 additionally requires B's frozen ≥5% event-day spec floor — either way the Day-0 close is by definition already in for every W2 candidate) → **due_date = today** (the W4 run date, America/Denver from `state.trading_day_today.today`), **even when today is a weekend/holiday** (analysis needs no live market; only the resulting order-confirmation event must land on a trading session). The ONLY legitimate future due_date in this section is the §E deconfliction case (1 trading day after an expected exit fill). Do NOT push due_date to "the next trading day", "the next D2 run", or "the Monday open" for cadence/load convenience — that is the forbidden "pushed later for load" pattern, and it needlessly force-declines near-expiry candidates whose entry window closes within a day or two (the 2026-06-21 W4 run mis-stamped all 8 B-theses to the next session, which would have auto-declined WIX whose window closed 6/22 had D2 not re-dated them). **Self-verify before the INSERTs (earliest-wins, not "always today"):** a future (after-today) due_date is legitimate ONLY when (a) §E deconfliction applies, or (b) the candidate's qualifying Day-0 close genuinely has not printed yet — in which case set due_date to the date that close lands (the earliest the analysis can actually run). Case (b) cannot occur for a W2 shortlist (every rankable W2 candidate's qualifying move, hence its Day-0 close, is by definition already in — §19 judges realized moves only), so in practice every §C row is due today. What is forbidden is pushing due_date later for cadence/load convenience (next-trading-day / next-D2 / Monday-open defaulting); if a row would post a later due_date for any reason other than (a) or (b), correct it to the earliest-doable date before writing.

D. THESIS CONSTRUCTION FROM W1 (Strategy A and C) — for the W1 top-tier shortlists:
   - **DIRECTION FILTER FIRST — drop `DIRECTION-INADMISSIBLE` names before anything else in this limb (added 2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE; the W4 half of W1 PART 2's DIRECTION ADMISSIBILITY rail — read that entry for the measurement).** Strategy A is long-only, so a W1 candidate whose hypothesized mispricing is that the name is OVER-valued cannot produce an A entry and must not consume a thesis slot or an A-queue row. Discard any top-10 name carrying W1's `DIRECTION-INADMISSIBLE (A long-only rail)` mark — **and check direction yourself from the candidate's own field (a) rather than trusting the mark's presence**, since a pre-2026-09-06 `Weekly_Catalyst_Calendar.md` predates the rail and carries no marks at all (the 2026-08-30 shortlist ranked a bearish AMAT at #3). **Backfill the slot from the next admissible candidate** so the limb still converts a full top-10 rather than shipping a short one, and name the dropped candidates in this run's `<note>`.
   - Strategy A top-tier (top-10, after the direction filter above): check `state.current_regime` / most-recent M1 A router. If DO-NOT-ACTIVATE → route to Watchlist.md A-queue (reason "router gate; queued for next M1 ACTIVATE"); no thesis. If ACTIVATE → enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) per top-tier name (analysis_type thesis-construction; strategy A; due_date today; context from W1 + Strategy.md/Operating_Protocols.md refs; conservative_default decline), ordered by catalyst-date proximity. No per-week cap. (The DO-NOT-ACTIVATE gate is a strategy gate, not a load cap.)
     - **CARRY W1's GATE MARK ACROSS THE ENQUEUE BOUNDARY (added 2026-09-20 by W4, closing the W4-owned half of `ops.alerts` `w4_a_queue_row_catalyst_stale_at_enqueue` — `559ee98c`, filed by W1 the same morning and naming this limb as the owning surface).** W1 PART 2's CATALYST-GATE MODE derives a gate date and marks every candidate `SPENT-BY-GATE` or `GATE-SURVIVING`, but nothing carried that mark into the row this limb writes, so an A-queue row banked a catalyst reference that the *same run* had already established would be spent before A can act on it — and no routine re-derives it afterwards. **MEASURED on the 2026-09-13 cycle, not inferred:** W4 added XOM, CVX, JPM and MRK citing catalysts of 2026-10-30, 2026-10-30, 2026-10-13 and the 2026-10-04/2026-10-10 PDUFAs, while the same run derived A's earliest reachable re-score as **2026-11-02** and wrote into `Watchlist.md` that all four are "very likely SPENT-BY-GATE"; all four still stand pending with no spent marker. So: **record W1's mark and the gate date it was derived against** in the row's context — on the `events.queue_events` row and in the `Watchlist.md` A-queue row alike — so a stale catalyst reference is self-declaring to a reader of `state.open_queue` or the file. This does **not** gate the routing and is not a reason to withhold a row: a `SPENT-BY-GATE` name is still banked, because the queue row's job is to remember the **NAME** for the next ACTIVATE epoch and a name whose catalyst passed simply draws a fresh one next cycle. The W1 half of that notice — having PART 2 publish the mark in a machine-readable field rather than in prose a downstream session must parse — is **NOT** fixed here, because W4 does not own W1's section; it stays with W5's SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE.
   - **ROUTER GATE FIRST — check `state.current_regime` (scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, key `C`) before enqueuing anything (limb added 2026-09-20 by W4; this codifies EIGHT consecutive cycles of actual behaviour and closes the last of this routine's three tier-routing asymmetries — the A limb above has carried a router gate since the section was written, §C gained one for B on 2026-08-23, and this limb alone still read as unconditional).** C's operative state is **not binary**: `Strategy.md` reserves broad ACTIVATE to a separate scope-widening adjudication whose conditions are unmet, so the live value has been **`HYBRID ACTIVATE (FOMC-only)`** continuously since 2026-08-05 (`div-C-202607-1`, re-affirmed UNCHANGED by `div-C-202608-1` on 2026-09-03). Under that carve-out **only an FOMC-type event is router-admissible**; every single-name / earnings candidate in the top-5 is **router-PARKED** and must NOT be enqueued — which is exactly what `Weekly_Catalyst_Calendar.md` PART 2C already publishes in its own `Router` column and restates in its Deferrals block ("Every candidate except the FOMC is **deferred on routing** — not on thesis quality and not on size"). If C is **DO-NOT-ACTIVATE**, nothing in the top-5 is admissible and this limb enqueues nothing at all. **This is a correction of the specification to match production, not a change to production** — the same shape as §C's 2026-08-23 KEY-FORMAT PIN. Every completed W4 run from 2026-07-26 through 2026-09-13 enqueued at most the ONE router-eligible FOMC row and parked the rest, reading the gate in by analogy to the A limb (2026-08-03's note is the most explicit: "Candidates 2-12 correctly NOT enqueued per the FOMC-only router gate … the gate working as designed"); the unconditional wording below has therefore **never been executed literally by any run**, and a session that did execute it literally would mint four or five theses into a closed carve-out for D2 to decline one at a time. **Dedupe on the FIELDS, never on the key string** — `(item_type='thesis-construction', strategy='C', ticker/event, due_date)` against both open and terminal queue history — the same rule §C pins for B: `thesis-FOMC-C-20261020` was minted by W4 2026-W37 and stays `pending` until D2 drains it on 2026-10-20, so every cycle from 2026-W38 until then MATCHES it rather than minting a duplicate. **There is no watch-overflow destination for a parked C name and none is created here:** `Watchlist.md` has no Strategy C section by design (its Architecture note — "not a name-queue; catalyst-driven via Weekly_Catalyst_Calendar.md and FOMC schedule"), W1 already carries the parked candidates at full detail in its own file, and a second index would duplicate that record rather than add to it — record the disposition in this run's `<note>` and decision row instead. The "No per-week cap" wording below governs **CAPACITY only** and never licenses enqueuing into a closed router, the same distinction §C draws for B.
   - Strategy C top-tier (top-5): enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) per top-tier name (analysis_type thesis-construction; strategy C; due_date = today if catalyst < 14 days, else the pre-catalyst window date 7-10 days before the catalyst; context from W1; conservative_default decline). No per-week cap.

E. CROSS-STRATEGY DECONFLICTION — per Strategy.md simultaneous-holding constraints (A↔B and A↔C cannot hold the same name): if a ticker is both a W3 weekly-thesis-action and a W1/W2 new-entry candidate, preserve both idempotent queue entries but add a context note requiring D2 to verify (via the connector / `state.current_positions`) the action disposition before any thesis conversion. Do not predict or stage an exit here.

F. WATCHLIST UPDATES — apply A-queue additions from D, B-watch overflow from C, and any other updates surfaced.

DEFERRAL DISCIPLINE: if a recommendation cannot be acted on this routine, specify (a) trigger date and information source, (b) conservative-default fallback. Deferrals do not chain. Enqueue deferred analyses to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`; never the calendar).

CHAT OUTPUT:
- One-line acknowledgment of file edits and idempotent `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue entries enqueued for D2; no order is crafted by W4.

If no file changes and no queue entries: "No actions required."

## W5. Factbase & Analytics Consolidation — regular routine

Runs weekly (Sunday, after W4). **Repurposed 2026-06-06 (BigQuery cutover §15):** the Decision_Log live/archive prune is RETIRED — `events.decision_log` holds everything, queryable + bounded, so there is nothing to archive. W5 is now **weekly knowledge + analytics consolidation**: extract new Strategy-B sub-patterns, capture protocol revisions, reconcile the Watchlist, and report historical calibration/reconciliation trends. It does not repair embeddings or investigate live account drift; D2a and the daily monitors own those operational controls. Not deep research.

```
Read access scope: Weekly cadence with factbase WRITE permission. Query `events.decision_log` (entries added since the last W5 run, by `entry_date`/`event_ts`), `analytics.calibration_summary`, historical `analytics.account_reconciliation` trends, and `state.current_positions`. Read the kept factbase/spec files `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md`, `Watchlist.md`, `Operating_Protocols.md`.

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before the dependency gate below, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='W5' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "W5 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or W5's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT redo the consolidation, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('W5', ['W4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if W4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current weekly period — W4 is `weekly_sun`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any W4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN` that week's Sunday `AND` today, not only a completion on this exact calendar day (this is also what fixed the pre-existing false-positive on a W5 running Monday against a Sunday-completed W4); self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

FACTBASE MIRRORING — walk the new `events.decision_log` entries since the last W5 run and mirror durable signal into the kept factbase files.

Mirror to `Watchlist.md`:
- For any entry that adds a name to a strategy queue (e.g., "AAPL added to A-watchlist queue per router-gate-failure pattern"), ensure the name appears in Watchlist.md under the appropriate strategy section. Per-name fields: ticker, date-added, source-`events.decision_log`-entry-date, reason summary, resolution-trigger condition (e.g., "next M1 with A router ACTIVATE").
- For any entry that resolves a queue item (e.g., a future thesis-construction session that processes a queued name), ensure the resolved name is removed from Watchlist.md.
- Do NOT add Strategy B prior-NO-GO names to Watchlist.md — B operates on event-flow with fresh evaluation per "NO-GO records are context, not barriers". Sub-pattern factbase preserves the durable signal.
- Do NOT add Strategy D pending re-screens to Watchlist.md — calendar events are the canonical source.
- Note: Watchlist.md is also written by D2 / M4 (action-conversion routines) and W4 (queue-only research handoff) for in-cycle additions; W5 reconciles any drift between those writes and `events.decision_log` signal.

Mirror to `Operating_Protocols.md`:
- For any entry that introduces or revises an operational protocol (operating-model updates, commission-disregarded protocol, "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" rule, conviction-calibration ladder, deferral chaining rules, file-conventions/read-access-scope policy, decision-log lifecycle policy, etc.), ensure the canonical-current text is reflected in Operating_Protocols.md. Each protocol gets a section with: title, current canonical text, revision-history list (date + `events.decision_log` entry pointer + brief change description per revision).
- When revising an existing protocol section, replace the canonical text with the new revision and append the prior canonical to revision history.
- Do NOT mirror NO-GO entries, position entries, calendar-recon entries, or session-end-consolidation entries — those are not protocol entries.
Mirror to `strategy/roster.yaml` (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive):
- For any `events.strategy_lifecycle` / roster transition in `events.decision_log` since the last W5 run (CANDIDATE / QUALIFYING / AUTHORING / UNDER_REVIEW / SHADOW / PAPER / PROBE / ADOPTED / RETIREMENT_PROPOSED / TERMINATED / POST_MORTEM / REJECTED), append a dated entry to the affected strategy's `revision_history:` list in `strategy/roster.yaml` (date + lifecycle event + `git_commit` + one-line note) — exactly the mirroring pattern this routine uses for Operating_Protocols.md protocol revisions. SL5 is the authoritative writer of roster MEMBERSHIP and the `roster_state` field; W5 only keeps the human-readable `revision_history` in sync and NEVER flips a `roster_state` itself.
- W5 is aware of `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py` (the roster analog of `check_cadence_consistency.py`): if a mirrored edit would make `strategy/roster.yaml` disagree with `state.strategy_roster` / the Strategy.md `## Strategy` sections / the slice-map, do NOT commit the drift — log a consistency-check anomaly (the CI gate would fail the build anyway, and auto-merge only merges on green CI).

ANALYTICS REVIEW (BigQuery) — the Decision_Log live/archive split + weekly prune is RETIRED (`events.decision_log` is queryable + bounded; nothing to archive). Instead:
- **Embedding trend only.** Routine-side `ops.sp_log_decision` embeds inline; pending/error detection and remediation are daily operational concerns. W5 may report the historical weekly embedding-health trend in its outcome, but performs no embedding maintenance.
- Review `analytics.calibration_shrunk` (self-improvement audit S-2/B-2, 2026-07-03 — supersedes reading `analytics.calibration_summary` alone) — per-conviction-tier `win_rate_shrunk` (Beta-Binomial posterior, honest-wide at low N) + `wilson_low`/`wilson_high` + `trustworthy_edge`. Log a one-line note to `events.decision_log` of the current per-tier posterior + interval width; this is the calibration signal any future thesis-construction session should read, NOT the raw `win_rate` column (which reads 1.000 on a small all-wins tier and is the exact overfitting hazard the foundation doc warns against). The BQML `conviction_model` (bigquery/04_analytics.sql, gated at ≥30 closed) is DEPRECATED — a logistic fit on ~30 fee-dominated, single-class, non-independent (one regime, correlated) binary outcomes with 4 categorical features and no CV/walk-forward would overfit; `calibration_shrunk` dominates it and needs no both-classes precondition. Do not build or gate on the BQML model even once 30 closed trades accrue.
- **Historical reconciliation reporting only.** Summarize week-over-week reconciliation/NAV history for learning and trend context, but do not diagnose a live discrepancy, raise an operational drift alert, or attempt a repair. D2a's daily broker reconciliation and its daily monitors are the sole operational owners of current account drift.
- **WASH-SALE EXPOSURE REVIEW (self-improvement audit ITEM 18, 2026-07-11).** **BACK-DATED PARK ROWS — ONE-TIME FULL SWEEP (2026-08-18).** `bigquery/178_park_wash_sale_exposure.sql` extends this view to cover park (`close_strategy='PARK'`) round trips, which were structurally invisible to it before (park fills live in `events.parking_events`, never in `events.trade_fills`). Those rows arrive ALREADY BACK-DATED — the first real one is the 2026-07-27 VOO liquidation, ~$78 of loss repurchased 2026-08-04 — so the "dated since the last W5 run" filter below would skip every one of them forever and this fix would land in the table without ever reaching the operator. Therefore: on the first W5 run that sees ANY `close_strategy='PARK'` row, ignore the date filter for park rows specifically and report the FULL park history once, then revert to the normal since-last-run behaviour (mechanically self-terminating: once reported, the prior `wash-sale-review` decision_log entry names those `close_trade_id`s, so a later run can tell already-reported park rows from genuinely new ones and must report only the latter). Read `state.wash_sale_exposure` (`bigquery/41_tax_lots.sql`, extended by `bigquery/178`) for any exposure rows dated since the last W5 run — a BUY within 30 calendar days of any strategy's loss-realizing SELL in the same ticker, ACROSS strategies (the roster's `n_max=8` ceiling means this experiment deliberately runs multiple strategies that can independently trade the same name; a per-strategy view cannot see this). Log a one-line note to `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='wash-sale-review'`) summarizing new-since-last-run exposure rows (ticker, strategies involved, estimated disallowed-loss amount) — **that entry is UNCONDITIONAL every cycle and is NOT gated by the materiality floor below; it is the audit trail the year-end review reads**; then, if any row is new since the last W5 run AND the MATERIALITY FLOOR below is met, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','wash_sale_exposure','<ticker> wash-sale exposure across strategies <strategies> — see payload for the estimated disallowed amount','<JSON>')` — **the template previously named the "estimated disallowed amount" as message content, contradicting this same bullet's own next sentence; corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep) so the template and the rule below it finally agree** so it reaches the monitored alert channel. **`_once`, not the plain `sp_raise_alert` this step used until 2026-08-25.** The step's self-termination guarantee rested entirely on a future memoryless session correctly diffing the prior cycle's `close_trade_id`s out of its own report; with the plain raise there was no dedup backstop if that prose-following ever slipped, and a duplicate exposure alert would simply be inserted. Keep the varying dollar amounts in the JSON payload and the message text stable per `(ticker, strategies)`, since `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on the exact `(category, message)` text. **RENDERING PINNED 2026-09-07: “stable per `(ticker, strategies)`” only holds once `<strategies>` has ONE spelling.** Render it as the DISTINCT strategy codes appearing in that ticker’s reported rows — the union of `close_strategy` and `replacement_strategy` — sorted ASCENDING, joined by a single comma with NO spaces. The 2026-09-07 raise was a single-element set (`PARK`) and so was stable by luck; a two-strategy set has two orderings and only one of them matches the already-open row. Same pin, same reason, as the `regime_restore_shortfall` bullet below. **MATERIALITY FLOOR ON THE RAISE — $25 of newly-reported disallowed loss measured SINCE THE LAST CYCLE THAT ACTUALLY RAISED, not since the last run (added 2026-09-14, interactive triage of the 2026-09-14 alert board).** This floor gates ONLY the `sp_raise_alert_once` call above; the `events.decision_log` `wash-sale-review` entry stays unconditional, so nothing stops being recorded and the year-end picture is unchanged. MEASURED, not projected: the park-v4 graded ladder now manufactures exposure rows BY CONSTRUCTION rather than as the trace of a discretionary trade — `target_f_pct` moved 0 -> 25 (2026-09-08) -> 50 (2026-09-10), each graded step SELLS VOO while either a prior step's buy or a routine weekly idle-cash park sweep sits inside the same 30-day window, and `events.trade_fills` holds ZERO VOO rows, so every one of these is park plumbing. The category fired on 2 of the 2 cycles since v4 went live, and the per-cycle figure has collapsed from the whole-vehicle-switch era ($78.61 on 2026-08-24, $107.73 on 2026-09-06) to $6.36 on 2026-09-13 — 0.04% of the $15,736.56 NAV. Note also what the cumulative $192.70 is NOT: it is not a lost dollar, it is loss disallowed for the current tax year and added to the replacement lot's basis, recovered when that lot sells. A WARNING that re-fires weekly at single-digit dollars is the alarm-fatigue pattern this plan retires elsewhere, and it would bury the whole-vehicle events that do matter. **Raise only once the sum of `estimated_disallowed_loss` over rows reported since the last cycle that actually RAISED this category reaches `$25`.** **"Since the last RAISE" is load-bearing and must NOT be simplified to "since the last run":** a per-run test lets an unbounded number of sub-threshold weekly steps each pass unreported and never accumulate — a silent under-report, which is the exact failure a floor exists to prevent. This needs no new state: the still-open or most-recently-resolved alert's own `close_trade_id_prefixes` payload field already identifies which rows were last reported. $25 sits BELOW every whole-vehicle switch observed to date and ABOVE every graded-ladder step observed to date, so a genuine re-vehicling still pages on the cycle it happens. When the floor is not met, say so in this run's `<note>` with the running sub-threshold total and the number of deferred rows, so a drip stays visible in the record even while it is off the board. **This changes the raise CONDITION only — the message literal is untouched**, so the `(ticker, strategies)` dedup pin above and `scripts/check_alert_message_stability.py` are unaffected. ROOT-CAUSE LEVER, deliberately NOT taken here: `PARK_ALLOCATOR_V4_DESIGN.md` item 4 (`VOO<->VTI`) would remove this row class at source by re-risking into a non-substantially-identical fund, but that is a live allocator-substance question with its own open contradiction, not alert plumbing, and it is not settled by this floor. Detection/reporting only — this never blocks a trade or a kill-trigger action (IBKR's own 1099-B, computed off the elected cost-basis method, remains the authoritative tax figure); it exists so the accumulating disallowed-loss exposure is visible before year-end rather than discovered on the 1099-B. **CLOSING THE PRIOR RUN'S NOTICE (added 2026-09-07, alongside the capital-review heal below — this category had no closer either, and for a subtly different reason worth stating so nobody "fixes" it the wrong way).** `wash_sale_exposure` is a **NOTICE, not a condition.** `state.wash_sale_exposure` is a historical record over realized closes and their replacement buys; a wash sale that occurred stays in the view permanently and the view never empties. So there is no condition-cleared moment to wait for, and a heal keyed on the exposure disappearing — the shape used for the two capital categories below — would wait forever and is the wrong instrument here. The alert's actual job is "there is exposure you have not been told about yet", and that job is DONE once this step has written its `wash-sale-review` entry to `events.decision_log`. Therefore, AFTER that entry is written: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'notice delivered: the exposure rows were reported in the events.decision_log wash-sale-review entry for <this run date> (closed by W5)' WHERE category = 'wash_sale_exposure' AND NOT resolved AND alert_ts < <this run's start timestamp>`. **The `alert_ts` bound is load-bearing:** without it this statement closes the alert THIS run has just raised, in the same run, and the operator never sees it — resolve only rows that predate this run, so every notice gets one full weekly cycle on the board. **BUT THE BOUND IS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THE ORDER IS: RESOLVE FIRST, THEN RAISE (pinned 2026-09-13, W5, on measurement).** The paragraph above says "AFTER that entry is written", and a session reading it literally does entry → raise → resolve. That sequence silently swallows the notice, because the raise is `sp_raise_alert_once` against a message deliberately held STABLE per `(ticker, strategies)`: when the same ticker/strategy pair is still exposed — which is the normal case, since the view never empties — the "raise" matches the still-open row from the PRIOR cycle and writes nothing new. The row now carrying this cycle's notice therefore legitimately predates this run, the `alert_ts` bound does not exclude it, and the resolve closes it. Measured 2026-09-13: the open row was the 2026-09-06 raise, and this cycle's exposure rendered byte-identically to it. So: (1) write the `wash-sale-review` entry; (2) resolve the prior-cycle rows with the `alert_ts` bound; (3) THEN `sp_raise_alert_once`, which — finding no unresolved match — inserts a fresh row carrying this cycle's reading. Net board state is one open row, freshly dated, and the prior notice is closed with the evidence that it was delivered. Do NOT "fix" this by varying the message to force a new row; that re-opens the `_once`-defeating drift the message-stability pin exists to prevent. **REGISTRY GAP, closed in-band (same date).** This category has no `ops.alert_policy` row at all — `bigquery/164` registered the three capital categories and nothing ever registered this one, so its latching semantics and closure rule were undeclared for its whole life and a triage session reading the registry would find nothing. Rather than land a one-row SQL file, register it on the first run that finds it missing, with the same `WHERE NOT EXISTS` guard `bigquery/164` uses so it is idempotent and safe to re-run. **THE `FROM UNNEST([1]) AS _g` IS LOAD-BEARING — DO NOT DROP IT (corrected 2026-09-14, after this exact template was executed and failed).** This template previously read `SELECT <literals> WHERE NOT EXISTS (...)` with no `FROM` at all, which BigQuery rejects outright: `Query without FROM clause cannot have a WHERE clause`. MEASURED by running it verbatim on 2026-09-14 while registering two other categories. `bigquery/164`, which this sentence cites as the pattern, does NOT have this bug — it selects `FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(...), ...]) AS p` and correlates the guard on `p.category`, and it is the `FROM` that makes the `WHERE` legal. The bug was introduced when the multi-row form was flattened to a single literal row and the `FROM` went with it. Any join-less source works; `UNNEST([1])` is the shortest. A future session hitting the broken form has to improvise under time pressure and may well improvise something that is NOT idempotent, which is the whole point of the guard: `INSERT INTO ops.alert_policy (category, latching, resolve_rule, note) SELECT 'wash_sale_exposure', FALSE, 'Closed by W5 on the run AFTER the one that raised it, once the wash-sale-review entry naming the exposure rows has been written to events.decision_log. NOT condition-healed: state.wash_sale_exposure is a permanent historical record that never empties, so an absence test would never fire.', 'Cross-strategy wash-sale exposure: a BUY within 30 calendar days of a loss-realizing SELL in the same ticker, across strategies and including PARK round trips (bigquery/178, bigquery/219). WARNING, never critical - detection and reporting only, it never blocks a trade, and IBKR 1099-B remains the authoritative tax figure.' FROM UNNEST([1]) AS _g WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ops.alert_policy e WHERE e.category = 'wash_sale_exposure')`.
- Review `analytics.process_scorecard` (self-improvement audit S-7/B-9, 2026-07-03) — decision-quality signals that accrue per-decision, not per rare close: `conviction_tiers_observed` / `analytics.conviction_monotonicity` (does higher stated conviction rank-order higher realized P&L — read as raw per-tier counts, directional only, never a trigger), `go_minus_opened` (a large gap between GO theses and positions actually opened flags a staging-pipeline issue worth a look), `forecast_pct_below_band` (is the M5 TWR forecast systematically biased — advisory only, per bigquery/06_forecast.sql), and `forecast_pct_above_band` (added 2026-09-14, bigquery/238, alert 8e8747ed-c8b0-4e87-8d4c-79c23bee765f — the mirror-image check: a one-sided ABOVE-band skew desensitizes the below-band downside read, since the same flat central forecast path that lets a rising equity curve exit the top of the band also pins pi_lower well under the live trajectory; MEASURED 2026-09-01, B 52.5% / D 51.2% of elapsed points landed above band that vintage vs 0% below, so a 0-below-band reading alone is weak evidence of health, not strong). Each metric carries its own `min_n_met` floor; below it, log the observation but do not treat it as signal. AUTONOMOUS ROUTING (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion): a detected staging-pipeline gap must NOT dead-end as a chat note a human is expected to "take a look" at. For any metric with `min_n_met=TRUE` whose reading is out of band (e.g. `go_minus_opened` materially positive), log the finding to `events.decision_log` AND `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','W5','process_scorecard_signal','<metric + value + strategy>','<JSON>')` so it reaches the monitored alert channel rather than an unread chat surface (severity bumped info→warning 2026-07-16, consumption-closure CC-7 — `info` is filtered by both `alert_emailer.gs` and `alert_relay.py`, so this alert never actually reached any monitored channel until now); `forecast_pct_below_band` and `forecast_pct_above_band` both stay advisory (log-only) per bigquery/06_forecast.sql.
- **CAPITAL-UTILISATION & RESTORE-INTEGRITY REVIEW (2026-08-11, `bigquery/164_capital_utilisation_and_restore_integrity.sql`).** Three read-only checks on whether the capital model is still doing what Experiment_Parameters.md says it does — reward winners passively via survivorship. All three are WARNING-class and none can halt trading.

  **HEAL FIRST, FROM THIS SAME READ, BEFORE YOU RAISE (added 2026-09-07 — the exact sibling of D2a's regime/nomadic heal added the day before, found because `regime_restore_shortfall` fired on 2026-09-07 with nothing anywhere able to close it).** `bigquery/164` registered all three of these categories `latching = FALSE`, each with a `resolve_rule` opening "Auto-resolves when …" — and W5, the only routine that reads these views, implemented ONLY the raise side. Nothing else can close them: `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` is hardcoded to an unrelated category set and touches none of the three, and no other routine reads `state.capital_utilisation_watch` or `state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` at all. So a condition that healed weeks ago still sits on the board as an open WARNING — and since `state.system_health.open_alerts` counts every unresolved row and the emailer re-lists the board, it becomes permanent weekly noise: exactly the alarm fatigue this plan warns about, arriving through a promise the registry made and no code kept. **Evaluate the heal from the SAME read that drives the raise, ABOVE the branch**, per ONE MOVEMENT PER READ — a second `SELECT` can observe a different snapshot and close a row the raise branch is about to re-open.
  - **`capital_stranded` — heal PER STRATEGY, never category-wide.** This is the one place D2a's pattern must NOT be copied verbatim. D2a may scope its heal by `category` alone because `sp_raise_alert_once` admits at most one open row per category *when the message is constant*; here the message deliberately names the strategy (see item 1 below), so this category holds **one open row PER STRATEGY**, and a category-wide `UPDATE` would close strategy B's live alert the moment strategy A deploys — silently destroying a true warning. For each strategy present in the rows you just read with `is_stranded = FALSE`: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'condition healed: state.capital_utilisation_watch no longer reports is_stranded for this strategy — it deployed, was evaluated again, or its idle capital fell below the floor (healed by W5)' WHERE category = 'capital_stranded' AND NOT resolved AND STARTS_WITH(message, '<strategy> has stranded idle capital')`. Match on the STRATEGY-BEARING PREFIX rather than the whole literal: the prefix carries the identity, and a prefix match still finds a row raised under an earlier wording of the tail.
  - **`regime_restore_shortfall` — heal on the FLAGS, never on an empty result.** `state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` is `FROM donors CROSS JOIN newcomer LEFT JOIN debt ON TRUE`, and `bigquery/164`'s own header states the consequence outright: "This shape always emits at least one row: a single all-clear row with `strategy = NULL` when no debt exists, and one row per debtor otherwise." That shape is deliberate — a monitor that goes silent when healthy is indistinguishable from one that has died — so an absence test here is not merely fragile, it is **unreachable**: it would never fire, and the heal would be vacuous. Heal only when the rows you just read carry `aggregate_at_risk = FALSE` **AND** `at_risk_including_newcomer_claim = FALSE` (both, since either one alone raises): `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'condition healed: donor capacity again covers the outstanding regime-capital debt including the pending-newcomer claim (healed by W5)' WHERE category = 'regime_restore_shortfall' AND NOT resolved`. Category-wide scope is correct HERE and only here: the raise is an aggregate condition over the whole book, so the pinned message admits exactly one open row.
  - **`capital_concentration` — nothing to heal, and that is not a defect.** `bigquery/164` registered it but, as its own note records, it is "not wired to a raise call on apply — reserved for a future D3/W5 step". Nothing raises it, so nothing can be open. Do NOT add a heal for it, and do NOT read its registered-but-unraised state as the same defect as the two above. **`cash_fee` (`bigquery/214`) is in the identical position** — verified 2026-09-07: no `sp_raise_alert` site anywhere names it, so its resolve_rule naming no routine costs nothing. **The general rule for a no-closer sweep: check whether anything RAISES the category before calling its missing closer a defect.** A registered-but-unwired category is a reserved slot, not a leak; only a category that can actually open a row needs a path to close it.
  1. `SELECT * FROM state.capital_utilisation_watch` — one row per capital-ENABLED strategy. For any row with `is_stranded = TRUE`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','capital_stranded','<strategy> has stranded idle capital — see payload for the idle amount and days since deployment','<TO_JSON_STRING of the row>')`. **MESSAGE STABILITY, corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep): the template here named `idle_capital` and `days_since_deployment` as MESSAGE content, and both drift every week the condition persists — `idle_capital` with marks, `days_since_deployment` by construction. `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on `WHERE NOT resolved AND category = in_category AND message = in_message` (`bigquery/10_observability.sql`), an EXACT string match and nothing else, so a drifting message degenerates `_once` into a plain `sp_raise_alert` and a persisting stranded strategy raises a FRESH weekly alert, each separately emailed. Keep the strategy code — constant for the life of the condition, so it correctly gives one open row PER strategy — and carry every varying number in the payload.** Same rule and same reason as the `wash_sale_exposure` bullet above and the `probe_funding_stalled` correction in SL3 STEP 5 (2026-08-26). **Read the `posture` column before acting.** A strategy that is idle but has a non-zero `evaluations_60d` is HEALTHY — Operating_Protocols §16 says an active strategy that is merely idle keeps its capital, and declining a thesis on its own mechanical criteria IS the strategy working. `is_stranded` deliberately fires only when idle capital is material AND there has been no deployment for 90+ days AND nothing has evaluated the strategy in 60 days. Do NOT widen this predicate to "idle capital alone"; it would fire on every healthy low-frequency strategy from day one and be muted within a week.
  2. `SELECT * FROM state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` — the swept-capital debt against what the enabled donors could actually return. On `aggregate_at_risk` or `at_risk_including_newcomer_claim`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','regime_restore_shortfall','debtors <strategy-codes> — swept-capital debt exceeds returnable donor capacity; see payload for total debt, donor capacity and shortfall','<JSON>')`. **MESSAGE STABILITY, corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep): the template named three DOLLAR figures as message content. This passage itself says `bigquery/98`'s restore trigger is "a standing condition … re-evaluated on every read, no transition gate, no cooldown" — so those figures move on every W5 evaluation while the same underlying under-capitalisation persists, and `sp_raise_alert_once`'s exact-message dedup therefore never matches. Name only the identifiers in the message; the dollars belong in the payload.** **RENDERING PINNED 2026-09-07 — the same class, third pass, found because this alert fired.** “Name only the identifiers” left HOW to name them to the session, and a memoryless routine composes that clause fresh every week: the 2026-09-07 raise rendered it `debtor strategies A, B and D against an empty enabled-donor set` — a sentence no second session reproduces byte-for-byte. That is the same `_once`-defeating drift as a moving dollar figure, arriving through PROSE instead of arithmetic, and nothing in the fleet can see it: `bigquery/205` swept moving VALUES, `bigquery/227` swept `STRING_AGG` ORDERING, and `scripts/check_alert_message_stability.py` parses `bigquery/*.sql` — none of the three looks at a template whose message is rendered by a ROUTINE rather than by SQL. The message is now a FIXED literal with exactly ONE substitution: `<strategy-codes>` is the DISTINCT non-NULL `strategy` values of the rows you just read, sorted ASCENDING, joined by a single comma with NO spaces, and nothing else — no prose, no donor-set clause, no counts, no “and”. Donor capacity moves independently of the debtor set, so naming it in the message would re-introduce exactly the drift this pin removes; it belongs in the payload only. **Read "shortfall" as THIS SESSION'S shortfall, not a loss.** `bigquery/98`'s restore trigger is a standing condition (any enabled strategy with `outstanding_debt > 0`, re-evaluated on every read, no transition gate, no cooldown, no retry guard), so an unpaid residual is re-proposed automatically as donor capacity recovers — the `>=$25-or-full-debt` floor only defers a sub-$25 tail, it cannot strand it. So this alert means "a re-enabled strategy is trading on a fraction of its owed capital right now," not "capital was lost." That is still worth surfacing, because an under-capitalised debtor is otherwise invisible — it just quietly trades smaller than it should, and nobody would connect that to a sweep weeks earlier. The view also nets the SISA pending-newcomer probe-stake claim, because newcomers outrank the restore on every inflow and nothing else shows the two claims against one pool.
  3. `SELECT * FROM state.sweep_recipient_weights` — informational this run. It precomputes the mechanical, judgment-free capacity tilt (share of the trailing 180 days each recipient actually held a position, mapped onto §16's sanctioned [0.5x, 2x] band) that a future D2a SWEEP substep may apply instead of DEFAULT-EQUAL. No alert; log the reading if `sweep_share` diverges materially from `equal_share`, since that is the first evidence the tilt would change an outcome.
- **EXTERNAL-SPEND DIGEST (2026-08-17, `bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql` — the consumer that closes the shared "Metered external calls" rule's part (d)).** Read BOTH: `SELECT * FROM state.web_spend_month WHERE month_start >= DATE_TRUNC(DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), INTERVAL 60 DAY), MONTH)` (per `(month, provider, routine)` call counts and credits) **and `SELECT * FROM state.web_duplicate_targets ORDER BY credits_on_repeats DESC LIMIT 25`** — both over `ops.web_calls`. Log one `events.decision_log` entry via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type='external-spend-digest'`, naming the current month's fleet total per provider, the top 3 routines by `credits`, and — **the finding that actually matters** — the top repeat-fetched targets with their `credits_on_repeats` and whether each is `is_cross_routine`. **A cross-routine repeat is the highest-value one to report**: neither routine can see the other doing it, so it is the class that persists indefinitely unnoticed, and it is the concrete instance of the shared rule's "the one thing that IS waste." **ALSO NAME THE PRICED-DEPTH SHARE, which this digest has never reported even though the column already exists (added 2026-08-21, external-spend audit).** `state.web_spend_month` already computes `n_priced_upgrade` (`bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql`) and nothing has ever read it, so the second of the two levers the shared rule's baseline note itself names — "search COUNT and search DEPTH, in that order" — is measured, stored, and then left out of the only report that reads this table. Per `(month, routine)`, state `n_priced_upgrade` as a share of that routine's Tavily searches together with the credits attributable to the upgrade (advanced bills 2 credits to basic's 1, so the upgrade's own cost in credits equals `n_priced_upgrade`), and say when that share MOVED rather than only where it stands: measured across the 171 logged Tavily calls to 2026-08-21, 95 were advanced (55.6%) = 95 of 252.4 logged credits, **38% of logged Tavily spend**, and the rate swung from 14% advanced on the 2026-08-19 D1 run (8 of 57 searches) to 76% on 2026-08-20 (54 of 71) across two consecutive runs with no recorded reason — the swing is the reportable finding, not the level. Same FLOOR caveat as (1) below: this share is computed over LOGGED calls only. **RECORD-ONLY — no threshold, no alert, no cap; nothing here gates anything and W5 never edits a token. Specifically, this share is NOT a proposal to disable `auto_parameters=true` or to force basic depth** — that setting is ENDORSED by owner directive 2026-08-17 (the session picks depth per task, paying 2 credits when that is the better answer), and a depth cap read out of this number would be exactly the unfounded knob the "no per-routine credit cap from spend alone" rule below refuses. Three honesty requirements, all binding: (1) **report `has_unreported_runs`** — where TRUE, that routine logged completed runs that emitted no token, so its credits are a **FLOOR, not a total**; name those routines rather than quoting a fleet figure that reads as complete; (2) per the shared rule this series is a **self-reported ESTIMATE, not a meter** (no usage endpoint exists on the Tavily MCP surface), so the provider's own dashboard stays authoritative for the account total — state the estimate as an estimate and never reconcile the two silently; (3) **A FALLING METERED TOTAL IS NOT PROOF OF FEWER EXTERNAL LOOKUPS** (2026-09-14, closes the `web_call_telemetry_offledger_gap` info alert) — `ops.web_calls.provider` accepts only the four literal tokens `tavily`|`anthropic`|`fmp`|`hf` (`bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql`, live-superseded on read by `bigquery/203_web_call_provider_normalise.sql`), so a routine that moves a lookup onto a free, unmetered direct-HTTP fetch (e.g. SEC EDGAR via the Bash tool) cannot log it here at all — there is no provider token for an unmetered surface, and coining one is a fleet-wide schema change out of scope for a single digest read. Measured instance: M2, 2026-09-01, ~175 direct SEC EDGAR HTTPS requests in one run, none representable, while the same run still wrote 225 genuine metered rows (not a coverage gap). Read a month-over-month DECREASE in this series as a possible sign that work moved off-ledger, not an automatic efficiency win, unless you can also confirm no such migration occurred. **Do not propose a per-routine credit cap from fewer than two COMPLETE months of tokens.** The series exists precisely to make such a cap evidence-based; a first partial month is the noise the sibling process-reliability loop's 3-consecutive-cycle persistence bar exists to reject, and the same discipline binds here.
- **SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE (added 2026-08-28 — W5 is the named owner on most of these and, until now, read none of them).**
  ```sql
  SELECT alert_id, alert_ts, severity, source, category, message, payload
  FROM ops.alerts
  WHERE NOT resolved
    AND ( severity = 'info'                                  -- the OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS convention's own filing level
          OR message LIKE '%SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE%' )    -- a defect filed ABOVE info that still names this step as its owner
    AND category NOT IN ('spec_defect_notice_stalled',       -- this step's own escalations; they close via the HEAL clause below,
                         'spec_defect_backlog_undrained')    -- never by being re-adjudicated as defects in their own right
  ORDER BY alert_ts
  ```
  **SEVERITY IS NOT THE FILTER — THE ROUTING MARKER IS (widened 2026-09-20, closing a verified dead-end).** This query read
  `severity = 'info'` ALONE from its creation until 2026-09-20. The convention tells a routine to file a cross-surface defect at
  `info`, so that matched for most rows — but a routine that judges a defect worth an OWNER-VISIBLE `warning` (because it also
  carries a live data error, say) was writing into a void: the row names this step as its owner in its own message, and this step
  could not see it. Found by the ORCL `screen_move_measured_on_opens` row (W2, 2026-09-20, `severity='warning'`), which said
  "Nearest owning routine for any spec change is W5, SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE" and was structurally unreachable from here; it
  also had no `ops.alert_policy` row, so nothing auto-resolved it either — a latch with no closure path at all.
  **The widening is bounded and was measured before landing, not assumed:** across ALL unresolved rows at the time, 38 of 62
  `info` rows named this step, and exactly 2 of 11 non-`info` rows did — one being this step's OWN `spec_defect_notice_stalled`
  escalation, which the `category NOT IN` guard above excludes because its closure path is the HEAL clause, not re-adjudication.
  So the marker clause admits real spec defects and cannot flood this step with operational warnings: `staged_order_awaiting_confirm`,
  `queue_driven_missed_fire` and their kin never name this step and never match. Do NOT re-narrow this to `severity='info'`,
  and do NOT instead go around telling routines to downgrade such findings to `info` — that would trade a reachable closure path
  for a quieter inbox on exactly the findings someone judged loud enough to escalate.
  These are cross-surface findings other routines recorded under the shared **OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS** rule
  (§Observability) — a routine found a defect on a surface it does not own and filed it rather than fixing it.
  **This step exists because the venue had no consumer at all.** Measured 2026-08-28: 12 open `info` rows,
  8 of them naming "W5 self-improvement" as the nearest owning routine, and W5's section contained ZERO reads of
  `ops.alerts` — every one of those rows was stranded by construction, some for days, and the fleet had begun
  independently rediscovering the same defects and filing the rediscoveries into the same void. That is the exact
  failure the rule now warns about, so W5 must not recreate it: the point of this step is that these rows get
  ADJUDICATED, not merely listed in a digest.
  For each row, do ONE of three things and say which:
  1. **FIX IT** if the surface is W5's own or the fix is a self-contained prose/spec correction W5 can make in this
     run. Then `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = '<what
     changed, with the file and named anchor>' WHERE alert_id = '<id>'` — scope by `alert_id`, never by category.
  2. **ROUTE IT** if a lane with a real drainer fits (`PENDING_ANALYSIS`→D2, `PENDING_REVIEW`→AR_att/AR_orc,
     `PENDING_DRAFT`→SL2, `PENDING_ROSTER`→SL5): write the queue row, then resolve the alert citing the
     `item_key` you created. Confirm the drainer really reads that lane before claiming it — the same
     verified-consumer obligation the shared rule states, and what `state.queue_venue_claim_unwired` checks
     mechanically.
     **SATISFY THE DESTINATION LANE'S OWN PAYLOAD CONTRACT — W5 IS A PRODUCER INTO IT, NOT AN EXEMPT CALLER
     (added 2026-09-21, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing SL2's `pending_draft_enqueue_omits_review_type`,
     alert `c0d5041a-2c1e-4b63-aa01-b586d36358cc`).** On a `PENDING_DRAFT` row of `item_type='strategy-revise'`,
     the PENDING_DRAFT LANE CONTRACT (SL2 section) REQUIRES `payload.review_type` — it is what SL2's route (B)
     dispatches on (`'pre-mortem'` for a live-strategy task, `'strategy-adoption'` for a candidate task) — and
     route (B) additionally identifies a live-strategy pre-mortem task by the TRIPLE `review_type='pre-mortem'`
     AND an active strategy code AND `artifact_path='strategy/08_pre_mortems.md'`. MEASURED: the row W5 wrote on
     2026-09-06 (`event_id fead6511-b57d-4de8-99fd-59300410db94`, `item_key premortem-B-provenance-flag-20260906`)
     carried NO `payload.review_type` and a NULL `artifact_path` — **two of those three identifiers absent.**
     **So: set `payload.review_type` on every `strategy-revise` row this branch enqueues — to `'pre-mortem'`
     or `'strategy-adoption'`, the contract's only two legal values, and NEVER to the row's own `item_type`
     string `'strategy-revise'` — and set `artifact_path` wherever the finding names a file.** **(Enum pinned
     AT THE IMPERATIVE 2026-09-22 by SL2, closing the WRONG-VALUE half that the 2026-09-21 wording left open —
     SL2's `pending_draft_review_type_wrong_value`, alert `42115b5f-2b6f-47e5-9cb1-5a7127e103a7`. The enum was
     already stated two sentences up, but only as context about how SL2 dispatches; the imperative itself sat
     the literal `strategy-revise` directly beside `payload.review_type`, and a later fire then wrote exactly
     that value. An omitted field is at least detectable as missing — a populated field carrying a
     plausible-looking wrong value reads as compliant, which is why the two halves needed closing separately.)**
     The cost that time was ZERO — the payload's own
     `surface`/`task` fields named the locus unambiguously and SL2 dispatched correctly and drained it in full
     (Strategy B pre-mortem rev 13, commit `a7667528`) — and that is exactly why it is worth pinning now: the
     failure mode of an under-specified lane row is not a loud error but a SILENT mis-dispatch or a no-op, and
     the next such row may not carry an equally self-describing payload. The append-only 2026-09-06 row is
     drained and terminal; it is history and must NOT be corrected in place. The same obligation binds every
     other lane this branch writes into — read the destination's contract before enqueuing, do not assume a
     free-form payload is acceptable because the drainer happened to cope once.
  3. **REJECT IT** if it is not a real defect, is already fixed, or is superseded. Resolve with the evidence that
     shows so. A rejection needs a reason a later reader can check, not an assertion.
  Leave a row OPEN only when you cannot dispose of it this cycle, and **record WHY against exactly one of three
  BLOCKER CLASSES** (added 2026-09-14): `owner_decision` — a policy or design call that is genuinely not W5's to
  make; `capacity` — a real, mechanically-fixable defect this cycle simply did not reach; `blocked_on_other_work`
  — it depends on a landing that has not happened yet. Name the class per row in this run's `<note>` and carry it
  in the escalation payload's `blocker_class` field below. **MEASURED 2026-09-14 (interactive triage of the first
  escalation batch) — the classes are nowhere near evenly split, and this sentence previously admitted only the
  first one.** All 20 escalated rows were independently re-verified as real, still-live defects (20 of 20
  `VERIFIED_TRUE`), and across the full 49-row open board 35 (71%) were mechanically fixable with no owner input
  at all, against 9 (18%) needing a genuine judgment call, 4 (8%) self-declared no-action, and 1 duplicate. So the
  dominant reason a row sat open was **capacity, not a pending owner decision** — while this sentence said the
  opposite and the escalation below told the owner all 20 'need an owner decision'. That miscategorisation is
  itself the defect: it asks for 20 rulings when about 4 were owed, and buries those 4.
  **MINIMUM ADJUDICATION BUDGET — dispose of at least 12 rows per cycle, OLDEST `alert_ts` FIRST, and take this
  step BEFORE the other W5 loops (added 2026-09-14).** MEASURED root cause of the backlog: this step shares one
  weekly session with eleven other substantial review loops (PROCESS-RELIABILITY, STRATEGY-PLAYBOOK,
  EXECUTION-QUALITY, CALIBRATION-PARAMETER, STRATEGY-ARSENAL LIFECYCLE DIGEST, ADVERSARIAL INDEPENDENCE AUDIT,
  CROSS-MODEL REFEREE, RESEARCH-QUALITY FEEDBACK, PARK SCORECARD, PARK FORWARD-TEST COUNTDOWN,
  CAPITAL-ALLOCATION SCORECARD) and it loses the scheduling fight to them as the board grows — drain fell
  **17 -> 15 -> 7** across the 2026-08-31, 09-07 and 09-14 cycles while arrivals held at ~32-48/week, so the open
  board grew +39 in 17 days. Those competing loops are overwhelmingly RECORD-ONLY and non-urgent by design (most
  write a heartbeat and a not-ready line); an unadjudicated spec defect is the one thing in this section that
  COMPOUNDS. Oldest-first is load-bearing: it is what drains a backlog in bounded time instead of churning the
  newest arrivals while the oldest rot. If a cycle genuinely cannot reach 12, say so in the `<note>` with the
  count actually reached and what displaced it — that is the signal this budget needs revisiting, and it must not
  be silent. **Never resolve one merely to clear the board** — an unactioned resolve is worse than the
  strand it replaces, because it destroys the record too. These categories are deliberately absent from
  `ops.alert_policy`'s auto-resolve allowlist so they latch until someone acts; do not add them to it.
  **ESCALATE A ROW LEFT OPEN ACROSS >=2 CONSECUTIVE CYCLES (added 2026-09-08, run-outcome notification design
  P6(d)).** A row correctly left OPEN above reaches no channel at all: `info` severity is filtered out of both
  `alert_emailer.gs` and `alert_relay.py` (measured: 104 of 104 `info` alerts raised in the trailing 90d were
  never delivered), and every one of the 33 live triggers routes its OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS into exactly this
  venue via the SCOPE_ADDENDUM — the same class CC-7 already fixed once for `immediate_action_flagged` /
  `process_scorecard_signal` (info→warning, 2026-07-16). For each row left OPEN this cycle, check whether
  `alert_ts < <the previous completed W5 run's log_ts>` (`SELECT MAX(log_ts) FROM ops.run_log WHERE
  routine='W5' AND status='completed' AND log_ts < <this run's start>`): since this step reads every open
  `info` row unconditionally every W5 cycle, a row whose `alert_ts` predates the last completed W5 run was
  necessarily read and left open on that prior cycle too, so this predicate alone proves >=2 consecutive
  cycles open with no separate counter to maintain. **ESCALATE PER-ROW ONLY WHAT ACTUALLY NEEDS THE OWNER (narrowed 2026-09-14; the >=2-cycle
  predicate above is UNCHANGED).** On a stale row whose `blocker_class` is **`owner_decision`**:
  `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5',
  'spec_defect_notice_stalled', '<alert_id> has sat OPEN in SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE for >=2 consecutive W5
  cycles and needs an owner decision', '<JSON: alert_id, category, source, first_seen_open_at, blocker_class>')`. **The
  message's only variable is the underlying row's `alert_id`, stable for the life of that row (C2) — never
  embed the cycle count or a date, both of which would re-mint a fresh alert every week this stays open.**
  On stale rows whose `blocker_class` is `capacity` or `blocked_on_other_work`, do **NOT** raise one alert each —
  raise exactly ONE aggregate: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','spec_defect_backlog_undrained','SPEC-DEFECT
  NOTICE INTAKE has rows that have sat open for >=2 consecutive W5 cycles for lack of adjudication capacity rather
  than for want of an owner decision — see payload for backlog depth, the oldest row and the per-class split','<JSON:
  n_stale_capacity, n_stale_blocked, n_open_total, oldest_alert_id, oldest_alert_ts, n_adjudicated_this_cycle,
  budget_met>')`. **That message is a FIXED literal and every count lives ONLY in the payload** — a count in the
  message re-mints a fresh alert the moment the depth moves, the exact `_once` defeat the pinned-literal rules
  elsewhere in this plan exist to prevent. HEAL it from the same read, before the raise: when NO stale
  `capacity`/`blocked_on_other_work` row remains, `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts =
  CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'condition healed: no SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE row remains open across >=2
  consecutive cycles for capacity reasons (healed by W5)' WHERE category = 'spec_defect_backlog_undrained' AND NOT
  resolved` — condition-healed, so unlike its per-row sibling it needs no parent row to close it.
  **WHY NARROWED, and what must NOT be concluded from it.** MEASURED 2026-09-14: the first firing put 20
  near-identical lines on one digest, of which only about 4 were genuine owner decisions and the rest were capacity
  rows the owner can do nothing about; on the then-current net growth (+25 to +41/week against a 7/week drain) the
  same email was projected to reach ~150-500 lines within 4-12 weeks — the alarm fatigue that buries the few rows

The rates axis is the live example of why this exists — `10Y >= 4.90` is an ABSOLUTE level on an unbounded series, so it tracks the rate regime rather than market stress and would go silently dead at a 3% 10Y or silently pinned at 6%. It fires 0.69% today and that is a DECISION, not a defect (the recalibration was replayed and lost 0.921pp — PARK_ALLOCATOR_V4_DESIGN.md §2.2 THRESHOLD STUDY), so do NOT report mere rarity as drift. Report the numbers every cycle even when all six read `ok`: a calibration line that appears only on failure gives the owner no trend to read, and this project has repeatedly found that absence-shaped signals read as healthy in both directions. Always `INSERT INTO ops.heartbeat (source, note) VALUES ('loop:park_allocator', 'W5 scorecard evaluated this cycle')` in ADDITION to D1's own daily heartbeat (Operating_Protocols.md §13.F) — belt-and-suspenders on the dead-man's switch, same multi-routine-heartbeat pattern `strategy_arsenal` uses.

- **PARK FORWARD-TEST COUNTDOWN — THE RE-EVALUATION TRIGGER (added 2026-09-04, owner directive on
  activating the graded ladder; `bigquery/221_park_episode_log_and_reevaluation.sql`).** The owner
  activated the v4 graded ladder on live capital 2026-09-04 with an explicit plan: run it forward,
  accumulate 2-3 more multi-axis episodes, then re-evaluate — and said plainly that the re-evaluation
  will NOT happen unless something triggers it. **This step is that trigger. Do not remove it, and do
  not let it become advisory.** Read `state.park_reevaluation_due` (one row). Report
  `episodes_since_activation`, `mean_edge_vs_actual_pp`, `mean_edge_vs_never_pp` and
  `episodes_ladder_beat_actual` in the `park-scorecard` decision-log entry EVERY cycle, whether or not
  the countdown has matured — a countdown nobody sees until it fires is a countdown nobody trusts.
  **When `due` is TRUE:** `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','park_ladder_reevaluation_due',
  'park v4 graded ladder: forward-test episode threshold reached — owner re-evaluation due',
  '<JSON: activation_date, episodes_since_activation, mean_edge_vs_actual_pp, mean_edge_vs_never_pp,
  episodes_ladder_beat_actual>')`. **The message string is deliberately CONSTANT** — no episode count
  or edge figure in the message itself, only in the payload — because `sp_raise_alert_once` dedupes on
  the message and a varying one would raise a fresh alert every week (the repo's own recorded
  alert-fatigue defect). Severity is `warning` on purpose: `critical` enters `blocking_criticals` and
  would halt order staging INCLUDING EXITS over a review reminder, while `info` is filtered out of
  BOTH notification paths (`scripts/alert_relay.py` and `alert_emailer.gs` each take
  `severity IN ('critical','warning')`) and would never reach the operator — which is the one thing
  this step exists to prevent. **CLOSURE PATH, so the row cannot latch open forever:** it is resolved
  by the owner-facing re-evaluation itself — a `events.decision_log` row with
  `entry_type='park-ladder-reevaluation'` recording the verdict (continue / retune / demote to shadow
  / abandon). Until that row exists the alert legitimately stays open and keeps re-notifying, which is
  the intended behaviour for a decision the owner has asked to be forced back to.
  **What the re-evaluating session must NOT do:** treat 3 episodes as a significance test. Measured
  before activation over 15 historical episodes, forward-looking with the execution lag, the defensive
  signal had mean edge −0.638pp with SD 1.308pp and won only 4 of 15 — SD is ~2x the effect, so
  resolving it statistically needs ~30 episodes (~2.5 years), not three. The forward test is for
  STRUCTURAL discovery (does the shock axis fire on real risk or on cross-asset noise; does STRICT
  decay hold f too long), and the decision-relevant criterion is `ladder_edge_vs_actual_pp` — the
  alternative to the ladder is the binary all-or-nothing switch, not never de-risking.
  `mean_edge_vs_never_pp` is reported alongside because whether to de-risk AT ALL is a real and larger
  question, but it does not gate this one.
