**NO-GO COUNTERFACTUAL SHADOW-TRACKING (self-improvement audit S-3, 2026-07-03) — makes step 3 above bidirectional.** The taxonomy above records only avoided trades; it never checks whether the avoided name actually underperformed, which is pure survivorship/confirmation-bias exposure. Two sub-steps, both best-effort (a connector hiccup must never abort W5). **Price sourcing (rewired 2026-07-19: IBKR-primary after FMP free-tier re-scope; owner-approved):** IBKR is PRIMARY — resolve the shadow ticker via `search_contracts` (exact-symbol row, US primary listing) and read `get_price_snapshot`'s `last` (when the market is closed, `last`/`prior_close` is the prior close — fine for a weekly shadow mark); `mcp__FMP__quote` is a best-effort FALLBACK only, and now works only for FMP's free-list symbols (~87 big-caps + 9 indexes) since FMP's 2026-07-19 free-tier re-scoping symbol-blocked the rest:
   a. **Log new shadow rows.** For each new criterion-4 NO-GO extracted in step 3 above (a genuine sub-pattern classification, not a mechanical NO-GO): fetch the ticker's current price per the sourcing note above, then `INSERT INTO events.nogo_shadow (decision_log_entry_id, ticker, sub_pattern, nogo_date, entry_ref_price)` (`horizon_days` defaults to 21 — leave it unless the thesis window implies otherwise). `bigquery/28_nogo_shadow.sql`.
   b. **Close out elapsed shadow rows.** Query `SELECT * FROM events.nogo_shadow WHERE forward_price IS NULL AND DATE_ADD(nogo_date, INTERVAL horizon_days DAY) <= CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')`. For each: fetch the ticker's current price per the sourcing note above and `UPDATE events.nogo_shadow SET forward_price = <price>, forward_price_date = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver') WHERE event_id = <id>` (a `SELECT`-then-`INSERT`-corrected-row pattern is fine too since this table is a low-volume shadow log, not the append-only trading truth — it is explicitly a mutable tracking table, not one of the audit-trail tables `state.append_only_integrity` watches).
   c. **Read the tally, update the taxonomy.** Read **`analytics.nogo_counterfactual_by_primary`** (per-PRIMARY-token `n_correct`/`n_incorrect`/`n_closed_unscored`/`min_n_met` — scored on EXCESS RETURN against the park, never raw price, so a rising-market false "wrong NO-GO" reading is avoided). **THE GOVERNING COLUMN PAIR IS THE UNLABELLED `n_correct`/`n_incorrect`, AND THE VIEW IS DEFINED BY `bigquery/238_nogo_counterfactual_vehicle_aware.sql`, NOT `bigquery/152` (corrected 2026-09-27, W5, after this sentence caused a live mis-read in the same session that fixed it).** This sentence said "excess return vs SGOV" and cited `bigquery/152`, and both halves went stale on 2026-09-13 when `bigquery/238` superseded 152's benchmark CTE — SGOV stopped being the park vehicle on 2026-07-15 (owner Rev 38, Operating_Protocols.md §13) and since the v4 graded ladder went live on capital 2026-09-04 the park is not one ticker at all but a VOO/SGOV blend at a moving fraction `f`. `bigquery/238` therefore scores against the park the capital WAS ACTUALLY IN and keeps the old reading queryable beside it as `n_correct_vs_sgov`/`n_incorrect_vs_sgov`. **So the view now carries TWO pairs, and the phrase "vs SGOV" names the SUPERSEDED one** — a session following the old wording literally reads `*_vs_sgov` and gets the repudiated benchmark back. MEASURED that this is not hypothetical: on 2026-09-27 it flipped PatternN's verdict, which reads 3 correct / 4 incorrect (BELOW chance) on the governing pair and 4 correct / 3 incorrect (ABOVE chance) on the legacy pair, so the wrong column pair would have withdrawn a below-chance note that `bigquery/238` had been landed specifically to justify. SP1 (3/6) and SP4 (5/12) read identically under both framings, which is why no earlier cycle had to disambiguate and the staleness survived three cycles unnoticed. Read `*_vs_sgov` only to explain a historical reading, never to decide the note or the demotion. **Read the by-primary view, NOT `analytics.nogo_counterfactual_summary`, for the `min_n_met` decision below** (2026-08-09, W5): the older summary groups on the RAW decorated `sub_pattern` string, and because the controlled vocabulary appends variant letters, ` (candidate)` and ` [overlay: …]` composites, 37 shadow rows fragmented into 33 single-row buckets — its `>=5 closed-out` floor was **structurally unreachable**, so this demotion branch could never fire. `nogo_counterfactual_by_primary` groups at the grain `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md` already documents (`REGEXP_EXTRACT(sub_pattern, r'^(SP[0-9]+|PatternN|Mechanical)')`) and collapses the same 37 rows to 13 tokens. The raw-grain summary view is kept, unchanged, for the finer per-composite detail. Also check `n_closed_unscored`: a NON-ZERO value there means closed rows whose excess return could not be computed, which is the failure mode that hid the 2026-07-19..2026-08-09 outage (a NULL scored in neither direction and read as "no signal yet" rather than "never scored") — investigate it rather than reading the tally as complete. For any sub-pattern with `min_n_met = TRUE` (>=5 closed-out) and `n_incorrect > n_correct`, append a note to that sub-pattern's B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md section: "counterfactual tally: X/Y NO-GOs where the avoided name subsequently underperformed SGOV — below-chance, candidate for taxonomy review" — an autonomously-actioned taxonomy update, NOT a chat/human-visible flag someone must resolve (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion). The N-floor caveat is PRESERVED as the data gate: a below-chance tally at low N can still be noise, so while `5 <= N < 20` the note above stays informational-only and routing is NOT down-weighted. Once a sub-pattern reaches **N >= 20** closed-out shadow rows still with `n_incorrect > n_correct`, the loop SELF-APPLIES the down-weight with NO human taxonomy-review step: change that note to a dated `DEMOTED — routing down-weighted` entry, commit + push (auto-merge on green CI), log an `events.decision_log` entry, and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','W5','nogo_subpattern_demoted','<sub-pattern + X/Y tally>','<JSON>')`.

**THE UPPER BOUND IS PINNED AT 20, RESOLVING THE PRIOR `15-20` RANGE (W5 2026-08-30).** This clause read `N>=15-20` on both sides of the partition from its authoring until 2026-08-30, which is not a threshold but a range — and because both clauses used the identical token, a token landing anywhere inside [15, 20] belonged to neither branch and to both. That went unnoticed for as long as no token had ever crossed 15. On 2026-08-30 SP4 closed out at **N=17 (5 correct / 12 incorrect)** — the first token ever to enter the range — and W5 had to adjudicate a SELF-APPLY, with no human step, on prose that did not determine the answer. It is pinned at the CONSERVATIVE end because that is the end the clause's own stated rationale points to: the caveat exists to avoid down-weighting on noise, so where the text is ambiguous the reading that declines to act is the one consistent with its purpose. Concretely, at n=17 with 5 correct the one-sided binomial p under a fair-coin null is **0.072** — above the conventional bar, i.e. the noise this gate guards against is demonstrably not yet excluded at the range's lower end. Do NOT re-open this as a range; if the bar should move, move the number.

**REPORT THE MARGINAL TRANCHE, NOT ONLY THE CUMULATIVE TALLY — binding whenever a token is at or near the bar.** A cumulative below-chance count says nothing about whether the evidence is still arriving in that direction, and the difference decides the action. Measured on 2026-08-30: SP4's cumulative reading was 5/17 (below chance, in-band) while the SEVEN rows that closed that very cycle went **4 correct / 3 incorrect** — above chance — moving the cumulative from 1/10 (10%) to 5/17 (29%). A session reading only the cumulative number would have seen a token marching toward demotion; the tranche shows its fresh evidence had just reversed. So whenever this step reports a tally for a token with `min_n_met = TRUE`, state (i) the cumulative `n_correct`/`n_closed_out`, (ii) the count and direction of the rows closed THIS cycle, and (iii) whether those two agree — and if the marginal tranche contradicts the cumulative direction, say so and do not treat the cumulative figure as a trend. This is a REPORTING requirement, not a second gate: it never blocks a self-apply that the N>=20 bar authorizes, it only forbids reaching that bar without having looked.

**DECISION-LOG VOCABULARY DRIFT WATCH (added 2026-07-30, decision-record audit).** W5 already owns controlled-vocabulary hygiene for `sub_pattern` (ops/RUNBOOK.md §21 — the one sanctioned in-place-UPDATE exception, and W5 conforms any drift). Extend that ownership to the two columns the learning views actually key on, which had NO owner and no check at all. This is a ROUTINE-side watch by necessity, not a CI gate: this repo's CI checkers are static offline text parsers with no live BigQuery access (only the keyless-WIF `warehouse-validation` job touches the warehouse), so nothing in CI can see a bad value that only exists as data.

Query the vocabulary actually in use since the last W5 run:

```sql
SELECT entry_type, decision, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(entry_date) AS first_seen, MAX(entry_date) AS last_seen
FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.decision_log`
WHERE entry_date > <last W5 run date>
GROUP BY entry_type, decision ORDER BY n DESC
```

Check BOTH DIRECTIONS. Checking only one is how the 2026-07-20..22 incident stayed invisible for months:

**(a) WRONGLY EXCLUDED (false negative)** — a value not in the controlled vocabulary, which a view's filter therefore drops. This is the entry_type='thesis' case.

**(b) WRONGLY INCLUDED (false positive)** — a value that a view's filter MATCHES but that is not in the sanctioned set. This direction exists because `analytics.thesis_outcomes.is_go_family` is a `^GO\b` PREFIX test, which is strictly more permissive than the two-value GO family it is meant to recognise: verified live that `'GO/NO-GO'`, `'GO-WITHOUT-ORDER'`, `'GO-AHEAD'`, `'GO,'` and `'GO (partial)'` would all match. Any of those would be counted as a GO observation in calibration AND would pass the campaign-join guard that exists to stop a non-GO thesis inheriting a real position's realized P&L. Run:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT decision FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.decision_log`
WHERE entry_type IN ('thesis-construction','thesis')
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(decision,''))), r'^GO\b')
  AND UPPER(TRIM(decision)) NOT IN ('GO', 'GO (ADD TRANCHE)')
```

Any row returned is a false positive already accruing into calibration — treat as CRITICAL, not a warning, and tighten `is_go_family` to an explicit allowlist in a new numbered `bigquery/` file in the same session.

For any value found in EITHER direction: **do not attempt to UPDATE the rows** (append-only; only `sub_pattern` has an exception, and a second standing exception was explicitly declined — ops/RUNBOOK.md §44). Instead, in the same W5 session: (i) determine whether any learning view's filter silently excludes it — check `analytics.thesis_outcomes`, `analytics.conviction_features`, `analytics.thesis_outcome_summary` for the affected row; (ii) if it IS excluded, widen the relevant view's synonym tolerance in a NEW numbered `bigquery/` file, apply it live, and mirror the change into the dbt model so the dbt-parity row-level check stays green; (iii) correct the emitting routine's text here so the drift stops at source; (iv) `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','W5','decision_vocab_drift','<the value + affected view>','<JSON>')` and log it in the W5 outcome entry. Self-executed, no chat step.

WHY this is worth a weekly query: the 2026-07-20..22 `entry_type='thesis'` incident ran for three days, self-corrected, and was never noticed — it took a dedicated audit four months later to find that a real Strategy B GO had been invisible to every calibration view the whole time. `analytics.thesis_outcomes.paired_by_fk` and the drift query above are the two cheap telemetry reads that would have surfaced it in a week.

What actually guarantees this metric is correct is the DATE-PINNING of the `treasury-rates` call itself — that is the control, not any subsequent arithmetic check. **Optional genuine cross-check, when reachable:** FRED publishes `T10Y2Y` as an independent series (`bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql`); if you can read it for the same pinned date, comparing it to your derived spread IS a real two-source test — a disagreement means one of the two pulls is off-date, so stop and re-resolve. Note `fred.stlouisfed.org` returns HTTP 403 to a direct fetch and needs the Tavily-extract route with a cache-busting query param (see `hy_oas` above), so treat this as best-effort, never a gate. *(Historical note: the 2026-07 defect was exposed by exactly this kind of disagreement — the stored spread 0.47 was right while its own stored legs implied 0.45 — but that was only detectable because the spread had come from FRED's independent T10Y2Y print while the legs came from a stale FMP row. Same-row derivation would have hidden it.)*
  - **`hy_oas`** — FRED `BAMLH0A0HYM2` remains the only source (FMP does not carry it, `bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql:68`; no independent dated credit-spread series exists anywhere in this project). **Require the source to actually contain a row for that date.** If the print is not yet published, write NO `hy_oas` row for the month and backfill it on the next run — never substitute the nearest earlier date silently. **This series publishes with a ~1-day lag and updates around 08:52–11:30 CDT**, so a `first_trading_day` M1a run in the early-morning MT slot will routinely fire BEFORE the month-end print exists — expect the deferred-backfill path to be the NORMAL case here, not an exception. **Fetch note (measured 2026-08-05, REVISED 2026-08-30):** `fred.stlouisfed.org` returns **HTTP 403 to a direct `WebFetch`** (both the `fredgraph.csv` and `/data/*.txt` forms); the series page IS readable via Tavily extract, and a cache-busting query param (e.g. `?cb=<today>`) is needed or a stale crawl comes back. **BUT TAVILY EXTRACT IS NO LONGER RELIABLE HERE, AND IT IS NO LONGER THE ONLY PATH.** D1 measured `Request timed out at 10.02s` against BOTH sanctioned paths (the `fredgraph.csv` endpoint and the series page, each cache-busted) on 2026-08-24 and again on 2026-08-30 — two runs six days apart, four failures, zero successes. Failed extractions are not billed, so this costs evidence, not credits. **MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-01 (M1a), AND IT SUCCEEDED — so treat the unreliability claim as INTERMITTENT, not settled:** the cache-busted series page returned current data via Tavily extract in 6.21s on the first attempt, and the rung-3 `curl` returned HTTP 200 in 1.56s with the same last observation, both agreeing on `BAMLH0A0HYM2` `2026-08-28,2.60`. Rung 2 is therefore still worth attempting before rung 3 rather than skipped as known-dead; the request-shaped-block hypothesis below is untouched by this (it still explains the `WebFetch` 403), but a blanket "no longer reliable" reading of Tavily is now contradicted by direct measurement. **FRED ITSELF IS UP: a plain `curl` with its DEFAULT User-Agent got HTTP 200 from both paths in under 0.3s, twice each, on 2026-08-30**, returning current data (`BAMLH0A0HYM2` last row `2026-08-27,2.63`). The same host, same session, same machine FAILED every one of four attempts when the request carried a normal browser User-Agent (HTTP/2 `INTERNAL_ERROR`; an 18s dead timeout when forced to HTTP/1.1). **So the block is REQUEST-SHAPED, not availability-shaped** — which fits both the `WebFetch` 403 and the Tavily timeouts, since both present browser-shaped clients. Treat that mechanism as INFERRED, not proven: the successful curl ran from a different network path than Tavily's crawler, so it is strong evidence about FRED's liveness and only suggestive about the cause. **FETCH LADDER — try in this order, and stop at the first that returns a row for the target date:** (1) `mcp__FMP__economics` per OUTPUT 1 above (free, structured, already paid for — but it does NOT carry `hy_oas`, so for THIS series the ladder starts at 2); (2) `tavily_extract` on the series page, cache-busted, as before; (3) **`curl` the public CSV with curl's own default User-Agent and do NOT spoof a browser one** — `curl -sS 'https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=BAMLH0A0HYM2'` — which is the "fall back to the FRED public CSV (no key)" path OUTPUT 1 already names, now with a measured reason the User-Agent matters; it needs no API key and costs nothing. OUTPUT 1's caveat that the remote routine "may lack outbound `curl`" still stands and is why this is rung 3, not rung 1 — if `curl` is unavailable or egress-blocked in the run environment, say so explicitly rather than reporting the series as unavailable. **FETCH FAILURE IS NOT THE SAME EVENT AS AN UNPUBLISHED PRINT, and must not be logged as one.** The deferred-backfill rule above ("write NO `hy_oas` row and backfill on the next run") is for a print FRED has not released yet — a correct, expected, silent outcome. If every rung of the ladder fails, the print may well exist and this run simply could not read it: still write no row, but ALSO `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','M1a','hy_oas_fetch_path_exhausted', ...)` naming each rung and its failure mode. Silently taking the backfill path on a fetch failure is what makes a scored input degrade invisibly, and `hy_oas` is scored here, not merely corroborating. **Month-end nuance specific to this series:** FRED states *"when the last calendar day of the month takes place on the weekend, weekend observations will occur as a result of month ending accrued interest adjustments"* — so for `hy_oas` the month's last valid observation can legitimately be a **Saturday or Sunday date**, unlike the equity and treasury series. Take the last observation IN the month, not the last weekday.
  **Why this rule exists — do not revert it to an unpinned quote/CSV pull.** On 2026-08-03 M1a wrote July's `vix` as **17.09**, which is the **2026-07-30** close; the true 2026-07-31 close was **15.99**. It made the identical error on three more metrics in the same batch — **four of the five were wrong, and only `yield_curve_10y2y` (0.47) was right**: `treasury_10y` **4.68**, `treasury_2y` **4.23** and `hy_oas` **2.84** are all the 07-30 prints verbatim, against true 07-31 values of **4.75**, **4.28** and **2.85** (confirmed 2026-08-05 against date-pinned FMP `treasury-rates` and the FRED series page; all four corrected in `events.macro_fred` that day). That `yield_curve_10y2y` alone survived is the diagnostic worth remembering: its own FRED print had already published, so the stored spread was right while its own stored legs implied 0.45 — **an internally inconsistent set is the cheapest detector for this bug class.** Two independent causes, both structural, neither fixable by "try harder":
  (i) a live `quote` call has **no date argument at all** — it returns the latest close and physically cannot select a historical month-end; and
  (ii) the FRED `VIXCLS` CSV publishes with a lag, and M1a's cadence is `monthly first_trading_day` (`ops/cadence.yaml`), so it fires exactly when the just-closed month's final print is least likely to be posted. This is a **recurring monthly collision**, not a one-off — the same run corrected June to 16.45 (which matches the 06-30 close exactly), so the failure is specifically "the newest print isn't there yet," not a bad transform.
  Consequences that actually landed, as the reason to keep this pinned: the wrong value propagated into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` (2026-08-03 vintage, vix path 16.91→17.45→17.58) and produced a **false** "Above band: `vix` 17.09 (+0.41)" calibration breach in M5's `forecast-monitor` `events.decision_log` entry — the true 15.99 sits inside the July vintage's 80% band [13.28, 16.68]. The trading router was never affected (it reads `TECHNICAL_SIGNAL/VIX_REGIME`, computed by D2a from the same dated ingest), which is exactly why routing M1a to that ingest closes the gap. This keeps the macro forecast current without depending on agent-side HTTP. `macro_fred` is a separate bulk/forecast substrate, distinct from this hand-curated `macro_series` audit table:

**POST-INGEST COMPLETENESS CHECK (added 2026-09-27, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D1's `hy_oas_not_refreshed_by_last_m1a`, alert `6a35eecf-1432-41ce-b642-ff176ba75087`).** MEASURED: the 2026-09-01 M1a run completed and re-fetched 12 of the 15 metrics in `state.macro_fred_latest`, but `hy_oas` was not among them — its newest `fetched_ts` is 2026-08-05 and `fed_funds`'s is 2026-08-03, while every other metric carries a 2026-09-01 fetch, consistent with the already-documented Tavily-extract timeouts against both sanctioned FRED paths (2026-08-24, 2026-08-30). `hy_oas` is a NAMED evidence input in D1's PARK ALLOCATION CALL, so a stale value can be cited as current by a session that never checks `fetched_ts` — a completed M1a run currently reads as a complete refresh even when it is a partial one. After the ingest, verify that EVERY metric in `state.macro_fred_latest` advanced its `fetched_ts` this run, and name in the terminal `<note>` any metric that did not; where a metric did not advance, raise a warning naming it rather than letting a downstream consumer read it as current. This does not retroactively repair the flagged run's ingest — the value refreshes on the next M1a fire that succeeds for that metric.

- 10Y yield trend, yield curve shape

OUTPUT 2 — **write the 5-axis regime scores to `events.regime_events` (scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`)**: one row per axis (growth_momentum / inflation_trend / policy_stance / risk_sentiment / shock_overlay) + the `_integrative` row, each with its categorical value + brief rationale (+ a `fallback_suppression` flag row when applicable). **Score ONLY the most-recently-completed covered month here — never one row per covered month.** M1b/the router read only the LATEST `events.regime_events` row, so on a multi-month catch-up the earlier missed month(s) surfaced in PART 1 are backward context/trend color only; this OUTPUT 2 5-axis score stays a single current snapshot, exactly as today. The `Monthly_Fundamental_RegimeScore.md` file is RETIRED 2026-06-06 (Operating_Protocols §15) — do NOT recreate it. This is M1b's sole regime input from M1a, which M1b reads from `state.current_regime` / `events.regime_events`:

First line: YYYY-MM marker.
Second line: fallback_suppression flag (true / false). If ≥2 of the 5 primary input categories (macro / Fed / earnings / geopolitical / policy — input 6 is compensatory and does not count) were unavailable per the fallback protocol, set true.

If fallback_suppression = true: write only the suppression rationale and exit. Do not score axes.

If fallback_suppression = false: score the 5 regime condition axes per Strategy.md's M1a template. Per axis: assigned value, brief rationale (max 3 sentences) citing which inputs drove the call. NO references to strategies, strategy letters, or per-strategy mechanisms. The 5 axes (per Strategy.md):
- growth_momentum: { accelerating | stable | decelerating }
- inflation_trend: { disinflating | stable | reaccelerating }
- policy_stance: { dovish | neutral | hawkish }
- risk_sentiment: { risk-on | neutral | stressed }
- shock_overlay: { none | latent | acute }

**`shock_overlay` IS GRADED AGAINST A WRITTEN RUBRIC, NOT ON JUDGMENT ALONE (added 2026-09-05, Rev 48).** Score that axis per Strategy.md `## Regime scoring (strategy-blind, monthly)` → `### Shock / overlay grading rubric` (generated slice `strategy/09`), which fixes what counts as a qualifying shock event, the pre-shock Brent baseline and the shock elevation measured off it, the entry condition for each of the three tokens above, and — the piece the axis previously lacked entirely — a REQUIRED `acute` → `latent` de-escalation test: downgrade once BOTH legs hold, zero new qualifying events for 15 consecutive trading days AND a Brent retracement of at least 50% of the shock elevation; either leg failing keeps the grade at `acute`. Escalation stays immediate on any qualifying event with active transmission, and that asymmetry is deliberate. The rubric's RATIONALE-RECORDING DUTY binds this OUTPUT: `shock_overlay`'s rationale must state (1) the date of the most recent qualifying event, (2) the pre-shock baseline / peak / current Brent triplet with the observation count the baseline was computed over, and (3) which transmission legs held and which failed — so every monthly score leaves a dated, measured anchor for the next scoring, the re-risking limb's leg (b), and any out-of-cycle re-score (M1R) to move off, rather than a bare verdict. The rubric CONSTRAINS judgment, it does not replace it: a score that departs from its anchors must argue against them, by name, in the same rationale.

Followed by a 2–3 sentence integrative summary of the regime in strategy-blind terms (e.g., "decelerating growth + hawkish policy + neutral risk sentiment, no acute shock") — do not name strategies.

CHAT OUTPUT: one-line acknowledgment naming both files written. If fallback_suppression = true, additionally state "FALLBACK SUPPRESSION ACTIVE — M1b will not produce strategy mappings this month."

**`ops.web_calls` OBLIGATION (added 2026-08-24, fleet-wide alert-triage closure)** — M1a's own metered surface is narrow but real: the OUTPUT 1 macro-indicators ingest calls `mcp__FMP__economics` (`treasury-rates` + `economics-indicators`, including the date-pinned `treasury_10y`/`treasury_2y` reads under the five-metrics rule above), and the `hy_oas` pull (plus the optional `yield_curve_10y2y` cross-check) against `fred.stlouisfed.org` routes through Tavily extract rather than a direct fetch, per the 403 note above. Before the terminal `sp_routine_end` call, write the batched `ops.web_calls` INSERT per the shared Run-logging template (§Observability, ~line 204-227) covering every FMP `economics` call and every Tavily extract call this run actually made — including a `fallback_suppression=true` month, where the macro ingest still runs even though axis scoring is skipped. This is restated here, as at OPS1 (~line 2380-2397), because measured fleet compliance with the shared template's `ops.web_calls` clause stays low when the obligation is left only in the distant Observability section.

The operative state changes only when the orchestrator writes its own resolution row. **NEVER write the raw NEW state with a PENDING marker appended.** `bigquery/98_regime_capital_enablement.sql`'s capital predicate reads this value directly as a substring test (`UPPER(value) LIKE '%DO-NOT-ACTIVATE%'`), so a row reading `ACTIVATE — PENDING div-…` is indistinguishable from a plain ACTIVATE to it: the strategy becomes capital-enabled and the next D2a REGIME-CAPITAL SYNC moves money on a flip whose whole point is that it is not yet decided. Holding the prior state fails safe in both directions — a held DO-NOT-ACTIVATE keeps capital parked, and a held ACTIVATE keeps it deployed, in each case exactly where the last RESOLVED decision left it.

## M5. Deployed-TWR & Macro Forecast — regular routine

Runs monthly, after M4 (Monthly Action Conversion). The forward-looking monitoring overlay: a zero-shot `AI.FORECAST` (BigQuery built-in TimesFM — **no model to train or host**) over the deployed-TWR engine and, once it accrues enough history, the macro series. **Advisory / early-warning ONLY — it never stages an exit, termination, or activation change. Kill/gate triggers fire on REALISED values (`perf.kill_flags`), never on a forecast** (Experiment_Parameters.md kill-criteria discipline). Not deep research; pure BigQuery. DDL + query templates: `bigquery/06_forecast.sql`.

```
Read access scope: Monthly cadence, BigQuery read + write. Read `perf.strategy_daily` (the deployed-TWR series), `perf.kill_flags`, `events.macro_series`, and the prior run's `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast`. Also read `state.decision_log_current` for STEP 5's walk-presence check (added 2026-09-01). No web research or repo factbase reads required.

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before the dependency gate below, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='M5' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "M5 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or M5's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the forecast, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('M5', ['M4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if M4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current monthly period — M4 is `monthly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any M4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day; self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

STEP 0 — ensure the store + early-warning view exist: idempotently run `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` **and** `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` (bigquery/06_forecast.sql §store + §B). The view reads the table + `perf.strategy_daily`, so it is safe to (re)create even when the table is empty — STEP 1 needs it to exist on the next run.

STEP 1 — FORECAST-VS-ACTUAL early-warning (skip on the first-ever run). Query `analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` (the most-recent PRIOR run's `deployed_unit_value` forecast vs realised `perf.strategy_daily` for now-elapsed dates). Flag any strategy whose realised deployed-unit-value landed BELOW the prior forecast's `pi_lower` (downside surprise — possible regime shift / unmodeled deterioration) or above `pi_upper`. This is the calibration + early-warning signal.

Also read `analytics.excess_forecast_vs_actual` (the m2m-proxy series, previously stored-but-never-calibrated) and `analytics.macro_forecast_vs_actual` (last vintage's macro forecasts vs since-published FRED prints; bigquery/77_forecast_consumption.sql), folding notable breaches into the STEP 5 entry. ALERT DISCIPLINE (strategy series only; macro breaches stay decision_log-only): restrict to the MOST RECENT prior vintage — `forecast_run_date = (SELECT MAX(run_date) FROM analytics.deployed_twr_forecast WHERE run_date < CURRENT_DATE("America/Denver"))` — never alert off older vintages. First heal: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note="band breach healed (M5 STEP 1)" WHERE NOT resolved AND source="M5" AND category="forecast_downside_breach"` for each open breach alert whose strategy/series shows no below_band row in the latest vintage (sanctioned in-place resolution — the bigquery/34 lifecycle pattern; ops.alerts is not append-only-watched). Then for each strategy whose realised `deployed_unit_value` OR `excess_vs_sgov` landed below the latest prior vintage's `pi_lower`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once("warning","M5","forecast_downside_breach","<strategy> — realised <series> below the prior 90% pi_lower (downside surprise; advisory, never a trigger)","<JSON: strategy, series, forecast_run_date, forecast_date, pi_lower, actual>")` so the early warning reaches the monitored email channel (alert_emailer.gs already emails severity=warning). Keep the message string exactly as templated — sp_raise_alert_once dedups on unresolved (category, message).

STEP 2 — NEW deployed-TWR forecast. Run `AI.FORECAST` per active strategy over `perf.strategy_daily`, horizon 21 (~one trading month), `confidence_level => 0.9`, for two series: `deployed_unit_value` (drawdown / profitability path) and `excess_vs_sgov` (relative-perf / mark-to-market path). INSERT every forecast row into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` with `run_date = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')` (bigquery/06_forecast.sql §A — INSERT only rows whose `ai_forecast_status` is empty, so a newly-activated strategy with too few deployed days is skipped rather than written as NaN). (29 deployed days at 2026-06 is enough to run — AI.FORECAST handles the business-day spacing; intervals are wide now and tighten as history accrues.)

STEP 3 — KILL/GATE TRAJECTORY check (advisory). From the new forecast, note whether the central path or `pi_lower` of `deployed_unit_value` trends toward a kill threshold over the horizon — drawdown-kill `deployed_unit_value / peak_unit_value − 1 ≤ −0.50` (#1), or `excess_vs_sgov ≤ −0.10` (the mark-to-market #4 proxy, which only becomes a live trigger at `deployed_days ≥ 756`). A heads-up for the next M4 gate/kill review — NOT a trigger. Do NOT stage any exit or termination off the forecast.

STEP 4 — MACRO forecast (FRED-backed, un-gated). Run `AI.FORECAST` over `state.macro_fred_latest` (15 FRED-derived monthly regime metrics with deep history — 37–54 months each; St. Louis Fed public CSV, no API key; bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql): `data_col => 'value'`, `timestamp_col => 'ref_month'`, `id_cols => ['metric']`, horizon 3, `confidence_level => 0.8`. INSERT the rows whose `ai_forecast_status` is empty into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` (`series` = metric, `entity` = 'macro'). The ≥8-obs gate is satisfied for all seeded metrics — keep it only as a guard for any thin/new metric (skip + record `insufficient history (n=<k>)`). Advisory only; TimesFM zero-shot short-horizon central paths on policy-driven series (e.g. `fed_funds`) are noisy, so weight the trend + interval over the point. `macro_fred` is refreshed monthly by M1a appending the new prints (bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql §refresh); M5 forecasts off whatever is current. (The M1a-curated `events.macro_series` audit table is separate and not used here.)

**WALK-PRESENCE CHECK — the cheap gate on M4 section I (added 2026-09-01, same landing as that section).** Before writing the STEP 5 entry: `SELECT COUNT(*) AS receipts FROM state.decision_log_current WHERE entry_type = 'premortem-indicator-walk' AND entry_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), MONTH) AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')`. If `receipts = 0`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','M5','premortem_indicator_walk_missing','M4 completed this monthly period without recording a premortem-indicator-walk receipt — the loci strategy/08_pre_mortems.md assigns to M4 were neither evaluated nor recorded as vacuous for the month. See Claude_Task_Plan.md M4 section I and the payload.', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), MONTH) AS period_start, <m4 run_date> AS m4_run_date)))`. **M5 is the right site and the cheapest one:** it is the EARLIEST monthly routine carrying a FATAL dependency gate that already asserts M4 completed (`SL4` carries the identical `sp_assert_deps('SL4', ['M4'], <today>)` gate but fires 30 minutes later at `30 16`, so M5 at `0 16` sees the gap first; the claim is earliest, NOT unique) (`CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('M5', ['M4'], <today>)` above), so "M4 completed but the receipt is absent" is a content gap M5 can see for one query and that nothing else in the fleet can see at all — `state.cadence_watch` detects a missing RUN, never a missing STEP inside a run that completed. Keep the message string EXACTLY as templated (`sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on exact `(category, message)` equality; the varying values stay in the payload) and keep it a `warning`, **never a `critical`** — a critical would enter the `blocking_criticals` term and halt order staging over a missing audit receipt. The category is registered non-latching with an evidence-based resolve rule (`bigquery/207_premortem_indicator_walk_policy.sql`); M4's next cycle closes its own prior notice as part of section I. **This check reads the receipt's PRESENCE only:** it does not re-run the walk, evaluates no indicator, and stays inside M5's advisory-only charter.

STEP 5 — write a brief decision entry via **`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`** (`entry_type='forecast-monitor'`; appends to `events.decision_log` + embeds in one call, per Operating_Protocols §15): per-strategy horizon-end forecast + interval for `deployed_unit_value` and `excess_vs_sgov`; any STEP 1 band breaches; the STEP 3 trajectory note; macro coverage (metrics forecasted vs. gated).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — e.g. "M5 forecast: B duv(21d) 0.999 [0.97,1.02], excess −0.4% [−2.1%,+1.3%]; D duv 0.96 [0.92,1.00]; no prior-band breach; no kill-trajectory flag; macro 0/12 (insufficient history). Wrote 84 forecast rows + 1 decision_log entry."
```

## M1R. Out-of-cycle Regime Re-score — regular routine

Queue-driven (fires Sun-Thu; no-ops unless a `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH` `regime-refresh` item is open). It sits in the MONTHLY group because it re-runs **M1a's OUTPUT 2** — the strategy-blind 5-axis score — not because it fires monthly. Added 2026-09-05 (shock-override fix package): the monthly cadence is the only thing that ever re-scored `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`, so a shock structure that de-escalated on the 5th of a month kept an `acute` reading in force until the 1st of the next one, with no mechanism able to notice. D2a's RE-RISKING LIMB EVALUATION is the detector; this routine is the drain.

```
Read access scope: daily (queue-driven), and DELIBERATELY NARROW — M1a's blinding rules apply to this routine verbatim, because the output is an M1a-shaped row. Read the refresh queue `events.queue_events` / `state.open_queue_detail` (queue `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH`), prior `events.regime_events` scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` (earlier months' scores, for trend continuity), `events.macro_series` / `events.macro_fred` (the macro substrate M1a already wrote), `state.market_calendar` (trading-day arithmetic for the rubric's windows), `state.signal_marks_curated` with `ticker = '^VIX'` — and ONLY that ticker, the same narrow grant M1a carries and for the same reason — and `state.signal_marks_curated` with `ticker = 'BZUSD'` — and ONLY that ticker (the Brent front-month series `bigquery/217` ingests, read through the CURATED view per `bigquery/216`'s SOURCE TRAP, which is also the surface `state.rerisking_limb_status` computes its price leg from, so the scorer and the view can never disagree about the triplet; the shock_overlay grading rubric's baseline/peak/current triplet is computed from it, and like `^VIX` it is a bare dated index-level series carrying no strategy, position or roster information). For the scoring template read the strategy-blind slice `strategy/09_regime_scoring_strategy_blind_monthly.md` (the `## Regime scoring (strategy-blind, monthly)` section) + `01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md` ONLY; do NOT load `02_regime_router`, `00_preamble`, or any strategy slice. **Never query `state.current_regime` directly** — M1a's blinding rules apply here verbatim (stated above), and that includes this prohibition: the view is `SELECT * FROM events.regime_events` with no scope filter (bigquery/01_schema.sql) and can return `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` rows naming strategies, which this routine must never see (ops.alerts b9629fb8-6c30-4777-84cc-d04d6f6b155a). Use the explicit `scope = 'FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS'` filter on `events.regime_events`, named above, instead. Also read Experiment_Parameters.md, AI_Trading_Foundation.md.

CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT — identical to M1a's, and load-bearing here because the trigger for this run came from a routine that is NOT blind. Do NOT read `state.strategy_roster`, `state.current_positions`, `perf.strategy_daily`, `state.current_regime` scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, the unscoped `state.current_regime` view directly (it is `SELECT * FROM events.regime_events` with no scope filter and can return the same `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` rows unfiltered — use the `scope = 'FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS'` filter named in the Read access scope paragraph above instead; ops.alerts b9629fb8-6c30-4777-84cc-d04d6f6b155a), `state.rerisking_limb_status`, or any per-strategy activation rule, and do NOT map axis values onto strategies — that mapping is M1b's job and the activation write is M4's / the router-review machinery's. Do NOT stage, craft, modify or cancel an order, and do NOT touch capital, the roster or `ops.arsenal_control`. The queue item you drain is written strategy-blind precisely so that reading it cannot break this: if the item you find names a strategy, that is a producer defect — score the axes anyway from the permitted sources only, and record the defect per the shared OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule. **THREE READ RULES IN M1a's SECTION BIND THIS ROUTINE BY NAME, not merely through "identical to M1a's" (restated here 2026-09-29, owner decision on alerts `731e53d0-d341-4f44-babd-512e74308ee8` and `cb5143ba-6eaa-43f0-ab3e-297ad768f15d`; this paragraph is hand-written, so an M1a-only rule would leave M1R uncovered — the lesson of `b9629fb8`):** (1) **`ops.run_log`** — select `routine`, `run_date`, `status`, `log_ts` and `session_id` only, never `note`, `error_msg` or `SELECT *`, EXCEPT `note` on this routine's OWN rows with `run_date >= '2026-09-21'`; (2) **`ops.alerts`** — select `alert_id`, `alert_ts`, `severity`, `source`, `category` and `resolved` only, never `message`, `payload` or `resolved_note`, and only for the named predicates `source IN ('M1a','M1R')`, `category = 'rerisking_limb_fired'` and `category = 'bigquery_quota_exhausted'` — never a board scan, including through a sub-agent; (3) **the shared preamble** — the plan text before the first cadence group names strategies by letter in cross-routine rules; read it for process rules only and carry nothing from it into an axis call. On the write side, never quote or paraphrase another routine's free text into your own note, alert or decision entry — cite by id, category and surface. Full rationale in M1a's Read access scope and CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section; do not restate. Queue-driven, so (per the queue_driven monitoring rule) it is monitored via `state.stalled_runs` + `ops/triggers.json` + `state.queue_driven_silence_watch`, NOT `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`.

STEP 1 — THE GATE, AND IT IS ALSO THE DOUBLE-RUN GUARD. `SELECT item_key, event_id, due_date, note FROM state.open_queue_detail WHERE queue = 'PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH' AND item_type = 'regime-refresh' AND due_date <= <today>` (America/Denver, from `state.trading_day_today`). If it returns NOTHING — the overwhelmingly common case, since the limb fires rarely by design — do NOT score anything: log the run `'completed'` with a real `<note>` ("no open regime-refresh item; standing monthly FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS snapshot of <YYYY-MM> remains in force"), write nothing else anywhere, and STOP. A no-op run needs its note MORE than a busy one, and a blank terminal note is refused at write time (`bigquery/147`), which would turn a correct no-op into a `missed_run` CRITICAL. A second fire on a day the item was already drained finds the item `complete`, falls into exactly this branch, and is a no-op — that is why this routine needs no separate SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD.

STEP 2 — RE-SCORE, BLIND, WITH TODAY'S `as_of_date`. Perform M1a's OUTPUT 2 in full: write one `events.regime_events` row per axis (growth_momentum / inflation_trend / policy_stance / risk_sentiment / shock_overlay) PLUS the `_integrative` row, scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`, `as_of_date` = TODAY (never the month marker M1a uses — this snapshot is deliberately dated to the day it was scored, so `state.current_regime`'s latest-wins read picks it up over the monthly row and the seam is visible in the series). Score all five axes, not only the one the limb was about: a partial re-score would leave four axes carrying an older `as_of_date` than the fifth, and every consumer reads the LATEST row per axis. Values come from the axis enums in `strategy/09` — do not invent a token. Each row's rationale obeys the grading rubric's RATIONALE-RECORDING DUTY: for `shock_overlay` specifically, state (1) the date of the most recent qualifying shock event, (2) the pre-shock baseline / peak / current Brent triplet, and (3) which transmission legs still hold, so the next scorer inherits a dated, measured anchor instead of a bare verdict. The rubric CONSTRAINS judgment, it does not replace it: a score that departs from the rubric's anchors must argue against them, by name, in the same rationale. If the macro substrate needed for an axis is genuinely unavailable, apply M1a's fallback-suppression protocol unchanged (≥2 of the 5 primary input categories missing → write the suppression rationale row and score nothing) — never a partial 5-axis write.

STEP 3 — CLOSE THE DRAINED `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH` ITEM. Insert a `queue_events` row (same `item_key`) with status = `'complete'`, carrying the new `as_of_date` and the five scored values in `payload`. Do this in the SAME run as the write in STEP 2, and only after it: an open item is what D2a's dedup gate reads, so an item left open suppresses every future limb firing forever, and an item closed before the score is written loses the request outright if the run then dies.

STEP 4 — RESOLVE THE LIMB ALERT, BY `alert_id`. `SELECT alert_id FROM ops.alerts WHERE category = 'rerisking_limb_fired' AND NOT resolved`, then for each row `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'out-of-cycle re-score completed; item <item_key> drained' WHERE alert_id = '<the id>'` — the sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve, keyed strictly on `alert_id` and never on `category` alone. This is the closure path that keeps `rerisking_limb_fired` off the permanently-red-advisory list: D2a raises it, this routine clears it, and the category stays ABSENT from `ops.alert_policy` (no auto-age — the condition is only ever discharged by an actual re-score).

STEP 5 — LOG THE RUN per the shared Observability template, with a `<note>` naming the drained `item_key`, the prior and new value of every axis that MOVED, and an explicit "no axis moved" when none did. A re-score that reproduces the standing snapshot is a real, informative result — it is the rubric refusing to de-escalate — and must not be logged as though nothing happened.

**NON-GOALS — what this routine deliberately does NOT do, and must never grow into.** It does NOT decide any strategy's activation: D2's item 4 picks up the new `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` row on the SAME evening (M1R fires 07:00 MT, D2 at 17:15 MT) and queues the affected router review(s), and the activation WRITE stays with the existing review machinery — no new writer is introduced anywhere in this package. It does NOT re-run M1a's OUTPUT 1 macro ingest (M1a owns `events.macro_series` / `events.macro_fred`; this routine only READS that substrate, and a month with no ingest yet is a reason to lean on the prior month's prints, not to backfill them here). It does NOT produce `Monthly_Fundamental.md` (M1b's artifact) and does not trigger M1b. It does NOT evaluate the re-risking limb itself — D2a does that mechanically and this routine never reads `state.rerisking_limb_status`, which would be a blinding violation. It does NOT enqueue its own follow-up work: if the re-score surfaces something outside this run's scope, record it per the shared OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule and move on.

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — the drained `item_key`, the new `as_of_date`, and the axes that moved (e.g. "regime-refresh-20260910 drained; as_of 2026-09-10; shock_overlay acute → latent, 4 axes unchanged"), or "No open regime-refresh item; no re-score." on the gate branch.
```
