5. Dominant macro narrative
- One or two themes dominating market commentary
- Inflection points (data, Fed actions, geopolitical events) shifting the narrative

6. Earnings and fundamentals backdrop
- Aggregate beat rates and surprise magnitudes for earnings seasons within the quarter
- Change in forward S&P 500 EPS consensus
- Sector-level earnings divergences

7. Overall regime characterization (3–5 sentences)

The in-use model is whichever model the OWNER configured on the remote-routine triggers — read `ops/cadence.yaml`'s top-level **`routine_model`** key, corroborate against `OWNER_ACTIONS.md` and (if the `RemoteTrigger` connector is available) a `get` on a trigger id from `ops/trigger_ids.json`. Then gather Section 1 / Section 3a evidence at **four widening levels, reporting ALL FOUR** — because research on the exact deployed model is usually gated or too slow to exist yet, and counting only deployed-model evidence would discard nearly everything:
- **L1** — the deployed model exactly. **L2** — the same model line, any version (classify by capability class, not literal name). **L3** — any Anthropic/Claude model. **L4** — non-Anthropic models and autoregressive-LLM-general claims.
- **Do not confuse L1–L4 with the foundation's Tier 1 / Tier 2**, which classify items as architectural-vs-empirical. Orthogonal axes.
- **The weight ordering applies to MAGNITUDES only.** For Tier 1 architectural/existence claims, L4 generality evidence is the appropriate and often strongest class — do not discount it for being off-model.
- Give each item a **cross-level verdict** (CONVERGENT / LEVEL-SPLIT / VERSION-VOLATILE / SPARSE) and a one-line transfer assessment. VERSION-VOLATILE within L2 means a neighbouring version's number does **not** transfer to the deployed model regardless of how much L3/L4 evidence exists.
- The hierarchy **refines weighting and reporting; it is NOT a gate and adds no bar of its own, including for reductions.** §5.5 guardrail 2 is satisfied by Claude replication (L1/L2/L3) *or* an architectural-generality argument (L4) — so an L3-only or L4-only reduction clears it as the foundation currently writes it, and §5.5's own closing rule exempts direct research findings from the guardrails entirely. **Do not impose a stricter standard than §5.5 codifies.** For a reduction, REPORT the level and cross-level verdict alongside the §5.5 guardrail results so the downstream §5.3/§5.6 machinery can see what a relaxation rests on; if you judge the bar too permissive, emit a PART 2 proposal to amend **§5.5 guardrail 2** (not §5.4 — that is a magnitude-threshold table with no provenance condition) rather than applying a tighter rule on this run.
- This quarterly slice supersedes the legacy "transferability filter" wording elsewhere in this routine where the two disagree: classify evidence as L1–L4 and apply §5.5 as written; do not run two parallel transferability schemes.
- Claude-specific evidence is **not on Hugging Face** — use Anthropic system cards, `anthropic.com`, `platform.claude.com` deprecation pages, and independent third-party evaluators. A general paper whose panel happens to include a Claude model is L2/L3 evidence; check panels rather than assuming L4.

Frame research adversarially: look for evidence that contradicts or updates documented edges and disadvantages, not evidence that confirms them. Offsets self-reference bias (this task evaluates LLM claims while being executed by an LLM).

Transferability filter for non-Claude evidence. For PART 1 findings drawn from models other than Claude (Sections 2, 3, 5), a finding triggers per-strategy foundation-change assessment only if at least one of the following is present: (a) replication on a Claude model, (b) architectural generality — the mechanism is a documented property of autoregressive LLMs broadly rather than a specific model's training artifact, or (c) evidence from an Anthropic-family model (prior Claude version). Non-Claude findings lacking transferability evidence are logged in the YES/NO answer and flagged as watch items for the next review cycle, but do not trigger foundation-change assessment on their own.

Verification questions (per AI_Trading_Foundation.md Part 4):
Q1 — Has any AI capability in Part 1 materially changed? (Tier 1 by structural change, or Tier 2 by measurement update.)
Q2 — Has any AI disadvantage in Part 2 been reduced or eliminated by capability changes? (Triggers constraint-relaxation review per Experiment_Parameters.md if reduction is material AND the strategy has constraints flowing from the reduced disadvantage.)
Q3 — Has any new disadvantage emerged that is not listed?
Q4 — Have any Part 3a questions been resolved by accumulated evidence?
Q5 — Has market saturation changed in a way that shifts edge accessibility?
Q6 — Has a synchronized-AI market event occurred in the prior quarter?
Q7 — Have calibration records confirmed or refuted any edge or disadvantage claim?
Q8 — Has new research surfaced specific new failure modes or confirmed edges?

Note: rev 3 dropped the previous Q8 ("model deprecation or version update") from triggering refresh — version changes follow a separate protocol per AI_Trading_Foundation.md Part 4 §"Version-change protocol" (no early refresh; flip Tier 2 to version-pending; quarterly delta picks up version-specific research as it emerges).

Per YES: (a) evidence triggering the yes, (b) whether the evidence clears the transferability filter (if non-Claude), (c) which Tier the affected item is (Tier 1 architectural / Tier 2 magnitude), (d) strategies affected, (e) which foundation-change-assessment branch is warranted (continue / terminate / constraint-relaxation per Experiment_Parameters.md §Foundation change trigger).
STRATEGY-ARSENAL BRANCHES (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive). Beyond the per-strategy continue / terminate / constraint-relaxation effects above, emit two machine-readable arsenal branches in PART 2's actionable-outputs table, consumed autonomously (no "recommendation for A3 / participant" dead-end):

- **strategy-retirement.** If the evidence is a sustained edge-decay short of a mechanical foundation-change terminate, surface it as an SL4-consumable signal (recorded in the actionable-outputs table + `events.decision_log`), written via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` (same structured `fields` shape as Q1: strategy_code + signal_class + evidence), `in_source_session` = this run's own `<session_id>` (per PART 2's WRITE-ONCE bullet above — NOT a per-quarter "`Q3 <date>`" label), rather than a participant recommendation; SL4 evaluates it monthly against `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (default-KEEP, affirmative RETIRE required). **IDEMPOTENCY:** before this CALL, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events.decision_log WHERE entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal' AND strategy=<code> AND source_session=<this run's session_id>`; skip the CALL if `>= 1`.

Warning, never critical: an open critical feeds state.trading_enabled blocking_criticals (bigquery/107) and an unexplained prompt edit must not halt trading by itself. Note the honest limit — this attributes to a DECLARED actor, not an authenticated one, so it is a detective control against accident, drift and unannounced edits, in the same posture as bigquery/scheduled_queries/safety_critical_dml_watch.sql. NO ATTRIBUTION COMES FROM THE VENDOR API, so do not spend a sweep looking for it there (recorded 2026-08-21): the API exposes `updated_at` but carries no actor/author field anywhere in its response, so on its own an out-of-band edit is DATED but never attributed — which is exactly the gap the observation/intent pair above closes on our side — a session that notices an unexplained `updated_at` bump cannot learn from the API who made it. Treat the bump itself as NEITHER evidence of intrusion NOR of safety; the only question that can be answered, and the one that matters, is whether the live text still matches the canonical in clause (b), which this sweep already answers and corrects for every routine regardless of who or what changed it.
     - INSTRUCTION drift (any cohort) → SELF-CORRECT: `RemoteTrigger update(<trigger_id>)` with a body containing ONLY the instruction field set to the FULL canonical string from `ops/routine_backup.json` (core one-liner + the standing operator paragraphs — never the bare `ops/triggers.json` core line, which would strip them; never include schedule fields in this call), then `RemoteTrigger get` again to confirm the round-trip. `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','Q4','trigger_drift_corrected','<routine> — instruction drifted — restored from ops/routine_backup.json via RemoteTrigger update','<JSON: routine, field:"instruction", live_value, canonical_value>')` plus an `events.decision_log` entry (`entry_type='trigger-audit'`, per-routine diff summary).

On success, raise the same info `trigger_drift_corrected` alert + decision_log entry as the instruction case; if `cron_utc` was still `TO_POPULATE`, commit the newly-observed value into `ops/cadence.yaml` (bootstrap, not drift).
     - SCHEDULE drift on a `daily`/`weekly` routine → NEVER `RemoteTrigger update` the schedule (these are native Daily/Weekly-picker triggers; `RemoteTrigger get` renders them as UTC crons while the live trigger is DST-aware — a raw cron write risks demoting one to a fixed-UTC Custom trigger, recreating the 2026-07-10 incident class). Instead `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','Q4','trigger_drift','<routine> — schedule drifted (live <x> vs canonical time_local <y>) — NEVER auto-corrected on a daily/weekly trigger; paste this schedule + instruction into the web-UI trigger manually','<JSON: routine, field:"schedule", live_value, canonical_value>')`, with the exact canonical schedule + instruction in the message so the fix is a single owner paste.
     - A routine with an `expected_trigger` but ABSENT from `ops/trigger_ids.json`, a `get` that errors on a recorded id (deleted/recreated trigger), or a disabled trigger: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','Q4','trigger_missing_live','<routine> — no live trigger reachable; recreate with schedule <expected_trigger> + instruction <ops/triggers.json text>, then record its trig_ id in ops/trigger_ids.json','<JSON>')` — NEVER auto-enable or auto-create a trigger from this step.
     - **FLEET-MODEL DRIFT — END-OF-SWEEP RAISE / RESOLVE (added 2026-09-28; clause (d) above).** On 2026-09-28 the whole 33-routine fleet was switched live to a new model of record with zero repo record and nothing flagged it: this sweep diffed schedule, instruction, enabled and `allowed_tools` presence but never the model, and D3's MODEL-OF-RECORD DOC SYNC reads only `routine_model`, so a stale `routine_model` made D3 see "already equal" and no-op. Only a human-run interactive sweep caught it. If ANY fleet routine's live model differs from `routine_model`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','<Q4|OPS0>','fleet_model_drift','Live fleet trigger model differs from ops/cadence.yaml routine_model — confirm with RemoteTrigger get, then bring the stale side forward (routine_model + check-N mirrors + routine_backup ingest)','<JSON: routine_model, mismatched routines with their live model>')`. **THE MESSAGE IS THAT FIXED LITERAL** — `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on exact `(category, message)`, so no model ids, counts, dates or routine names may enter it (they belong in the payload), and it carries no apostrophe. On a clean model comparison across every routine in `ops/trigger_ids.json` (a routine whose `get` failed is no evidence — leave the alert open), resolve: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='clean sweep: every fleet trigger model equals routine_model' WHERE category='fleet_model_drift' AND NOT resolved`. This sweep only reports: bringing the stale side forward is a repo edit by an interactive session or the owner.
     - NEVER call `RemoteTrigger run` from this step — re-firing missed routines is exclusively OPS0's job (its readiness view enforces the order-staging exclusion list; step E has no such rail).
   - **FALLBACK 1 (only if `RemoteTrigger get` errors for ALL ids this session — a tool outage, not per-id staleness):** the prior Claude-in-Chrome read-and-diff branch — read each trigger's schedule + Name/Instructions field verbatim in the console, diff the same way against `expected_trigger` / `ops/triggers.json`, and for any drift found `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','Q4','trigger_drift', '<routine — what drifted and by how much>', '<JSON>')`, noting in the decision_log entry that the next session with RemoteTrigger access must apply the self-correct procedure above — not left to the owner.
   - **FALLBACK 2 (both surfaces unavailable this session):** `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','Q4','trigger_audit_needs_chrome', 'Quarterly web-UI trigger audit could not run this cycle (no RemoteTrigger or Chrome/console access) — retry from a session with one of those available before the next quarter.', '<JSON: quarter, last_audit_date_from_cadence_yaml, drift_classes_uncovered:["schedule","allowed_tools"]>')` — now WARNING (emailed); the old info-severity version of this alert was never emailed and is retired. **`drift_classes_uncovered` SCOPED to exactly these two (corrected 2026-08-10, established gap-audit) — do NOT list `instruction` or `enabled` here even though this specific sweep also skipped them.** Both of those two already have independent, headless coverage elsewhere in the system that runs regardless of whether this quarterly (or OPS0's weekly-mirrored) sweep ever executes: `instruction` drift is caught NIGHTLY by `state.instruction_drift` (built from `ops.run_log.instruction`, `bigquery/15_routine_catalog.sql`) via `ops.sp_sq_cadence_check`'s `instruction_drift` WARNING block, and `enabled`/deleted-trigger drift has real, if LAGGED, headless coverage via `state.trigger_attestation`/`state.cadence_watch` (`trigger_missing`/`missed_run`/`period_missed`) — a silently disabled trigger surfaces within its monitor class's own gap window with zero sweeps required. Only `schedule` (cron expression content) and `allowed_tools`/model (job_config content) have NO BigQuery visibility at all — this sweep and its Chrome-console fallback are the ONLY coverage either class has, so those two alone are the genuine blind spot this alert should claim; naming all four overstates it and would misdirect a future audit into thinking `instruction`/`enabled` drift goes fully unmonitored between quarters, which is false. **DO NOT word this alert as a request to re-apply `allowed_tools` or to "re-diagnose the config" (rev 2026-07-27).** That remediation is verified futile: `OWNER_ACTIONS.md` item U applied `RemoteTrigger` to all 30 then-existing triggers on 2026-07-19 with live echo-verification (commit `5a39d38`), and its own same-day addendum plus `ops/RUNBOOK.md` §15b record that headless/scheduled sessions still lack the tool **at the platform level regardless of what any trigger's `allowed_tools` lists**. An alert that asks the owner to re-apply a verified-applied, verified-insufficient config sends them on an errand that cannot succeed, every single time it fires. State the actual position instead: the sweep could not run because this is a scheduled session; the config is correct and is not the cause; the only real fix is platform-level (`RemoteTrigger` exposed to headless sessions, or a server-side trigger-audit API); and the working interim path is a manual sweep from an INTERACTIVE session, which does retain the tool. **PARTIAL-SWEEP NOTE (2026-07-27; CORRECTED 2026-09-07 — it is no longer partial):** an interactive session's `mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers` returns id / name / `cron_expression` / `enabled` / `ended_reason` / `suspension_reason` / `next_run_at`, **and also `derived_state.prompt` — the FULL live instruction text, standing operator paragraphs included — plus `session_request.config.allowed_tools`, `model` and `environment_id`.** Its cursor pagination also works (`has_more` / `next_cursor` page the whole fleet, not a first page). So it covers EVERY drift class this step audits, not a subset. The previous wording — "It does NOT return the instruction text or `allowed_tools`, so those two classes still require the full `RemoteTrigger get`" — was MEASURED FALSE on 2026-09-07 by a session that swept all 33 fleet routines on instruction, schedule and enabled through this tool alone, with no `RemoteTrigger` and no Chrome (`events.decision_log` `entry_type='trigger-audit'`, 2026-09-06 cycle: 33 checked, 0 drift). **That false premise is the direct cause of the 13-day observation gap alert `d5d3905a` measured** — sessions read this note, concluded a full sweep was out of reach, and recorded nothing. So when `RemoteTrigger` is absent, sweep with `list_triggers` and treat it as a FULL sweep; say in the alert which classes were covered, and note that only the `allowed_tools` SELF-HEAL still needs `RemoteTrigger update` — the allowed_tools CHECK does not. The same wording rule and the same partial-sweep option apply to OPS0 STEP 3, which mirrors this ladder verbatim.
   - Any branch: log the outcome (audited-via-api / audited-via-chrome / needs-chrome) to `events.decision_log` alongside the D. entry above, with checked/corrected/warned counts.

DEFERRAL DISCIPLINE: deferrals don't chain. Conservative-default fallback per deferred decision.

CALENDAR MCP USAGE: Q4 creates no calendar events — its analyses are enqueued to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`) and run by D2. Anchor dated due_dates on the America/Denver date. Time zone per Experiment_Parameters.md.

CHAT OUTPUT:

- One-line acknowledgment of file edits and `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue entries enqueued.

If no file changes, no queue entries: "No actions required."

# ANNUAL (first trading day of January, or experiment anniversary month if January-anchoring isn't operationally clean)

A1, A2 are deep-research routines; A3 (action conversion) runs after A1 and A2 are saved.

## A1. AI Foundation Annual Full Re-Derivation — deep research

```
**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='A1' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "A1 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or A1's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the re-derivation, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

Read access scope: Annual cadence. Read everything, including full `events.decision_log` history (queryable, no live/archive split, §15).

Read AI_Trading_Foundation.md (Parts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in full — pay particular attention to the Tier framework distinction and to §5.4/§5.5), Experiment_Parameters.md, Operating_Protocols.md, the CURRENT `Quarterly_AI_Foundation_Delta.md`, and the prior `Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md` if one exists (positions from `state.current_positions`, regime from `state.current_regime`, decisions from `events.decision_log`). **Do NOT read `Strategy.md` whole** — it is ~366 KB and would consume most of the context budget before research starts; per the slice-map above, load `strategy/01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md` + `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` (the pre-mortems carry the per-strategy foundation-citation graph PART 2 needs) and pull an individual `strategy/0N_strategy_<x>.md` slice only if a specific per-strategy question requires it. **Note the quarterly delta is a single overwritten file** — there is no series of "prior year's outputs" to read; earlier cycles' findings live in `events.hf_capability_captures` and `events.decision_log`, which are queryable and are the correct source for prior-cycle context.

**STEP A — MODEL OF RECORD. Establish this FIRST, before any capability research (owner directive 2026-07-28).** The foundation document describes the capabilities and limitations of **the model this experiment actually runs**, which is whichever model the OWNER configured on the remote-routine triggers — NOT the newest or most capable model Anthropic has released. Those are routinely different, and conflating them would make the entire document describe a model the experiment does not use. **All remote routines always run the SAME model** (standing owner invariant), so there is one answer, not one per routine.

Read `ops/cadence.yaml`'s top-level **`routine_model`** key — that is the version-controlled record of the owner's choice. Corroborate against `OWNER_ACTIONS.md` and, if the `RemoteTrigger` connector is available in-session, a `get` on any routine's trigger id from `ops/trigger_ids.json` (the live trigger config is ground truth; `routine_model` is a mirror of it and is the thing that is stale if they disagree — say so explicitly and flag it for the owner rather than silently preferring either). Do **NOT** infer the in-use model from this session's own self-reported identity alone, and do **NOT** assume it is the current frontier model. If `routine_model` is absent or unreadable, say so plainly, fall back to the corroborating sources, and state the assumption you proceeded under rather than guessing a version. Also report any of the four known hardcoded model-id sites that disagree with it: `ops/cadence.yaml` `routine_model`, the OPS2 trigger comment in the same file, `OWNER_ACTIONS.md`'s OPS2 model line, and OPS2's NO MODEL DOWNGRADE rule.

**STEP B — THE FOUR-LEVEL EVIDENCE HIERARCHY. Traverse ALL FOUR levels for EVERY item, EVERY run (owner directive 2026-07-28 — supersedes the earlier "non-deployed research is context only" rule, which was too blunt).**

*Why this exists.* Research on the exact deployed model will almost never be current: vendor evals are gated or self-reported, independent replication takes months, and by the time it lands the fleet may have moved on. A rule that only counts deployed-model evidence would therefore discard nearly everything and leave the foundation evidenced by almost nothing. Instead, gather evidence at four widening scopes and report all four, so the picture is complete and the *degree of transfer* is an explicit, reasoned judgement rather than an accident of what happened to be published.

**NAMING — do not confuse these with the foundation's own Tier framework.** `AI_Trading_Foundation.md` uses **Tier 1 / Tier 2** for *architectural-vs-empirical* item classification. The levels below are **L1–L4** and describe *how close the evidence is to the deployed model*. The two axes are orthogonal: a Tier 1 item can have L4 evidence, a Tier 2 item can have L1 evidence. Never write "Tier" when you mean a level.

- **L1 — DEPLOYED MODEL.** Measurements on exactly the `routine_model` id. Highest weight for magnitudes. Expect this to be sparse or empty, especially within a few months of a model switch — that is normal and is not a failure of the sweep.
- **L2 — MODEL LINE.** Same line as the deployed model, any version, version numbers disregarded (e.g. every Opus release when Opus is deployed). **Decision rule, applied in order, so this is reproducible run-to-run:** (1) same product-line NAME as the deployed model → same line; (2) different name but the vendor documents it as the direct successor/rename of that line → same line, cite the vendor statement; (3) otherwise → **different line, so it is L3, not L2.** Default to (3) — a wrongly-widened L2 is worse than a narrow one, because L2 is what licenses transfer. Concretely: with `claude-opus-5-5` deployed, other Opus releases are L2 while Sonnet, Haiku, Fable and Mythos releases are **L3** unless the vendor documents a rename. If the deployed model is the FIRST release of its line, L2 contains one member, line stability is unassessable, and every version-volatility question resolves to "cannot assess" — say that explicitly rather than defaulting to CONVERGENT.
- **L3 — ANTHROPIC / CLAUDE FAMILY.** Any Claude model across all lines. Captures vendor-level effects — the post-training pipeline, Constitutional-AI/RLHF variant, tokenizer, safety scaffolding — that apply across lines but not necessarily to other labs.
- **L4 — GENERAL / ARCHITECTURAL.** Non-Anthropic models, and claims asserted for autoregressive LLMs trained with current methods broadly. Widest scope.

**L4 IS NOT "WEAKEST" — the weight ordering applies to MAGNITUDES ONLY.** For a Tier 1 architectural or existence claim (autoregressive models lack internal arithmetic units; pre-training embeds historical outcomes; RL post-training degrades calibration), an L4 architectural-generality result is the *appropriate and often strongest* evidence class, because the claim is about the model class, not about one release. Do NOT downgrade a Tier 1 item's evidence merely because it sits at L4. Conversely, an L1 measurement of a *magnitude* outranks an L4 one for that magnitude.

**CROSS-LEVEL VERDICT — the analytical payoff. For each item, after gathering all four levels, assign exactly one. THE DEFAULT IS `SPARSE`; assign a more informative verdict only when its stated evidence bar is met, and on ambiguity record the MORE RESTRICTIVE verdict** (this mirrors the asymmetric defaults used everywhere else in `Experiment_Parameters.md` — tie goes to the conservative branch):
- **CONVERGENT** — levels agree in direction and magnitudes sit in a common band. **Bar: ≥2 independent sources, and where L2 is invoked, ≥2 distinct versions measured on the same dimension.** Non-L1 evidence transfers to the deployed model with high confidence.
- **LEVEL-SPLIT** — L1/L2 disagree with L3/L4. Something is specific to this model or line; trust the NARROWER level for **magnitudes** and say why. **For a Tier 1 architectural/existence claim, do NOT apply narrower-wins** — L4 generality remains the appropriate class there, per the magnitudes-only rule above.
- **VERSION-VOLATILE** — within L2, measurements swing materially across versions of the same line. **Bar: ≥2 versions measured on the same dimension, differing by enough to change a §5.4 band or reverse a direction.** This is the decisive negative case: a measurement on a neighbouring version is NOT good evidence about the deployed model, no matter how much L3/L4 evidence exists — that magnitude is version-pending regardless. (Worked example: an Opus-line long-context retrieval score that fell ~2.4× between consecutive releases is VERSION-VOLATILE; an ECE holding ~0.12 across three Claude models is CONVERGENT.)
- **OFF-LINE-ONLY** — **this is the EXPECTED MODAL CASE, especially in the months after a model switch: L1 and L2 are empty, but L3 and/or L4 carry real evidence.** It is emphatically NOT `SPARSE` — the evidence exists, it simply sits away from the deployed line. Transfer consequence: for a Tier 1 architectural/existence claim, L4 evidence is sufficient and the item resolves normally. For a Tier 2 **magnitude**, the number may be reported and carried, but it is a family/architectural estimate rather than a measurement of the deployed model — say so at the item, and treat it as version-pending if the in-use model changed this cycle.
- **SPARSE** — too little at **every** level to classify. Reserve this for genuine evidentiary emptiness; do not use it when L4 is rich (that is OFF-LINE-ONLY). Say so plainly; do not manufacture a verdict.

**TRANSFER ASSESSMENT.** State explicitly, per item, whether non-L1 evidence transfers to the deployed model and on what basis — normally the L2 volatility read. This replaces the blunt context-only rule: evidence is *weighted and reasoned about*, never discarded for being off-model.

**RELATIONSHIP TO §5.5 — the hierarchy REFINES reporting and weighting; it is NOT a gate, and it adds no bar of its own anywhere, including for reductions.** `AI_Trading_Foundation.md` §5.5 guardrail 2 (transferability) is satisfied by *either* Claude-family replication *or* an architectural-generality argument: **L1/L2/L3 satisfy the first, L4 satisfies the second, and an L3-only or L4-only reduction therefore CLEARS guardrail 2 as the foundation currently writes it.** §5.5's remaining guardrails (≥3 independent sources, sustained across ≥2 quarters or a 2-year window, domain coverage) do the conservative work, and §5.5's closing rule — direct research findings count regardless of benchmark coverage — is **not** subject to the guardrails at all. **A1 must NOT impose a stricter standard than §5.5 codifies** (e.g. "only L1/L2 counts for a reduction"): a routine instruction is not the place to change the foundation's criteria, in either direction.

**What A1 does instead for a reduction claim: REPORT the level, and PROPOSE if it disagrees.** State plainly which level the reduction evidence sits at and what the cross-level verdict is, so A3 and the downstream §5.3/§5.6 machinery can see exactly what a constraint relaxation would rest on. If the sweep judges that §5.5's transferability bar is too permissive for a capital-affecting relaxation — e.g. that an L4-only reduction on non-Anthropic models should not be able to loosen a sizing cap — then emit an explicit **PART 2 proposal to amend §5.5 guardrail 2**, with the reasoning and the proposed wording, for A3 to apply once it lands in the document. Do not apply the stricter bar on this run as though it were already the rule. (Note the correct cross-reference throughout: the transferability question lives in **§5.5 guardrail 2**, not §5.4 — §5.4 is a PARTIAL/MATERIAL magnitude-threshold table containing no evidence-provenance condition, so there is nothing in §5.4 for a provenance argument to clear.)

This is a FULL RE-DERIVATION task, not a delta. The scope is the LONGER of last-24-months primary-source research or the full period since A1's last successful completion (owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW, see Observability § above — in the ordinary case these are the same ~24 months, since A1 fires annually; only widen further in the pathological case A1 has been down for more than 2 years), not last-quarter. The purpose is to catch cumulative slow drift on Tier 2 numerical claims that quarterly deltas can't reliably surface, and to verify Tier 1 architectural items against any affirmative architectural-change evidence over a longer window.

**HOW TO RUN THIS AFFORDABLY — search by battery, then CLASSIFY into levels. Do NOT run a separate four-way search per item.** The research protocol is battery-shaped (9 topic queries) while the output is item×level-shaped; the bridge is a single classification pass, not repeated searching. Sequence: (1) run the batteries and anchor checks ONCE, building a pooled evidence set; (2) for every result, record the models actually evaluated by name and version, and assign it a level; (3) attribute pooled findings to items and emit the per-item level blocks from the classified pool; (4) only then run targeted gap-filling searches for items where a *decision-relevant* level is empty — typically L1/L2 on a Tier 2 magnitude. A naive per-item four-way search does not fit A1's slot and its overrun is not benign: A3 is `catchup_safe: false` and gated same-day on A1 and A2, so an A1 that runs long means `AI_Trading_Foundation.md` goes un-updated for a **year**, not a day.

**USE SUBAGENT FAN-OUT — this is expected, not optional.** Decompose the batteries across parallel sub-tasks (the prior sweep used eleven and it worked), each returning only its structured evidence block rather than raw transcript. Keep the orchestrating context for classification, cross-level verdicts and PART 2 synthesis. Per the shared Observability rules, run this routine's own guard, run-logging and model-of-record step in the orchestrating context FIRST — never delegate those to a sub-task.

**WHERE EACH LEVEL'S EVIDENCE ACTUALLY LIVES.** The levels need different sources, and searching the wrong surface for a level is the main way a sweep wrongly concludes `ABSENT`:
- **L1 / L2 / L3 (Claude-specific) — NOT on Hugging Face.** HF hosts no Anthropic model cards, evals, or announcements. Use `web_search` / `web_fetch` / Tavily against: Anthropic **system cards** (the richest L1 source — they carry per-surface injection, honesty and long-context tables, and are `VENDOR-CLAIMED` by definition), `anthropic.com/news`, `docs.anthropic.com`, `platform.claude.com` model-deprecation pages (for the release/retirement trajectory that defines the L2 line), and Anthropic's research blog. For **independent** Claude measurements — which are what L1/L2/L3 most need and most lack — check third-party evaluators and leaderboards that publish per-model numbers (e.g. Artificial Analysis and its indices, METR time-horizon reports, independent red-team firms, academic papers that happen to include a Claude model in their panel). When an academic paper's panel includes a Claude model, that paper is L2/L3 evidence *even if the paper is not about Claude* — check panels explicitly rather than assuming a general paper is L4.
- **L4 (general / architectural) — Hugging Face is the strong surface.** Use `hf_fs` for the paper index and `hub_repo_search` for model cards and leaderboards.
- Record for every measurement which model and version it was taken on. **A paper that names no model version cannot be placed at L1 or L2** — classify it L3 or L4 and say the version was unspecified rather than assuming.

HF tool orientation. Read `HF_Resource_Catalog.md` once at session start for the authoritative HF tooling map, but note the catalog is itself subject to drift — verify a tool exists before relying on it and report any correction needed. Apply the following operational rules during PART 1 research:

Write the complete content directly to `Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md` (overwrite; first line = current calendar year in YYYY format).

PART 1 — Last-24-months coverage of primary-source research, organized by AI_Trading_Foundation.md item rather than by topic. For EACH numbered item in Parts 1 and 2 (1.1 through 1.10, 2.1 through 2.26 or whatever the current count is) — **and also for each Part 3a and 3b question, which are in scope and must appear in the evidence-coverage matrix with their own level rows and verdict** (3a questions resolve on accumulated evidence and 3b questions are explicitly open, so their rows will often read OFF-LINE-ONLY or SPARSE — that is a legitimate and informative result, but they must not be silently omitted as they were in prior cycles):

  - Item identifier and tier (per AI_Trading_Foundation.md headers — Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 1 existence / Tier 2 magnitudes).
  - Current text of the item.
  - **EVIDENCE BY LEVEL — depth scaled to what the item can actually consume (cost control; the run must finish inside its slot).** Two treatments, and state which one you applied:
      - **FULL four-level traversal — for items carrying a Tier 2 MAGNITUDE** (the §5.4 threshold-table rows, plus 1.3 and 1.7, plus any item whose text contains a specific number). These are the only items where "which level is this number from" changes a resolution, so they get the full L1→L4 search and a cross-level verdict.
      - **L4-PRIMARY block — for pure Tier 1 architectural/existence items.** §5.5 and STEP B both already hold that L4 generality evidence is the appropriate class for these, and Tier 1 items are audited only for affirmative architectural-change evidence. Search L4 properly; record L1–L3 only if a Claude-specific result happens to surface. Verdict may be recorded as `OFF-LINE-ONLY (Tier 1 — L4 is the appropriate class)` without a four-way search.
    **Report each level explicitly even when empty** for the items under full traversal; `ABSENT` is a first-class, informative answer, because *which* levels are empty is itself the finding that drives the transfer assessment. Citations inline, reverse-chronological within each level. For every measurement give the model(s) actually evaluated by name and version, and label vendor-published results `VENDOR-CLAIMED`.
      - **L1 — deployed model** (`<routine_model>`): …or `ABSENT`.
      - **L2 — model line** (`<line>`, all versions): …or `ABSENT`. Where the line has multiple versions measured on the same dimension, list them in version order so volatility is visible at a glance.
      - **L3 — Anthropic / Claude family** (all lines): …or `ABSENT`.
      - **L4 — general / architectural** (non-Anthropic and autoregressive-LLM-general): …or `ABSENT`.
  - **CROSS-LEVEL VERDICT**: exactly one of CONVERGENT / LEVEL-SPLIT / VERSION-VOLATILE / SPARSE, plus one sentence of justification naming the levels that drove it.
  - **TRANSFER ASSESSMENT**: does non-L1 evidence transfer to the deployed model, and on what basis? Normally decided by the L2 volatility read. Be explicit — this is what licenses (or refuses) every downstream resolution on this item.
  - **Benchmark-result summary**: for Tier 2 items with benchmark mapping per §5.5, summarize benchmark trajectory over last 24 months — score progression on each mapped benchmark, models evaluated, whether the trajectory clears the §5.5 Goodhart guardrails (≥3 sources, transferability, sustained, domain coverage). Note which level each benchmark's evidence sits at. For Tier 1 items: no benchmark trajectory required (Tier 1 not subject to benchmark inference).
  - For Tier 2 items specifically: list the specific numerical claims and tag each as "supported by recent research", "contradicted/refined by recent research" (with proposed update), "supported by benchmark inference" (with §5.5 verification), "contradicted by benchmark inference" (with §5.5 verification), or "absent from recent research" — and **annotate every tag with the level its evidence sits at**, e.g. `SUPPORTED-BY-RESEARCH [L3]`. A claim supported only at L4 reads very differently from one supported at L1, and the annotation is what makes that visible to A3.
  - For Tier 1 items: report whether any architectural-change evidence has emerged. (Default: NO unless affirmative evidence is found.) Remember that L4 architectural-generality evidence is the *appropriate* class here and must not be discounted for being off-model.

PART 2 — Per-item resolutions. The downstream A3 routine reads this PART 2 verbatim and produces the updated AI_Trading_Foundation.md applying the per-item resolutions, plus schedules per-strategy foundation-change assessment events per the aggregate outcomes. Make per-item resolutions explicit and structured.

Every resolution must state **the level its governing evidence sits at and the cross-level verdict**, so A3 can see what each change rests on. Resolution rules:
  - If Tier 1 with no architectural-change evidence: KEEP UNCHANGED.
  - If Tier 1 with architectural-change evidence: UPDATE per evidence; flag for foundation-change assessment. (L4 generality evidence fully qualifies here.)
  - If Tier 2 with supporting research: KEEP, optionally update with the most-recent measurement — **preferring the narrowest level available** (an L1 or L2 number supersedes an L3/L4 one for the same quantity). If the best available number is L3/L4 and the item's verdict is VERSION-VOLATILE, KEEP the item but mark the magnitude version-pending rather than importing an off-line number as though it were measured on the deployed model.
  - If Tier 2 with contradicting/refining research: UPDATE numerical claim per evidence; flag for foundation-change assessment (may trigger constraint-relaxation review per Experiment_Parameters.md if the update represents a disadvantage reduction). Where the update is a **reduction**, state the level its evidence sits at and the cross-level verdict alongside the §5.5 guardrail results, so the downstream §5.3/§5.6 machinery can see what a relaxation would rest on — but apply §5.5 as the foundation writes it and do not add a level-based bar of your own (see STEP B).
  - If Tier 2 absent from recent research **at every level**: MARK AS VERSION-PENDING.
  - If Tier 2 present at L3/L4 but the verdict is VERSION-VOLATILE: MARK AS VERSION-PENDING for the deployed model, and say explicitly that this is a *transfer* failure, not an absence of research — the two produce the same label for different reasons and A3 must not conflate them (an absence needs new research; a transfer failure needs a measurement on the current line). Do NOT auto-remove. The two-year absence is signal but not sufficient on its own to remove a previously-documented item — publication asymmetry means improvements often don't generate papers. The residual resolution is NOT deferred to a human (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive): A3 enqueues an `out-of-table-resolution` review (default-HOLD-current-state) for the item, which stays VERSION-PENDING until an affirmative RESOLVE verdict lands and is re-surfaced each review cycle in the meantime.

Then aggregate:
  - **EVIDENCE-COVERAGE MATRIX (new, owner directive 2026-07-28)** — one row per item, one column per level, marking which levels had evidence and the cross-level verdict. Then the headline counts: how many items have ANY L1 evidence, how many rest on L3/L4 only, and how many are VERSION-VOLATILE. **This matrix is the honest one-screen answer to "what does this sweep actually establish about the model we run," and it must appear before the resolution lists.** A low L1 count is an expected and acceptable finding — report it plainly rather than obscuring it; what is NOT acceptable is leaving the reader unable to tell.
  - **VERSION-CHANGE PROTOCOL SCOPE (state explicitly, do not leave A3 to infer).** If the in-use model changed since the last sweep, Part 4 step 4 flips **all** Tier 2 numerical claims to version-pending-replication — a document-wide flip, distinct from the per-item fade-review VERSION-PENDING list below. Enumerate which mechanism applies to which items so A3 cannot conflate them. **Do NOT instruct A3 to exempt any magnitude from the flip.** If the sweep's cross-level TRANSFER assessments argue that some magnitudes demonstrably carry across versions and that a blanket flip is therefore over-conservative, raise that as an explicit **PART 2 proposal to amend Part 4 step 4 and Tier 1 item 2.9**, with the evidence and the proposed new wording — A3 applies it only after it lands in the document with a revision-history entry. Proposing a loosening is legitimate; applying one from a routine instruction is not, and the discipline is identical to the one this routine is forbidden from breaking in the tightening direction.
  - Also run **`ops/foundation_change_review.md` §C "Model-version change"** if the in-use model changed, and hand its checklist to A3 with the required `events.decision_log` completion record (`entry_type='foundation-change-review'`). Do not reinvent it.
  - List of all items KEEP UNCHANGED.
  - List of all items UPDATE (with old text → new text and citation).
  - List of all items MARK AS VERSION-PENDING.
  - List of all items proposed for REMOVAL (rare; requires Tier 1 architectural-change evidence or Tier 2 with explicit contradicting research, NOT mere absence).
  - List of all NEW items proposed for addition (new failure modes or new edges discovered in the 24-month window).
  - Per-strategy foundation-change assessment recommendations: for each strategy A through E, list which items materially change its foundation and what the recommended outcome is (continue / terminate / constraint-relaxation review).
  - Arsenal candidate seeds and research leads (rev 2026-08-03 correctness hardening): classify each new/restart archetype before handoff. A **candidate seed** must already name a valid Part-1 return-generating edge, a compensated non-version-pending Part-2 disadvantage, valid target regime cells, and a prospective/countable signal from which frequency, invalidation, and kill structure are derivable. If any field is absent, a cited disadvantage is merely refined/contested rather than reduced, a §5.5 guardrail fails, or implementability is unresolved, record a **research lead** instead with its blocker and objective promotion threshold. A research lead is not a candidate and carries no rejection cooldown. A3 writes leads to `events.strategy_research_leads`; only eligible seeds enter `state.strategy_candidates`.

OUTPUT: write the complete content (PART 1 + PART 2) directly to `Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md`. First line is the YYYY marker. Chat output: one-line acknowledgment.
```

## A2. Per-Strategy Constraint Audit — deep research

```
**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='A2' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "A2 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or A2's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the audit, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

Read access scope: Annual cadence. Read everything, including full `events.decision_log` history (queryable, no live/archive split, §15). A2 traces foundation-citation graphs across full `events.decision_log` history.

Read Strategy.md (full, including all per-strategy pre-mortems), Experiment_Parameters.md, AI_Trading_Foundation.md (current revision), Operating_Protocols.md, most recent Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md output, and recent Quarterly_AI_Foundation_Delta.md outputs (positions from `state.current_positions`, regime from `state.current_regime`, decisions from `events.decision_log`).

This is the INVERSE of pre-mortem. Where pre-mortems attack strategies looking for missing constraints to ADD, this audit reviews strategies looking for existing constraints to potentially RELAX. Per AI_Trading_Foundation.md rev 4, the audit is fully mechanical — apply the criteria from §5.3-§5.6, no orchestrator discretion.

Write the complete content directly to `Annual_Constraint_Audit.md` (overwrite; first line = current calendar year in YYYY format).

For EACH strategy (A, B, C, D, E — and any others added since this task was authored), execute the §5.3 mechanical procedure:

PART 1 — Constraint inventory and foundation-citation graph.

  List every distinct constraint in the strategy's mechanism document and pre-mortem. Each constraint should be linked to:
  - The specific text of the constraint (entry rule, sizing cap, eligibility restriction, exit trigger, etc.).
  - The constraint's PRIMARY citation per AI_Trading_Foundation.md — parsed from the rev N annotations explicitly linking the constraint to a specific disadvantage. Mechanical: the constraint's primary citation is the item named in the annotation "rev N per cycle M T1.X" where T1.X is the cycle attacker output that originally surfaced the need for this constraint, traced to the specific 2.X item.
  - The constraint's SECONDARY citations — any other disadvantages named as mitigation targets in the pre-mortem's Section 5 entries or binding-constraint section. Mechanical: exact-text-match against pre-mortem Section 5 mitigation citations.
  - The revision in which the constraint was added.
  - Constraint type per §5.6 lookup (per-position sizing cap / universe restriction / concentration limit / frequency-cadence rule / hit-rate threshold / out-of-table).

PART 2 — Mechanical per-constraint relaxation verdicts. The downstream A3 routine reads this PART 2 verbatim and produces the updated Strategy.md applying mechanical relaxation verdicts per §5.6, plus queues out-of-table flags for explicit review. Make per-constraint outcomes explicit.

For each constraint:

Step 1 — Reduction status of primary citation. From most recent Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md and prior-year Quarterly_AI_Foundation_Delta.md outputs, classify the primary cited disadvantage's reduction magnitude:
- NONE (no reduction signal) — constraint not a candidate; skip remaining steps.
- PARTIAL (25-75% reduction per §5.4 thresholds, with direct research evidence OR benchmark inference clearing §5.5 Goodhart guardrails) — proceed to Step 2.
- MATERIAL (>75% reduction or full elimination per §5.4 thresholds) — proceed to Step 2.

Step 2 — Benchmark-inference verification (rev 4 added). If the reduction signal comes from benchmark inference rather than direct research, verify §5.5 Goodhart guardrails:
- ≥3 independent benchmark sources (different research groups, different benchmark suites)?
- Replication on Claude family OR architectural-generality argument documented?
- Sustained improvement across ≥2 quarterly cycles OR documented in last-2-years annual sweep?
- Domain coverage matching workflow usage (general-purpose benchmarks always count; narrow benchmarks count only if domain matches)?
If any guardrail fails, downgrade reduction to NONE for this audit cycle. Constraint is not a candidate.

Step 3 — Load-bearing test. Check the constraint's secondary citations from PART 1:
- For each secondary citation, is the cited disadvantage still in force per current AI_Trading_Foundation.md (i.e., not eliminated, and not classified as MATERIAL reduction in this audit cycle)?
- If any secondary citation is still in force → constraint is load-bearing for multiple disadvantages → no relaxation, regardless of magnitude on primary citation.

Step 4 — Apply §5.6 mechanical relaxation lookup. For constraints passing Steps 1-3:
- Per-position sizing caps: PARTIAL → cap × (1 + reduction%); MATERIAL → cap × 2 (capped at 5%).
- Concentration limits: PARTIAL → limit + (limit × reduction%); MATERIAL → limit + 15pp (capped at 50%) or removed if all citations eliminated.
- Universe restrictions: PARTIAL → no change; MATERIAL with full elimination of all citations → reconsider for full removal (subject to Step 3).
- Hit-rate thresholds with disadvantage-keyed derivations: PARTIAL → threshold loosened proportionally per derivation citation; MATERIAL → threshold reconsidered at next gate review.
- Frequency-cadence rules: no auto-relaxation. Flag for explicit annual review.
- Out-of-table constraints: flag in §5.7 audit trail; no relaxation; constraint stays at current value and is routed to an `out-of-table-resolution` review (default-HOLD-current-value) that A3 enqueues — NOT deferred to participant resolution (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive).

Step 5 — Output structured audit trail per §5.7 for each strategy:
- Strategy identifier and current revision.
- Foundation citation graph.
- Per-citation status changes since strategy's foundation revision.
- Per-constraint evaluation: primary citation reduction status, benchmark-inference verification result (if applicable), load-bearing test result, applicable relaxation form per §5.6, new constraint value (if relaxed), reason for non-relaxation (if not).
- Out-of-table flags listing any constraints the criteria couldn't deterministically resolve, with the specific gap identified.

The expected outcome of A2 in any given year is: most constraints have NONE primary-citation reduction (Step 1 terminates the evaluation); a small number have PARTIAL or MATERIAL reduction; of those, most fail Step 3 load-bearing test; of the remainder, §5.6 lookup produces structured relaxation forms; out-of-table flags are rare. The audit is operationally cheap when no constraints have reduction signals and only generates substantive output when AI_Trading_Foundation.md has documented disadvantage reductions.

OUTPUT: write the complete content (PART 1 + PART 2) directly to `Annual_Constraint_Audit.md`. First line is the YYYY marker. Chat output: one-line acknowledgment.
```

CHAT OUTPUT:

- One-line acknowledgment of file edits and `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue entries enqueued.

If no file changes, no queue entries: "No actions required." (rare for A3 — at minimum AI_Trading_Foundation.md will have a revision bump documenting the sweep, even if all items KEEP UNCHANGED.)

# STRATEGY ARSENAL LIFECYCLE (SL1–SL5)

The Self-Improving Strategy Arsenal (SISA) routines make strategy ADDITION and DELETION fully autonomous — no human review / approval / chat anywhere in the path (residuals: the system-wide IBKR order-confirm tap + deposits). Roster MEMBERSHIP is versioned policy (the roster analog of the 2026-06 capital-allocation pivot); each strategy's OWN machinery freezes at SHADOW entry and its edge-measurement clock starts at its first PROBE trade. Single source of truth: `strategy/roster.yaml` (CI-guarded by `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py`) mirrored to `events.strategy_lifecycle` → `state.strategy_roster` → `state.active_strategy_codes`. Owner kill-switch: `ops.arsenal_control` (+ `ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled`) freezes the whole loop with one out-of-band INSERT without disturbing live trading. Loop recorded at `active_auto` in `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml` (2026-07-10 owner decision); BQ objects in `bigquery/35_strategy_arsenal.sql`; incident/decision write-up in `ops/RUNBOOK.md` §37 + Operating_Protocols.md §SISA. All five follow the shared "Observability — run logging & failure alerts" section for connector pre-flight / run-logging / failure alerts; none ever asks a chat question. (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive.)

## SL1. Strategy Candidate Synthesis & Qualification — deep research

Quarterly (first trading day of quarter), after Q1 and Q3 are saved. The scouting + mechanical-qualifier head of the lifecycle: deep-research synthesis biased toward under-covered regime cells, then a default-REJECT qualification gate deciding which candidates enter the authoring queue. Writes structured `state.strategy_candidates` rows + lifecycle transitions; never authors a strategy (SL2) and never touches the live roster (SL5).

```
**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='SL1' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "SL1 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or SL1's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the synthesis, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

Read access scope: Quarterly cadence, deep research (HF `hf_fs` + `web_search`/Tavily per HF_Resource_Catalog.md, as Q3/A1 use them). Read the candidate feed `state.strategy_candidates` (rows written by D1/Q1/Q3/A1), the open lead feed `events.strategy_research_leads`, and final-effective prior SL1 `events.decision_log` `entry_type='arsenal-heartbeat'` rows (exclude targets named by correction rows through `superseded_by`) + the roster/coverage/rails state `state.strategy_roster`, `state.active_strategy_codes`, `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`, `state.arsenal_rails`, `events.strategy_postmortems`, `ops.arsenal_control`. Read the just-saved `Quarterly_Regime.md` (PART 2 diagnostic flags), `Quarterly_AI_Foundation_Delta.md` (Q3 strategy-adoption/retirement branch), `Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md` (A1's most recent full re-derivation), `events.hf_capability_captures`, and `AI_Trading_Foundation.md` (edge/disadvantage registry) — these are the LIVE capability-flag sources (cadence audit 2026-07-29). **`Monthly_AI_Capabilities.md` is a FROZEN one-time March-2026 snapshot, not a live input** — one commit ever, self-describing a two-generations-stale decision-maker model, and no routine has written it since the old monthly AI-capabilities task was folded into quarterly Q3 at the 2026-06-06 renumbering; it stays reachable for its own dated historical content only and must NOT be read as current capability state. Stage no orders; do not edit Strategy.md or the roster.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, and failure alerts are EXACTLY per the shared "Observability — run logging & failure alerts" section — do not restate, just make the calls. This routine writes no cadence `.md`; it is monitored via run-logging + `state.period_watch` + the meta-heartbeat in STEP 6.

**`ops.web_calls` OBLIGATION (added 2026-08-24, fleet-wide alert-triage closure)** — SL1's own Read-access-scope line above names the metered surfaces this routine draws on for its deep research: HF `hf_fs` and `web_search`/Tavily, per `HF_Resource_Catalog.md`, the same tools Q3/A1 use; STEP 2 (SYNTHESIZE) is where they actually get called, as it researches each candidate mechanism and research lead. Unlike OPS1's one fixed `^VIX` probe per run, STEP 2's call count is NOT constant — it tracks how many candidates (0-2) and leads (0+) this firing actually works, so some quarters may issue several such calls and some may issue none. Before the terminal `sp_routine_end` call, write the batched `ops.web_calls` INSERT per the shared Run-logging template (§Observability, ~line 204-227) covering every HF/`web_search`/Tavily call this run actually made — one row per call, inside the same best-effort wrapper — and if STEP 2 made none this firing, log nothing and say so in the `<note>` rather than fabricating a row.

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL1')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + a `critical` alert (then abort) if `state.arsenal_enabled.enabled = FALSE` or `incubation_frozen = TRUE` (owner froze the loop via a single `ops.arsenal_control` INSERT). Live trading is unaffected — this gate freezes only candidate generation / graduation / retirement.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL1', ['Q1', 'Q3'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Q1/Q3 are `quarterly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any Q1/Q3 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, QUARTER) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day — **this period-window rule, not self-bootstrapping, is what actually protects SL1 here:** the real 2026-07-27 false positive (alert `177646a6`) fired precisely BECAUSE Q1/Q3 HAD both completed, on 2026-07-01 (the quarter's first trading day) — self-bootstrapping never applied, since Q1/Q3 were not unadopted, merely dated earlier in the same quarter. Self-bootstrapping (Q1/Q3 are research feeders that may not yet log `completed` AT ALL; treated as satisfied until they do) is a separate, additional tolerance that still applies too, for the genuinely-never-run case. This is the general rule from Observability § above, inlined per-routine.

**`events.strategy_research_leads` WRITE CONTRACT — binds EVERY producer of a research lead (SL1 STEP 2 and A3's arsenal-handoff bullet); pinned 2026-08-19. Producers do not restate it, they cite it.** Three of this table's columns are `NOT NULL` with no default (`bigquery/133_sl1_research_leads_and_record_corrections.sql`:20-39) and, until this contract, **no instruction anywhere in this document named any of them** — `lead_id` appeared zero times. Two producers that never share a session were each left to invent the key, and MEASURED 2026-08-19 they did: the only two rows in the table use two different schemes.

```
lead_id  = '<lowercase source_routine>-<YYYY-MM of the opening event>-<the archetype value, verbatim>'
           -- NOT NULL, no default. STABLE FOR THE LIFE OF THE LEAD: the table's own description is
           -- 'Latest event per lead_id is current', so every later UPDATED/CONVERTED/CLOSED event MUST
           -- reuse the opening event's exact lead_id. A new id is a new lead, not an update to one.
           -- The prefix is the ORIGINATING routine, which is not always the writing routine: A3
           -- writing an A1 handoff uses 'a1-', matching the source_routine='A1' its candidate-seed
           -- branch already pins on the same bullet.
           -- TWO GRANDFATHERED ROWS, both event_type='OPEN', neither to be renamed (this table is
           -- append-only; a rename would fork the lead into two):
           --   'sl1-2026-08-disclosure-information-surprise'  conforms to the rule above.
           --   'a1-2026-2.20-heterogeneous-regime'            does NOT: its middle segment is the A1
           --     disadvantage id 2.20 rather than a YYYY-MM, and its tail truncates the archetype
           --     ('heterogeneous-regime' for archetype 'heterogeneous-regime-momentum-participation').
           --     Continue this lead under its existing id; apply the rule to NEW leads only.
event_type = 'OPEN' | 'UPDATED' | 'CONVERTED' | 'CLOSED'
           -- NOT NULL, no default. OPEN on first write; UPDATED whenever evidence_status, blocker or
           -- next_step moves; CONVERTED only when the lead becomes a state.strategy_candidates row
           -- (set converted_candidate_code in that SAME event); CLOSED when the mechanism is
           -- abandoned. Append-only: never UPDATE a prior row, always add an event.
archetype  = the same archetype token the candidate feed uses, in full
           -- NOT NULL, no default. This is what BOTH idempotency rules that guard this table ('skip
           -- an already-open lead with the same archetype', A3 and SL1) actually match on, so an
           -- invented or truncated value silently defeats both and re-opens the lead every cycle.
```

**BEFORE OPENING A LEAD, resolve it against the table, never against memory:** `SELECT lead_id, archetype, ARRAY_AGG(event_type ORDER BY event_ts DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS latest FROM events.strategy_research_leads GROUP BY lead_id, archetype`. If the archetype already has a lead whose latest event is neither `CLOSED` nor `CONVERTED`, append an `UPDATED` event under that existing `lead_id` — do not open a second one. Match on `archetype`, not on `lead_id`, precisely because the legacy ids do not all follow the format.

STEP 1 — READ THE CANDIDATE AND RESEARCH-LEAD FEEDS. Collect every `state.strategy_candidates` row with `status='NEW'` (sources D1/Q1/Q3/A1), every open `events.strategy_research_leads` row, and final-effective prior SL1 heartbeats. A lead is context for research, not a candidate: do not run STEP 3 on it or stamp a cooldown unless its objective promotion threshold is now met and a complete candidate row is first created. Also read the diagnostic factbase: Quarterly_Regime.md PART 2 flags, the Quarterly_AI_Foundation_Delta.md strategy-adoption branch, `events.hf_capability_captures` + `Annual_AI_Foundation_Sweep.md` capability flags (the live sources — cadence audit 2026-07-29; NOT `Monthly_AI_Capabilities.md`, a frozen March-2026 snapshot no routine has written since the old monthly AI-capabilities task folded into quarterly Q3 at the 2026-06-06 renumbering), terminated-strategy `events.strategy_postmortems`, and `state.arsenal_regime_coverage` (which regime cells are zero/under-covered).

STEP 2 — SYNTHESIZE (0-2 additional candidates; 0+ research leads). Deep-research mechanisms biased toward genuine uncovered cells. `state.arsenal_regime_coverage` is demonstrated-PAPER coverage and is degenerate for founding A-E, which skipped incubation; therefore cross-check every apparent gap against every live router and treat the declared-router result as authoritative until an ADOPTED-coverage leg exists. A mechanism becomes a candidate only if the research already supplies enough evidence and implementable machinery that it can plausibly clear STEP 3 today. If magnitude, transferability, prospective signal/detector, frequency, invalidation, kill structure, or cost fit is unresolved, write/update an `events.strategy_research_leads` row with evidence_status, blocker, and concrete next_step instead — do NOT create a candidate row merely to reject it, because doing so burns the archetype's cooldown without adding evidence. Where a candidate's edge is judgment-shaped (regime interpretation, narrative synthesis, event-severity assessment — an edge a numeric proxy would flatten), PREFER specifying its machinery judgment-native per SL2's JUDGMENT-NATIVE MACHINERY option (owner-approved Redesign B, 2026-07-19, `AI_DECISION_REDESIGN.md` §3) rather than forcing it into fixed numeric triggers. Write each actual candidate as a CANDIDATE `events.strategy_lifecycle` row (to_state=CANDIDATE, driver_routine='SL1') + a `state.strategy_candidates` record {provisional code, thesis_md, cited_edges 1.x, cited_disadvantages 2.x compensated, instruments, sizing_method, kill_structure, target_regime_cells, declared_frequency, `declared_annual_roundtrips` (a numeric best-estimate; NULL defaults to the strict fast-archetype PAPER graduation bar), is_restart_of}. **THE CREATION ROW IS MANDATORY, AND ITS `event_ts` MUST BE STRICTLY EARLIER THAN ANY SAME-RUN TRANSITION ROW FOR THE SAME CODE (PINNED 2026-08-21, alert triage; CONFIRMED GAP `lifecycle-creation-row-unwritten`).** Two live defects turned this from a restatement into a pin. **(a) The row has already been silently skipped once.** SL1's 2026-07-27 run wrote the CANDIDATE row for BOTH F and G, but its 2026-08-03 run wrote H's `CANDIDATE`→`REJECTED` row with no row recording H entering candidacy — so H's earliest lifecycle row declared a `from_state` the log never recorded it reaching. It sat unnoticed for 18 days because `state.strategy_roster.current_state` reads the LATEST row per code and so still read `REJECTED` correctly: the OUTCOME was right and only the provenance was gone, so nothing downstream disagreed and no gate ever went red. That is the failure mode to expect here — this omission never announces itself. Repaired 2026-08-21 by `bigquery/190_strategy_lifecycle_provenance_repair.sql` (a backdated, NOT-EXISTS-guarded reconstruction carrying `driver_routine='repair-2026-08-21'`, never `'SL1'` — a repair must stay distinguishable from the write it stands in for) and now detected by `state.strategy_lifecycle_provenance`, which D3's QUEUE HYGIENE step polls. **(b) A same-`event_ts` batch settles the roster on a coin-flip.** When STEP 4 below default-REJECTs a candidate in the SAME run that this step created it, writing both rows at the same instant leaves `state.strategy_roster` to break the tie on `event_id DESC` (`bigquery/35`:306) — a `GENERATE_UUID()` value, i.e. an arbitrary one. F's and G's four rows all carry the identical `2026-07-28 06:10:29.279889Z`, and both codes read `REJECTED` today ONLY because their UUIDs happened to sort that way; the other sort order would have reported a default-REJECTED candidate as `CANDIDATE`, reopening a code whose 90-day archetype cooldown is keyed off the REJECTED row. Those two pairs are recorded ACCEPTED HISTORICAL on the detector view (they are terminal and the table is append-only, so they cannot be restamped and will never change) — but never add a third: stamp the creation row first and let any same-run transition row take a strictly later instant. Never synthesize a candidate that would push the roster above `state.arsenal_rails.n_max`. Each `target_regime_cells` entry MUST use the coverage view's two-token key `SPY_TREND/VIX_REGIME` (for example `DOWN/HIGH`), with both tokens drawn from `strategy/01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md`; yield-curve and breadth conditions belong in the thesis/router specification, not this join key.

STEP 3 — MECHANICAL QUALIFICATION (DEFAULT-REJECT on any unmet rail or ambiguity). For each NEW candidate, in order — fail any → REJECTED:
   (a) **Cited-edge validity.** Every thesis rule cites a valid live `AI_Trading_Foundation.md` edge/disadvantage and the candidate names a compensated non-version-pending Part-2 disadvantage. A scope refinement, contradiction, version-pending magnitude, or guardrail-failing reduction is NOT compensation and cannot be routed as relaxed. A research-grade source label or upstream seed does not exempt the candidate. The return-generating mechanism itself must trace to a Part-1 edge; an edge used only to detect/select a classical factor wrapper is insufficient. If a named prospective detector/signal, target cells, frequency, invalidation, or kill structure cannot be derived, fail on the merits under default-REJECT rather than treating the fields as merely unfilled.
   (b) **Material-structural-difference vs every live AND every terminated strategy** — differs in >=1 of {approach, instrument scope, sizing methodology, router structure, kill-criteria structure} beyond threshold numbers (the Experiment_Parameters.md restart constraints, now machine-enforced). For a restart (`is_restart_of` set): the terminated strategy's `events.strategy_postmortems` row MUST exist AND its `material_diff_required_for_restart` field must articulate the difference; require that a restart is never proposed without a post-mortem (the fresh-derivation byte-match check is applied by SL2/AR against `derivation_provenance`).
   (c) **Non-redundancy / differentiation vs the current roster** — not dominated by a live strategy on its target regime cells.
   (d) **Capacity/cost fit** at the $2,000 probe floor: modeled all-in round-trip commission as a percentage of deployed notional must be `<= state.arsenal_rails.max_roundtrip_commission_pct` (=1.8%, the current accepted probe-scale ceiling). Frequency is reported separately as annual-dollar drag; do not multiply a percentage of per-trade notional by frequency and compare it to a per-round-trip ceiling. Include borrow and spread/slippage when the instrument requires them; default-REJECT if executable size or a fillable price cannot be verified.
   (e) **Ceiling clear** — roster active-count below `n_max`.
   (f) **Cooldown clear** — no same-archetype `cooldown_until` in force (post-rejection / post-termination stamp).

STEP 4 — PROMOTE / HOLD / REJECT.
   - PASS + `NOT state.arsenal_rails.incubation_cap_reached` (concurrent-incubation count < `k_incubate` — `state.arsenal_rails` has no `caps_ok` column; that name exists only on `state.strategy_adoption_readiness`, a later-stage view) + adoption-rate window open: write a QUALIFYING lifecycle row, set `state.strategy_candidates.status='QUALIFYING'`, and enqueue a `PENDING_DRAFT` `events.queue_events` item (`item_type='strategy-draft'`, trigger_context = candidate_code) for SL2. **`due_date` = the NEXT calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today` (America/Denver) — same pin, same reasons, as the AR_orc `strategy-revise` enqueue (AR_orc Step 4, pinned 2026-08-17 by SL2); this bullet carried the identical unstated-offset gap, and it is pinned here now rather than waiting for it to drift the first time SL1 ever qualifies a candidate.** Never compute this date from a session-local or UTC clock — see §Calendar MCP usage. If the cap or rate window is closed, leave the candidate QUALIFYING and wait FIFO (re-checked next firing) — never exceed the cap.
   - FAIL: write a REJECTED lifecycle row + set `status='REJECTED'`, `reject_reason`, and a `cooldown_until` stamp. **If this REJECT fires in the SAME run that STEP 2 created the candidate, this row's `event_ts` MUST be strictly LATER than the creation row's (STEP 2's order pin, 2026-08-21):** an equal stamp leaves `state.strategy_roster` to settle the code's current state on the `event_id DESC` `GENERATE_UUID()` tiebreak, which is the only reason F and G read `REJECTED` today rather than `CANDIDATE`.

STEP 5 — FLOOR SAFETY VALVE. If the roster active-count is at the `n_min` (=2) floor, force-generate candidates (relax the coverage bias, still default-REJECT-qualify) and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','SL1','roster_below_floor', 'Strategy roster is at the n_min=2 floor (<N> active) — SL1 is force-generating successor candidates.', '<JSON per the preamble ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract: roster_active_before/after, reason; strategy_code NULL — this notice is about the roster, not one strategy>')` — the successor-experiment safety valve. **`warning`, not `info`** (ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, preamble): the operator is told the arsenal has shrunk to its floor rather than having to query for it.

STEP 6 — META-HEARTBEAT. EVERY firing (even when nothing qualified) write a `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` `events.decision_log` entry `entry_type='arsenal-heartbeat'` recording candidates read / synthesized / qualified / rejected plus research leads opened / advanced / converted. When correcting a prior heartbeat, preserve `entry_type='arsenal-heartbeat'`, tag the replacement `correction`, and set `superseded_by` to the obsolete heartbeat's entry_id; a later narrative that merely disagrees does not make the earlier row final-ineffective. This arms the meta-heartbeat dead-man's switch (a missing quarterly SL1 evaluation alarms via W5 + the scheduled-query guard).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — candidates read / synthesized / qualified / rejected counts, roster active-count vs floor/ceiling, any `roster_below_floor` alert. If nothing changed: "SL1 evaluated, no roster change."
```

Every `PENDING_DRAFT` enqueue writes at minimum:

```
queue      = 'PENDING_DRAFT'                 -- NOT NULL, no default
item_key   = per item_type below             -- NOT NULL, no default; STABLE across cycles
item_type  = 'strategy-draft' | 'strategy-revise' | 'post-mortem'
status     = 'pending'                       -- NOT NULL, no default; SL2 writes 'complete' on drain
strategy   = the strategy or candidate code (A-E, or a candidate code)
due_date   = the NEXT calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today` (America/Denver)
```

- **`due_date` — the next Denver calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today`, never the next TRADING day and never a hand-computed date.** SL2 fires Sun-Thu and drains `due_date <= today`, so a next-calendar-day offset is always reachable on the following fire; a next-*trading*-day offset silently skips the item across a weekend, which is the 2026-08-16 drift. Per the preamble's timezone rule, `today` comes from `state.trading_day_today` — never the assistant-context `currentDate` (UTC-based; already rolled over during evening MT) and never local Bash `date`.
- **`item_key` — stable per item_type, and the cycle number NEVER belongs in the key** (it goes in `payload.cycle_number`, so a re-enqueue of the same work is recognisable as the same work):

     - **THE IDEMPOTENCY GUARD ABOVE MUST COVER THIS TABLE TOO — NOT-EXISTS on `(strategy_code, phase, incubation_day)` before each insert.** **AND THE SPELLING IS PINNED, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS ONE DOES NOT COMPILE (added 2026-09-23, SL3; reproduced against BigQuery, not inferred).** Both guards in this STEP — this one and the `events.shadow_positions` one above — are stated as prose ("NOT-EXISTS check on (…) before each insert") with no executable template anywhere, and the form a session naturally reaches for, `INSERT … SELECT <literals> WHERE NOT EXISTS (…)`, fails at analysis time: **`Query without FROM clause cannot have a WHERE clause`**. A `SELECT` of bare literals has no `FROM`, so it cannot carry the `WHERE` the guard lives in. **Write it with a `FROM UNNEST([…])` so the SELECT has a FROM clause** — `INSERT … SELECT <cols> FROM UNNEST([1]) WHERE NOT EXISTS (…)` — or read first and branch in the session; both compile. A systematic strategy re-firing on the same ticker across consecutive days is the NORMAL case, not an exotic one, so that collision is likely rather than remote. Direction (b) is a silent LOSS of live signal evidence, which is strictly worse than the duplication in (a) and is the same failure direction — a false negative on the candidate's own record — that the `incubation_day` pin above calls out as the one no other rail catches.

It is corrected here rather than left to the bullets below to override, on this block's own rule that a drifted pointer is worse than none: those bullets are marked as corrections OF this one, but this one was the only place the bound was ever stated as a plain imperative, and an imperative refuted 300 lines later is still the first thing a reader obeys.** The overlap that re-admits costs nothing and is already paid for: STEP 1's two idempotency guards key on `(strategy_code, phase, incubation_day)` and on `(strategy_code, event_type, ticker, DATE(event_ts))`, so a day already written is skipped row by row rather than re-inserted — precisely what those guards exist for, and the 2026-08-26 `event_ts` pin is what makes the second of them actually bind on a backfilled day rather than being vacuous.
