Measured against `state.decision_log_current` through this STEP's own tolerant filter, SL3's 52 `arsenal-heartbeat` rows carry **FOUR** different treatments of that one slot: **`no_transition` (6 rows, 2026-07-10..07-30), `EVALUATED_NO_CHANGE` (15, 2026-08-04..08-23), `HOLD` (1, 2026-08-24) and NULL (30, from 2026-07-11 and unbroken across the last sixteen fires since 2026-08-25)**. **Only `HOLD` is in the vocabulary, and it is the one used once.** The other fifteen slots of the same call show no such exposure, and that contrast is the diagnosis rather than a reassurance: `strategy`, `ticker`, `conviction`, `conviction_pct`, `sub_pattern` and `theater_check` are NULL on all 52 — perfectly consistent — while `fields`, `refs` and `tags` vary freely and are MEANT to. **`decision` is the only one of the sixteen slots where variation is forbidden, and it is the only one that varied.**
       - **WHY IT DRIFTED — AND IT IS *NOT* "THIS BLOCK GIVES NO `CALL` TEMPLATE", A HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND FALSIFIED THIS RUN.** The obvious reading is that the heartbeat instruction names the table and the `entry_type` and stops, while `ops.sp_log_decision` takes **sixteen** positional arguments (re-measured live against `ops.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARAMETERS`), leaving each session to fill the other fifteen from nothing. But eliding is the FLEET NORM rather than an SL3 omission: of the **88** `sp_log_decision(` call sites in this document, **86 write `(...)`** and exactly two spell an argument list out (M4's `premortem-indicator-walk`, D1's `add-candidate-review`), and the shared preamble gives no template either. A convention 86 sites follow cannot be what singles this one out. **The actual discriminator is WHICH FIELDS this block has ever named, and it maps onto the drift exactly.** Four sweeps hardened this one write — 2026-08-19 (`entry_type` plus the `title` prefix, not `tags`), 2026-08-20 (the two are a CONJUNCTION), 2026-09-07 (the `entry_type` is three-way shared), 2026-09-09 (the filter must tolerate `CORRECTED — ` and be read from the current view) — and all four are about `entry_type` and `title`, for one stated reason: W5's meta-heartbeat check READS those two. **Every field a consumer keys on is pinned to the character; every field no consumer reads was never mentioned once — and that is precisely the set that drifted.** So the rule is not "pin the call"; it is that **a write's UN-READ fields are exactly where drift is invisible, and an audit scoped to what a consumer reads can never find it.**
       - **THE PRECEDENT SITS IN THE SAME RULE LIST AND IT SAYS THIS IS LUCK, NOT SAFETY.** §Decision-log lifecycle pins the exit family at the single token `exit` after measuring **six spellings of one concept**, and says outright that the only reason that fragmentation stayed harmless is that "no live view or procedure filters on the exit family at all" — "That is luck, not design: the moment anyone writes an exit-side learning view, five of the six spellings silently vanish from it." The same sentence transfers here verbatim. Nothing filters on `decision` for `arsenal-heartbeat` today; the two mechanical backstops that rule list names do not reach it either, since the GO filters are a `^GO\b`-anchored family test that none of these four values would match and the `analytics.thesis_outcomes` tolerance is for the `thesis` `entry_type` synonym; and **no `scripts/check_*.py` validates the `decision` vocabulary at all** (repo-wide grep this run — the rule is prose-enforced only, as that same list already concedes when it says a NEW variant "is still invisible to both"). The exposure is a future arsenal-side learning view, and the failure it would produce — three of four cohorts silently dropped — is the `thesis` / `thesis-construction` incident the rule list opens with, which cost a real Strategy B GO its place in every calibration view and "was never noticed".
       - **THE FIX IS PROSE AND IT IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN: write `decision = NULL` on the `arsenal-heartbeat` row, deliberately, and it is stated at the instruction above so the next session does not have to choose.** NULL is not a dodge, and it is not merely what the last sixteen fires happened to do — it is the semantically correct value. **A heartbeat asserts that an EVALUATION OCCURRED, which is not a decision.** Every decision SL3 actually takes is a lifecycle transition and is recorded where transitions are recorded: `events.strategy_lifecycle` plus the `ops.roster_change_log` marker (STEPs 3 and 4), surfaced by its own `info` notice (`strategy_paper_promoted` / `strategy_incubation_culled`, pinned 2026-09-15). The heartbeat is never the venue for one — on a quiescent fire or a transitioning one — so no token belongs in the slot, and **specifically no mapping from "transitions fired" onto `GO`/`NO-GO` should be invented for it: coining a MAPPING is the same defect as coining a TOKEN, one level up.** The in-vocabulary candidate a later session will reach for is `NO-ACTION`, and it is wrong for the same reason — it would assert a decision to do nothing on a fire that may have just promoted a strategy.
       - **The 22 historical non-NULL rows are NOT retro-relabelled, and the rule forbidding it is explicit.** §Decision-log lifecycle: corrections are NEW rows carrying `superseded_by`, never `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, and "`entry_type` has no sanctioned UPDATE exception (only `sub_pattern` does, ops/RUNBOOK.md §21)" — which binds `decision` identically, since a `sp_log_decision` correction can only ever append. They stand as read-tolerated historical spellings, exactly as `position-close` does for the exit family, and any arsenal-side view built later must allowlist them rather than assume one. **Prose only — no SQL, no view, no threshold, no gate and no declaration is changed, and SL3 owns the surface edited, so no referral is owed for SL3's own leg.**
       - **THE SIBLING LEGS CARRY THE SAME DEFECT AND ARE NOT SL3'S TO FIX — recorded rather than carried silently.** The `entry_type` is three-way shared (pinned 2026-09-07), and across all 57 `arsenal-heartbeat` rows in the current view the non-SL3 ones add **`REJECT` (2, SL1) and `NO RETIREMENT PROPOSED` (1, SL4)** — both coined, and the second not even token-shaped. SL1's STEP 6 and SL4's STEP 4 are the write sites and each owns its own section, so this is raised as an `ops.alerts` `info` row (`heartbeat_decision_vocabulary_drift`) naming both, per the 2026-08-28 OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule and the return-path convention; the open-`info`-row de-dup check prescribed 2026-09-14 was run first and no open row covers it. **Do NOT "fix" SL1's or SL4's rows from an SL3 fire**, and do not add a `decision` allowlist to any `scripts/check_*.py` from one either — that is a CI change on landed, green history, the failure CLAUDE.md warns about by name.
       - **ONE METHOD NOTE, because it is the reason this was found on the very run that went looking somewhere else.** This fire ran the block-wide template census the 2026-09-15 finding prescribed — all sixteen executable templates in this block re-derived against live procedure signatures and `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`, fifteen clean, the sixteenth reproducing only the SHADOW `stuck_reason` hazard STEP 4 already pins. **That census could not have found this, by construction: it audits TEMPLATES, and the heartbeat is the one instruction in this STEP with no template to audit** — so the instrument returned "not a defect, simply underspecified", right about the specification and blind to the outcome. What found it was the complementary instrument: a census of the ROWS ACTUALLY WRITTEN — the same method this block already uses for `''` occurrences, for `writes:` cells and for `sp_raise_alert` argument lists, pointed for the first time at a write's own HISTORY instead of at its specification. **A template census tests what a call WOULD do; only the rows test what it DID. And the instruction that executes most often is the one least likely to carry a template, precisely because nothing ever broke.** **Extend the re-resolve once more: each fire, re-measure the referrals, the quotations, the executable templates — and, for every write this STEP performs on EVERY fire, the distinct values its own rows carry in any controlled-vocabulary column.**

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — SHADOW/PAPER members monitored, transitions fired (SHADOW→PAPER; PAPER→PROBE enqueued), culls. If nothing: "SL3 evaluated, no incubation transition."

## SL4. Discretionary Retirement Proposer — regular routine

Runs monthly (first trading day), after M4. The REMOVE-ONLY discretionary-retirement scanner, with a hard default-KEEP bias. It adds the missing discretionary-retirement path WITHOUT touching any mechanical kill trigger (drawdown / 30-trade gate / foundation-change / m2m stay exactly as-is in D1/D2/M4). It can only move in the fail-safe direction — retire an edge-decayed / redundant / dominated strategy — and can NEVER spare or continue a strategy a mechanical trigger flagged, so it does not reintroduce the context-aware KILL/SPARE judgment AI_Trading_Foundation.md:384 reserves.

```
Read access scope: Monthly cadence. Read `perf.strategy_daily`, `perf.kill_flags`, `analytics.strategy_vs_park`, `state.strategy_roster` (ADOPTED members), `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy`, `state.strategy_probe_progress`, `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`, `state.arsenal_rails`, `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`, `ops.arsenal_control`, `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` rows), `ops.alerts` (open `category='interim_underperf_warning'` rows). Stages no orders; edits no repo/roster.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section. Monitored via run-logging + `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`/`stalled_runs`.

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL4')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL4', ['M4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Aborts (RAISE) + `missing_dependency` critical if M4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current monthly period — M4 is `monthly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any M4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day. Self-bootstrapping.

STEP 1 — READ RETIREMENT CANDIDACY (objective; default-KEEP). For every ADOPTED strategy read `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy`, which fires ONLY on an objective sustained signal:
   - **edge-decay** — a foundation-citation-status change short of a mechanical foundation-change terminate, AND trailing-12-month deployed-TWR excess-vs-SGOV below a floor, sustained `>=2` quarters;
   - **redundancy** — rolling return-correlation with a peer above threshold where the peer strictly dominates on excess. ENCODED (2026-07-18 audit — `analytics.strategy_return_correlation` (`bigquery/83_correlation_controls.sql`) was built as this signal's substrate but never wired to a consumer; this is its sole read): `SELECT strategy_a, strategy_b, corr, overlap_days FROM analytics.strategy_return_correlation WHERE corr >= 0.7 AND overlap_days >= 40`. For each returned pair where BOTH codes are currently ADOPTED, the signal fires against the DOMINATED member only — the one whose latest `perf.kill_flags.excess_vs_sgov` is STRICTLY lower than its peer's; if either side's excess is NULL/unreadable or they are equal, fire nothing (default-KEEP on ambiguity). A fired redundancy signal counts toward STEP 2 eligibility exactly as `edge_decay_signal` does, PROVIDED `floor_ok AND arsenal_ok AND cooldown_clear` all read TRUE in `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (the rails stay binding), and the STEP 3 floor guard applies unchanged — cite the pair + corr + both excess values in `trigger_context`;
   - **dominated-by-newcomer** — a newer ADOPTED strategy covers the same regime cells with strictly better excess.
   No fired signal → no proposal (the default). QUALITATIVE-EVIDENCE INTAKE (consumption-closure audit 2026-07-16 — closes the Q1/Q3/A3 dead channel): additionally query `events.decision_log` for `entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` rows from the trailing 2 quarters and `ops.alerts` for open `category='interim_underperf_warning'` rows (D1's 90-day/−15% early signal). For an ADOPTED strategy with such signals from `>=2` rows carrying DISTINCT `source_session` values, or ONE signal PLUS an open interim_underperf_warning alert, treat candidacy as fired for STEP 2 EVEN IF `edge_decay_signal=FALSE`, PROVIDED `floor_ok AND arsenal_ok AND cooldown_clear` all read TRUE in `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (the rails stay binding; only the perf-threshold component is supplemented — the proposal still faces the default-KEEP adversarial review). **DISTINCT `source_session` is a mechanical, queryable bar, not "different quarters" (owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW hardening — closes a gap an adversarial review found: two rows dated into two different quarters by ONE Q1/Q3 catch-up session backfilling a multi-quarter window would otherwise satisfy an "or different quarters" reading of this test even though they reflect one session's judgment, not two independent corroborating cycles).** This is why Q1/Q3's WRITE-ONCE convention (their PART 2 sections above) requires `source_session` on every `strategy-retirement-signal` write to be the writing run's own `<session_id>` (the same literal value that run's Run-logging `sp_log_run`/`sp_routine_end` calls use) rather than a per-write "`Q1 <date>`"/"`Q3 <date>`"-style free-text label: every row a single catch-up session writes, however many quarters it covers, then shares exactly one `source_session` and counts as ONE source cycle here — only a genuinely separate future run (its own session) earns a second. Cite the decision_log `entry_id`s + alert `alert_id` in STEP 2's `trigger_context`. A single uncorroborated signal is only noted in the STEP 4 heartbeat.

STEP 1b — PROBE PROGRESS WATCH (loop-completeness audit 2026-07-16). Read `state.strategy_probe_progress` (`bigquery/73_probe_progress_watch.sql`). For any row with `stuck = TRUE` (>=400 days in PROBE, fully funded, ZERO closed trades and ZERO open positions, no RETIREMENT_PROPOSED within 90 days — a dead signal path, not a slow archetype): treat it exactly like a fired candidacy in STEP 2 — enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-retirement'` (`conservative_default='KEEP'`, trigger_context = strategy_code + ' probe_stuck: 400+ days funded with zero trades and zero open positions'), write the RETIREMENT_PROPOSED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row + the `ops.roster_change_log` proposal row (this row is also what arms the view's 90-day re-proposal cooldown), and respect the STEP 3 floor guard. An affirmative AR_orc RETIRE verdict routes through the existing D2 step-5 termination handler (closes out and redistributes the idle $2,000 probe stake); a KEEP verdict stamps the per-strategy `cooldown_until` exactly as STEP 2 does. Never a chat question.

STEP 2 — PROPOSE (affirmative-RETIRE-required). For each fired candidacy, enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-retirement'` (`conservative_default='KEEP'`, trigger_context = strategy_code + the fired signal) and write a RETIREMENT_PROPOSED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row AND an `ops.roster_change_log` row (`change_key='<code>:ADOPTED->RETIREMENT_PROPOSED:<YYYY-MM>'`, `strategy_code=<code>`, `from_state='ADOPTED'`, `to_state='RETIREMENT_PROPOSED'`) — this row is what `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy.cooldown_clear` (**live def `bigquery/81_arsenal_fixes.sql`** — corrected 2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing SL4's `stale_live_sql_pointer`; this pointer read "bigquery/39" until then, but `bigquery/39_beta_adjusted_alpha.sql`:139 carries its own SUPERSEDED-LIVE marker naming 81 as current, and SL4's 2026-09-01 run built a `refs` entry for a nonexistent `bigquery/39_retirement_candidacy.sql` straight off the stale text) reads; without it the 90-day post-KEEP re-proposal cooldown is unenforced. Only an affirmative AR_orc RETIRE verdict routes the strategy to the existing D2 step-5 termination handler; a KEEP verdict writes the ADOPTED lifecycle row + its roster_change_log marker (see AR_orc step 4); the proposal-time roster_change_log row above is what enforces the 90-day re-proposal cooldown.

STEP 3 — FLOOR GUARD. NEVER propose a retirement that would drop the active roster below `state.arsenal_rails.n_min` (=2) — skip, and if the floor binds leave SL1 to backfill a successor candidate.

STEP 4 — HEARTBEAT. Write the monthly `arsenal-heartbeat` `events.decision_log` entry (strategies evaluated, candidacies fired, proposals enqueued) + on any proposal `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','SL4','retirement_proposed', '<code> (<name>) proposed for RETIREMENT — <fired signal: edge decay / redundancy / dominated-by-newcomer / probe-stuck>. AR_orc adjudicates (conservative default KEEP); no action needed from you.', '<JSON per the preamble ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, with kill_trigger = the fired signal>')`. **`warning`, not `info`** (ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, preamble) — a pending drop is a roster-membership change the operator learns of by email, not by query. One notice per proposal, at proposal time; the eventual RETIRE or KEEP verdict surfaces separately (SL5 deregister, or AR_orc's decision-log entry).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — ADOPTED strategies evaluated, retirement proposals enqueued (with the fired signal), floor-guard skips. If nothing: "SL4 evaluated, no retirement proposed."
```

## SL5. Strategy Register & Roster Sync — regular routine

Queue-driven (fires Sun-Thu; no-ops unless a roster-mutation task is due). The D2a-pattern self-executing transition + fanout engine and the ONLY writer of roster MEMBERSHIP — a dedicated idempotent registrar. It fires on three inputs: a SUFFICIENT `strategy-adoption` verdict (→ SHADOW register), a PAPER→PROBE `probe-register` enqueue from SL3 (→ live registration), and a TERMINATED transition (→ deregister). Never asks a chat question, ever — it self-executes the repo edit / commit / push / live-view re-apply exactly as D2a's autonomous cutover does.

```
Read access scope: daily (queue-driven), full repo + SQL write access (the D2a self-execute model). Read `state.strategy_adoption_readiness`, `state.strategy_roster`, `strategy/roster.yaml`, `ops.roster_change_log`, `events.queue_events` / `state.open_queue_detail`, `events.strategy_lifecycle`, `ops.arsenal_control`, `ops.trading_control`, `analytics.theater_judge` (via `ops.sp_score_theater()`, ITEM 7).

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section. Queue-driven → monitored via `state.stalled_runs` + `ops/triggers.json` (NOT cadence/period watch).

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL5')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL5', ['AR_orc'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Self-bootstrapping. **`<today>` IS `state.trading_day_today.today` — the `America/Denver` OPERATING DATE, read off the connector pre-flight's own liveness query and reused verbatim; NEVER a bare `CURRENT_DATE()`, never the host UTC date, never `date` in the shell. This section's two `<today>` sites are this one and the `PENDING_ROSTER` scan below, and until 2026-09-27 NEITHER named a source (PINNED 2026-09-27, SL5 diligence sweep, MEASURED not reasoned; see the DATE-PLANE pin two paragraphs down).**

**WHAT THIS GATE DOES WHEN AR_orc HALTED — AND WHY SL5 NEEDS NO UPSTREAM-HALT LIMB OF ITS OWN (added 2026-09-21 by the first SL5 fire ever to fail this gate; MEASURED not reasoned).** The shared DEPENDENCY-WAIT WINDOW already dispositions this correctly for SL5, and the derivation is recorded here only so the next fire does not re-derive it under time pressure. On 2026-09-21 the fourth BigQuery OAuth expiry halted AR_att at connector pre-flight with **no `ops.run_log` row at all** (halt record `6b30626`), AR_orc then halted at its own gate (`5b5f4c5`), and this gate RAISEd for SL5 at 19:25 MT — raising `critical missing_dependency` `2fd2a966` before it RAISEd, as the shared bullet says it does. **The branch is "upstream terminal `'failed'`/`'halted'` today → REFIRE once if refireable; otherwise FUTILE — exhaust immediately", and AR_orc is `catchup_safe: false` in `ops/cadence.yaml` (verified by parse, not by memory — the REFIREABLE definition drops all five queue-driven routines automatically), so the correct outcome is FUTILE with zero polls waited, carrying `DEPWAIT[dep=AR_orc;polls=1;waited_s=0;outcome=futile;refired=none]`.** Do NOT sit out the 60-minute window, and do NOT halve-and-wait on the ≥45-min-past-slot branch: that branch is for the NO-upstream-row case and AR_orc's row is present. **The reason SL5 escapes the fleet-wide defect AR_orc filed the same evening** (`dependency_gate_misreads_upstream_halt_record`, info notice `d8da6e78`, owner W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE) **is structural and worth stating: that defect bites only when the upstream's halt is INVISIBLE to `ops.run_log` — a connector-outage halt that cannot write its own row — which is AR_att's case, not AR_orc's.** AR_orc's pre-flight PASSED and it logged `started` then `halted`, so SL5 reads a terminal row and lands squarely on an enumerated branch; neither the §38 git-evidence fallback (which would mint a phantom `completed` from a halt-record commit) nor the futile branch's blind spot is ever reached. SL5 inherits that exposure only if AR_orc is someday halted by an outage that also takes the run log — in which case the fix is the shared bullet's, still filed, and NOT a limb here. **Record the cycle HALTED, never as a no-op: "no roster mutations due" is a CONCLUSION this gate forbids reaching**, and the three inputs being empty is not a licence to report the quiet outcome — the same discipline AR_orc applied when it recorded its 2026-09-21 drain HALTED rather than empty.

**DATE-PLANE PIN FOR THIS SECTION'S TWO `<today>` SITES — THE DEPENDENCY GATE ABOVE AND THE `PENDING_ROSTER` SCAN BELOW (PINNED 2026-09-27, SL5 diligence sweep, MEASURED not reasoned; the FOURTH instance of a defect class AR_orc closed in its own section the same evening, and one its own narrowed list omitted).** Measured at `3078d5a` over this section: `<today>` occurs exactly **twice**, and `state.trading_day_today`, `CURRENT_DATE` and `DATE ANCHOR` occur **zero times each** — so both executing sites named a date with no stated source. **The rule that should have supplied it is enumerated, not fleet-wide, and SL5 is not in the enumeration.** The shared preamble's Time zone / "today" bullet governs exactly this case in these words — "Whenever a routine needs 'today' to create/delete/filter a dated calendar event **or a queue `due_date`**, use `state.trading_day_today.today`" — and closes "Binds D2, D2a, D3, W4, M4, Q4, A1, A3". SL5's dispatch scan IS literally a queue `due_date` filter and SL5 is absent from that list. The bullet also names only two forbidden sources, the assistant-context `currentDate` and shell `date`, and **does not name BigQuery's own `CURRENT_DATE()`** — which is the third and the natural one, because this predicate is written as SQL. Verified live this fire: `state.trading_day_today.today` = 2026-09-27 while the host UTC clock read 2026-09-28, and SL5's slot is `25 1 * * 1,2,3,4,5` = 19:25 MT, so the UTC date is ahead by one on every on-time fire rather than on a boundary case. **THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS PIN PUT THE GATE'S DIVERGENCE AT 17 OF 62 FIRES (27.4%), IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THAT IS WRONG BY A FACTOR OF FOUR — IT MODELLED A NAIVE `EXISTS`, NOT `sp_assert_deps`'s ACTUAL PREDICATE (self-caught 2026-09-27 by reading `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` instead of the neighbouring prose about it).** AR_orc is `queue_driven`, so its `period_start` is NULL and the gate takes the strict daily branch: satisfied iff a `completed` upstream row carries `run_date = in_run_date`, **OR** `run_date = in_run_date - 1` while the Denver clock is still before noon of `in_run_date`. That grace clause is INERT under the correct anchor — 19:25 MT is not before noon of the same day — but under a UTC anchor `in_run_date` is already tomorrow, so "noon of `in_run_date`" is noon TOMORROW, the clock test is trivially TRUE, and the grace branch accepts the upstream's completion for the true Denver date. **So the midnight-crossing grace, built for an unrelated purpose, silently rescues a mis-anchored `<today>` at every evening-MT slot, and the UTC-anchored satisfied-set is a strict SUPERSET of the Denver-anchored one.** Re-measured under the real predicate over all **62** SL5 `started` rows ever: the two anchors disagree on **4 of 62 = 6.5%**, **all four fail-OPEN and ZERO fail-closed** — run_dates **2026-07-10, 2026-07-13, 2026-07-16 and 2026-09-21**. **LEGACY ROWS RAISED BEFORE THIS CONTRACT — HEAL THEM, DO NOT STRAND THEM (added 2026-08-20).** A row whose payload is missing `pinned_columns`, or missing the refs entirely, is NOT evidence that the contract is still unpinned — it is evidence that the RAISER predates this paragraph. Treat the payload as best-effort and fall back, in order: (a) any key the payload does carry; (b) the refs and column list named in the row's own `message` text, which every raise to date has stated in prose even when the payload did not; (c) the `git log` for the commit the message cites. Then apply the SAME evidence test — read both sides in the repo and confirm they agree — and resolve or leave open on THAT evidence. **Never leave a row open merely because a payload key is absent**, and never resolve it merely because the key is absent either: an unparseable payload is a reason to read the message, not a reason to skip the row. If after all three fallbacks the handoff genuinely cannot be identified, resolve it with `resolved_note='unidentifiable payload and message; superseded by the 2026-08-20 raise contract'` and re-raise a correctly-shaped row for any contract still believed unpinned — an unreadable row that no future cycle can ever evaluate is the accumulation this non-latching class is most vulnerable to, and re-raising costs one email. **Agree** → `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='<both refs re-read at <git sha>; every pinned column agrees — <one-line verdict>>' WHERE alert_id='<id>'` — scoped by `alert_id`, one row at a time, the sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve (ITEM 17 precedent; same discipline as D3's `queue_item_stale` and `queue_venue_claim_unwired` HEAL-RESOLUTIONs). **Disagree** → the contract is genuinely still unpinned: leave the row OPEN and pin the missing side in `Claude_Task_Plan.md` this cycle, then resolve on the next fire against the landed commit. **NEVER resolve on age** — this class is silent by construction (both routines log `completed` either way), so an aged-out row is indistinguishable from a fixed one: the aging-alert trap `phantom_run_completion` documents. **NEVER resolve a row for a different handoff** — the evidence is per-handoff, the same discipline `queue_venue_claim_unwired` keeps per `(item_key, finding_class)`. Scoped to `source='SL5'` deliberately: this is the raising routine's own debt, and any FUTURE routine that raises this category owes itself the same step rather than inheriting SL5's. Best-effort — a failure here can never abort the run, and it never gates the roster work below.

   ```

          l.from_state IS NULL AS from_state_missing,   -- fail-closed guard, see below
